idaṃ | agne | sudhitaṃ | duḥdhitāt | adhi | priyāt | ūṃ iti | cit | manmanaḥ | preyaḥ | astu | te | yat | te | śukraṃ | tanvaḥ | rocate | śuci | tena | asmabhyaṃ | vanase | ratnaṃ | ā | tryaṃ ‖ 11 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे अग्ने इदमस्मदीयं सोमादिरूपं हविः । कीदृशं तत् । दुर्धिताद्दुष्टं स्थापितात्मठिनात्काष्ठादेरध्युपरि सुधितं सुहितं सुष्टु दत्तं । मन्मनो मननीयात्पियादु चित् तव हृद्यादपि । उशब्दोऽवधारणे जिच्छभोऽपिशब्दार्थः । ते तव प्रेयोऽतिप्रियतममस्तु । तत्किमित्याह । हे अग्ने ते तव तन्नः शरीरस्य धृतेनोज्वलिताया ज्वालायाः शुचि निर्मलं शुक्रं दीप्तं यत्तेजो रोचते तेन सह रत्नं रमणीयं मणिमुक्तादिकं वितरन्नस्मभ्यं वनसे । अस्मान्संभजस्व ॥ वनतेर्व्यत्ययेनात्मनेदं ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, this our oblation, in the form of soma and the like. What kind is it? It is well placed (सुधितं (sudhitaṃ)), well set, well given, upon the ill-placed (दुर्धितात् (durdhitāt)), that is, the hard fuel-stick or the like that has been laid down. It is fit to be reflected on (मन्मनः (manmanaḥ)), so even more than what is dear (प्रियादु चित् (priyādu cit)), more than what is pleasing to your heart. The word उ (u) is for emphasis, and चित् (cit) has the sense of "even". May it be most dear to you. What follows from that? O Agni, the pure, bright radiance (tejas) that shines from your body, from the flame kindled by ghee: along with it, bestowing on us delightful wealth such as gems and pearls, favour us (वनसे (vanase)), that is, take us to yourself. The verb vanati is here used in the ātmanepada by vyatyaya.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • अग्ने (agne)—O Agni
  • दुर्धितात् अधि (durdhitāt adhi)—upon the hard fuel-sticks and the like
  • सुधितं (sudhitaṃ)—carefully offered
  • इदं (idaṃ)—this oblation, in the form of soma and the like
  • मन्मनः (manmanaḥ)—that which is worthy of praise
  • प्रियादु चित् (priyādu cit)—than all things that are beneficial
  • ते (te)—to you
  • प्रेयः (preyaḥ)—as most dear
  • अस्तु (astu)—let it be
  • ते (te)—your
  • तन्नः (tannaḥ)—of the body in the form of a flame kindled by ghee
  • शुचि (śuci)—pure
  • शुक्रं (śukraṃ)—shining
  • यत् (yat)—which radiance
  • रोचते (rocate)—shines (blazes)
  • तेन (tena)—with this
  • त्वं (tvaṃ)—you
  • रत्नं (ratnaṃ)—delightful wealth
  • अस्मभ्यं (asmabhyaṃ)—to us
  • आ वनसे (ā vanase)—fill up and give
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, may this oblation in the form of soma and the like, carefully offered upon the hard fuel-sticks and the like, be dearer to you than all your other things that are worthy of praise and beneficial. Come with that pure and shining radiance of your flame-form body, kindled by ghee, and fill up for us delightful wealth.

Printed English

May this oblation, Agni, carefully placed upon the rugged but agreeable (pile of fuel), be most acceptable to you, so that the pure radiance of your person may shine brightly, and you may grant us wealth.

p. 144

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

दुर्धितात् अधि सुधितं (durdhitāt adhi sudhitaṃ): Although the fuel-sticks and the like are hard, Agni is here prayed that the offerings such as oblations may be soft and agreeable.

मन्मनः (manmanaḥ): The word मन्म (manma) has been explained as "to be reflected on, worthy of meditation". The word is also used in the senses "praiseworthy" and "venerable". In many ṛks such as 1-26-2, 1-127-2 and 1-151-8, the words मन्मना (manmanā) and मन्मभिः (manmabhiḥ) mean an excellent and praiseworthy movement of the mind. The Nirukta-author quotes three ṛks in which the word मन्म (manma) occurs. First,

उप प्रागात्सुमन्मेऽधायि मन्म देवानामाशा उप वीतपृष्ठः । अन्वेनं विप्रा ऋषयो मदंति देवानां पुष्टे चकृमा सुबंधुं ॥ (upa prāgātsumanme 'dhāyi manma devānāmāśā upa vītapṛṣṭhaḥ | anvenaṃ viprā ṛṣayo madaṃti devānāṃ puṣṭe cakṛmā subaṃdhuṃ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-162-7)

In this ṛk the Nirukta-author explains the word मन्म (manma) as "mantra" (Ni. 6-22): a mantra that is to be reflected on, that is, worthy of meditation. Sāyaṇa explains it as "the fruit that is to be thought of". Second,

तनूनपात्पथ ऋतस्य यानान्मध्वा समंजन्त्सृदया सुजिह्व । मन्मानि धीभिरुत यज्ञमृंधन् देवत्रा च कृणुह्यध्वरं नः ॥ (tanūnapātpatha ṛtasya yānānmadhvā samaṃjantsṛdayā sujihva | manmāni dhībhiruta yajñamṛṃdhan devatrā ca kṛṇuhyadhvaraṃ naḥ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-2)

Here he has explained it as अस्मदभिप्रेतानि स्क्रोत्राणि (asmadabhipretāni skrotrāṇi). In the same way he quotes ṛk 1-129-9 (Ni. 10-42) and shows that there too the same meaning holds. In the present ṛk the meaning is "worthy of praise".

ते तन्वः शुचि शुक्रं (te tanvaḥ śuci śukraṃ): The radiance, pure and shining, of the flame-form body kindled by ghee. Thus the special quality of Agni's radiance after the sacrificial offering is described.

अग्निश्शुचि व्रततमश्शुचिर्विप्रः शुचिः कविः । शुची रोचत आहुतः । उदग्ने शुचयस्तव शुक्रा भ्राजंत ईरते । तव ज्योतीग्‌ष्यर्चयः ॥ (agniśśuci vratatamaśśucirvipraḥ śuciḥ kaviḥ | śucī rocata āhutaḥ | udagne śucayastava śukrā bhrājaṃta īrate | tava jyotīgṣyarcayaḥ ‖) (Kṛ. Saṃ. 1-3-14)NOTE

As this is described in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā, Agni's white radiance is described.

रत्नं (ratnaṃ): The word रत्न (ratna) is listed among the names for wealth (Ni. 3-9). It means delightful wealth.

p. 145

Grammar
  • सुधितम्—डुधाञ् धारणपोषणयोः इति धातुः । कर्मणि क्तप्रत्ययः । दधातेर्हिः इति हि-आदेशः । व्यत्ययेन धत्वम् । गतिरनंतरः (पा. सू. ६-२-४९) इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरः भवति । एवं दुर्धितात् इत्यत्रापि स्वरादयः भवंति ।
  • मन्मनः—मन ज्ञाने इति धातुः । अन्वेभ्योपि दृश्यते (पा. सू. ३-२-७५) इति मनिन् प्रत्ययः । इत्यादिर्नित्यम् इति आद्युदात्तस्वरः भवति । पंचमी-एकवचनांतरूपम् ।
  • प्रेयः—अतिशयार्थे ईयसुन् प्रत्ययः । प्रियस्थिरस्फिर (पा. सू. ६-४-१५७) इति प्रियशब्दस्य प्रादेशः । गुणः । ईयसुन् प्रत्ययस्य नित्त्वात् आद्युदात्तस्वरः भवति ।
  • अस्तु—आस भुवि धातुः । अदादि लोट् प्रथमपुरुष एकवचनांतरूपम् । तिजंतनिघातस्वरः भवति ।
  • तन्वः—तनु शब्दः । षष्ठी एकवचने परे तन्वादीनां छंदस्युपसंख्यानम् इति वचनेन यणादेशः । उदात्तस्थाने यण् आगतत्वात् उदात्तस्वरितयोर्यणः (पा. सू. ८-२-४) इति परस्य स्वरितस्वरः भवति ।
  • रोचते—रुच दीप्तौ धातुः लट् । प्रथमपुरुषएकवचनांतरूपम् । यत्संबंधत्वात् यद्वृत्तान्नित्यम् (पा. सू. ८-१-६६) इति निघातस्वरप्रतिषेधः भवति । तास्यनुदात्तेत् (पा. सू. ६-१-१८६) इति लसार्वधातुकस्य अनुदात्तत्वात् धातुस्वरः अवशिष्यते ।
  • वनसे—वन षण संभक्तौ धातुः । व्यत्ययो बहुलम् (पा. सू. ३-१-८५) इति आत्मनेपदी भवति । लेट् । मध्यमपुरुषएकवचनांतरूपम् । अतिजंतस्य परत्वात् निघातस्वरः भवति ।
  • रत्नम्—रमयतीति रत्नम् । रमु क्रीडायां धातुः । रमेस्तच (उ. सू. ३-२९४) इति नप्रत्ययः । तत्सन्नियोगेन मकारस्य तकारादेशः । नित् इति अनुवृत्तत्वात् आद्युदात्तस्वरः भवति ।NOTE

p. 146

Ṛk 12

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

रथा॑य॒ नाव॑मु॒त नो॑ गृ॒हाय॒ नित्या॑रित्रां प॒द्वतीं॑ रास्यग्ने ।
अ॒स्माकं॑ वी॒रा उ॒त नो॑ म॒घोनो॒ जनां॑श्च॒ या पा॒रया॒च्छर्म॒ या च॑ ॥ १२ ॥

rathāya nāvamuta no gṛhāya nityāritrāṃ padvatīṃ rāsyagne | asmākaṃ vīrā uta no maghono janāṃśca yā pārayāccharma yā ca ‖ 12 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

रथाय । नावं । उत । नः । गृहाय । नित्य अरित्रां । पत्वतीं । रासि । अग्ने ।
अस्माकं । वीरान् । उत । नः । मघोनः । जनान् । च । या । पारयात् । शर्म ।
या । च ॥ १२ ॥

rathāya | nāvaṃ | uta | naḥ | gṛhāya | nitya aritrāṃ | patvatīṃ | rāsi | agne | asmākaṃ | vīrān | uta | naḥ | maghonaḥ | janān | ca | yā | pārayāt | śarma | yā | ca ‖ 12 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे अग्ने उतापि च रथाय रंहणाय गृहाय सर्वस्यायतनभूताय नोऽस्माकं यजमानाय नावं संसारोत्तारिकां सोमयागात्मिकां नावं । यज्ञो वै सुतर्मा नौरित्यादिषु श्रुतिषु नौरूपत्वेन स्तुतत्वात् । कीदृशीं तां । नित्यारित्रां नियतर्त्वग्रूपोदाकर्षणकाष्ठसाधनोपेतां पद्वतीं ॥ ह्रस्वनुड्भामिति मतुप उदात्तत्वं ॥ द्रव्य देवतामंत्रादिरूपपादोपेतां । ईदृशीं यज्ञात्मिकां नावं रासि । देहि । संपादय । रातिर्दानकर्मा दासति रातीति तन्नामसु पाठात् । सैव विशेष्यते । उतापि च या नौरस्माकं वीरानस्मत्संबंधिनः पुत्रादीन्मघोनो हविर्लक्षणान्नवतः करोति । जनांश्च यजमानानस्थानपि या नौः पारयात् पारयेत् उत्तरयेत् ॥ पारयतेर्लेट्याडागमः । जननमरणादिबहुदुःखात्मकस्य पारं निरतिशयसुखास्पदं ब्रह्मलोकं प्रापयेत् । एष वः पुण्यः सुकृतो ब्रह्मलोक इति यागाद्यनुष्ठानवतां श्रूयमाणत्वात् । एवं प्रापय्य च या नौः शर्म सुखं निरतिशयं ब्रह्म प्रापयेत् परस्यांते कृतात्मानः प्रविशंति परं पदमित्युक्तत्वात् । चित्तशुद्धुत्पादनद्वारा विविदिषंति यज्ञेन दानेनेति श्रुतेः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, and for our sacrificer, who is "ratha" (that is, रंहणाय (raṃhaṇāya), one who speeds) and "gṛha" (the abode of all), give the boat (नावं (nāvaṃ)) that carries across saṃsāra, a boat in the form of the Soma sacrifice. The sacrifice is praised as a boat in śrutis such as यज्ञो वै सुतर्मा नौरित्यादिषु श्रुतिषु (yajño vai sutarmā naurityādiṣu śrutiṣu). What kind is it? नित्यारित्रां (nityāritrāṃ): furnished with the means of fixed oars (poles for pulling), in the form of the ṛtvijs. पद्वतीं (padvatīṃ): furnished with feet in the form of the materials, deities, mantras and so on (the affix मतुप (matupa) here has its accent through ह्रस्वनुड्भामिति (hrasvanuḍbhāmiti)). Give (रासि (rāsi)), supply, such a boat in the form of the sacrifice; राति (rāti) is a verb of giving, since दासति रातीति (dāsati rātīti) stands in its list of names.

The same boat is further qualified: it makes our heroes, our sons and others, wealthy (मघोनः (maghonaḥ)), that is, possessed of oblations; and it would carry across (पारयात् (pārayāt)) the sacrificers who are our people, bring them over, take them to the far shore of the many sufferings of birth, death and the like, to Brahmaloka, the seat of unsurpassed happiness; for it is heard of those who perform sacrifices and the like, एष वः पुण्यः सुकृतो ब्रह्मलोक इति (eṣa vaḥ puṇyaḥ sukṛto brahmaloka iti). Having carried them across thus, the boat would bring them शर्म (śarma), happiness, unsurpassed Brahma, as it is said parasyāṃte kṛtātmānaḥ praviśaṃti paraṃ padam, and by way of producing purity of mind, according to the śruti विविदिषंति यज्ञेन दानेन (vividiṣaṃti yajñena dānena).

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • अग्ने (agne)—O Agni
  • नित्यारित्रां (nityāritrāṃ)—having permanent oars in the form of the ṛtvijs
  • पद्वतीं (padvatīṃ)—furnished with feet in the form of materials, deities, mantras and so on
  • उत (uta)—and
  • या (yā)—which
  • अस्माकं (asmākaṃ)—our
  • वीरान् (vīrān)—heroic sons
  • मघोनः (maghonaḥ)—(which makes) wealthy

p. 147

  • उत (uta)—and
  • नः (naḥ)—our
  • जनांश्च (janāṃśca)—and the sacrificers
  • पारयात् (pārayāt)—(which) carries across (saṃsāra)
  • च (ca)—and
  • या (yā)—which
  • शर्म (śarma)—(which has) happiness (of the excellent Brahmaloka) (brought about) such a one
  • नावं (nāvaṃ)—the boat (in the form of the Soma sacrifice)
  • रथाय (rathāya)—to him who is dear
  • गृहाय (gṛhāya)—who is a place of refuge like a house
  • नः (naḥ)—to our sacrificer
  • रासि (rāsi)—supplyNOTE
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, supply to our sacrificer, who is dear to us and a place of refuge like a house, the boat in the form of the Soma sacrifice. It has permanent oars in the form of the ṛtvijs, and feet in the form of materials, deities, mantras and so on. It makes our heroic sons wealthy, carries (the sacrificers who perform the sacrifice, or our sacrificers) across saṃsāra, and brings them the happiness of the eternal Brahmaloka.

Printed English

Bestow, Agni, upon our excellent patron a boat ever fitted with oars and feet, ( one that may render ) our posterity prosperous, and may bear mankind across (the ocean of life) to felicity.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this ṛk the (Soma) sacrifice is compared to a boat, saṃsāra to the ocean, and the ṛtvijs to the oars. Poverty, fear of enemies and other kinds of sorrow are the terrible circumstances of the ocean of saṃsāra. Although the boat is the chief means of crossing this ocean, the boat cannot carry the sacrificer safely across without the boat itself and its oars. Therefore the prayer is that the boat in the form of the Soma sacrifice, propelled by the oars in the form of excellent ṛtvijs, may carry us safely across saṃsāra.

In the Ṛk-saṃhitā generally, it is a most fitting simile to compare sorrow such as poverty, the sin that is its cause, and the enemy to a deep flood of water, and the help of the gods to a boat. For example,

जातवेदसे सुननाम सोममरातीयतो नि दहाति वेदः । स नः पर्षदति दुर्गाणि विश्वा नावेव सिंधुं मरितात्यग्निः ॥ (jātavedase sunanāma somamarātīyato ni dahāti vedaḥ | sa naḥ parṣadati durgāṇi viśvā nāveva siṃdhuṃ maritātyagniḥ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-99-1)

p. 148

नू न इंद्रावरुणा गृणाना पृंक्तं रयिं सौश्रवसाय देवा । इत्था गृणंतो महिनस्य शर्धोऽपो न नावा दुरिता तरेम ॥ (nū na iṃdrāvaruṇā gṛṇānā pṛṃktaṃ rayiṃ sauśravasāya devā | itthā gṛṇaṃto mahinasya śardho 'po na nāvā duritā tarema ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-8-8)

In ṛks such as these, just as a river (sindhu) is crossed easily by a boat, there is a prayer that sin may be crossed with the help of deities such as Agni. In the same way Agni is here prayed to supply the boat in the form of the sacrifice.

Here it is said that the service of the boat in the form of the Soma sacrifice is threefold: first, making the sacrificers and their sons wealthy; second, carrying the sacrificers across saṃsāra; third, giving the happiness of the excellent Brahmaloka. Sāyaṇa has given his explanation for the sentence अस्माकं वीरान् मघोनः (asmākaṃ vīrān maghonaḥ); उत नः जनांश्च पारयात् (uta naḥ janāṃśca pārayāt); च या शर्म नावं (ca yā śarma nāvaṃ) accordingly. Not only in the Ṛk-saṃhitā but in the Śatapatha and other Brāhmaṇas too the same simile is well known. For example,

नौर्ह ना एषा स्वर्ग्या । यद्बहिष्पवमानं तस्या ऋत्विज एव स्फाश्चारित्राश्च स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य संपारणास्तस्या एक एव मज्जयिता य एव निंद्यः स यथा पूर्णामभ्यारुह्य मज्जयेदेवं हैनां समज्जयति तद्वै सर्व एव यज्ञो नौः स्वर्ग्या तस्मादु सर्वस्मादेव यज्ञान्निंद्यं परिबिबाधिषेत । (naurha nā eṣā svargyā | yadbahiṣpavamānaṃ tasyā ṛtvija eva sphāścāritrāśca svargasya lokasya saṃpāraṇāstasyā eka eva majjayitā ya eva niṃdyaḥ sa yathā pūrṇāmabhyāruhya majjayedevaṃ haināṃ samajjayati tadvai sarva eva yajño nauḥ svargyā tasmādu sarvasmādeva yajñānniṃdyaṃ paribibādhiṣeta |) (Śa. Brā. 4-2-5-10)

The Soma sacrifice, and the Bahiṣpavamāna hymn to be recited on the opening day of the Soma sacrifice, are boats that take one to heaven. The ṛtvijs themselves are their oars. If even one among these ṛtvijs has a blameworthy conduct, he makes these boats sink. Therefore such a one must be kept away from the sacrificial act, as the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa says; and likewise,

यज्यो वै सुशर्मा नः (yajyo vai suśarmā naḥ) (Ai. Brā. 1-13) ) नाममिवारुहेमेति समेवैनमेतदधिरोहति स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य समष्टैः संपत्तैः संगत्यैः ॥ () nāmamivāruhemeti samevainametadadhirohati svargasya lokasya samaṣṭaiḥ saṃpattaiḥ saṃgatyaiḥ ‖) (Ai. Brā. 4-20)

In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa too this kind of simile is well known.NOTE

And since the fruit of this sacrifice is the highest, even the gods desire it and are devoted to the sacrifice. Therefore men too, following them, should be devoted to the sacrificial work. Instructing thus,

p. 149

त आसत । श्रियं गच्छेम । यशः स्यामान्नादाः स्यामेति तथो एवेमे सत्त्रमासते श्रियं गच्छेम यशः स्यामान्नादाः स्यामेति । ते होचुः यो नः श्रमेण तपसा श्रद्धया यज्ञेनाहुतिभिर्यज्ञस्योदृचं पूर्वोवगच्छात्स नः श्रेष्ठोऽसत्तदु नः सर्वेषां सहेति तथेति । तद्विष्णुः प्रथमः प्राप । स देवानां श्रेष्ठोऽभवत्तस्मादाहुर्निष्णुर्देवानां श्रेष्ठ इति । (ta āsata | śriyaṃ gacchema | yaśaḥ syāmānnādāḥ syāmeti tatho eveme sattramāsate śriyaṃ gacchema yaśaḥ syāmānnādāḥ syāmeti | te hocuḥ yo naḥ śrameṇa tapasā śraddhayā yajñenāhutibhiryajñasyodṛcaṃ pūrvovagacchātsa naḥ śreṣṭho 'sattadu naḥ sarveṣāṃ saheti tatheti | tadviṣṇuḥ prathamaḥ prāpa | sa devānāṃ śreṣṭho 'bhavattasmādāhurniṣṇurdevānāṃ śreṣṭha iti |) (Śa. Brā. 14-1-1-2-3)

Since performing the sacrifice brings dignity, greatness and wealth of food, the gods desired these and became devoted to the sacrifice. Among them Viṣṇu obtained the first place, so Viṣṇu became the best of all the gods: thus the fruit of the sacrifice is praised. Similarly,

तस्मादाहुः पुण्यलोक ईजान इति (tasmādāhuḥ puṇyaloka ījāna iti) (Ta. Cā. 3-6-2-15)NOTE

What is said here, that the sacrifice is a means to a meritorious world, is indicated in the present ṛk by the word शर्म (śarma). Explaining the word शर्म (śarma) as सुखं निरतिशयं ब्रह्म प्रापयेत् (sukhaṃ niratiśayaṃ brahma prāpayet), the happiness of the unsurpassed Brahmaloka, Sāyaṇa quotes the sentence of the Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad विविदिषंति यज्ञेन दानेन (vividiṣaṃti yajñena dānena) (Bṛ. U. 4-4-22) and states the meaning of the word शर्म (śarma). Agni is prayed to supply to the sacrificer such a boat, giver of an excellent fruit and in the form of the Soma sacrifice.

रथाय (rathāya): रंहणाय यजमानाय (raṃhaṇāya yajamānāya); thus it is shown that this word is an adjective of the sacrificer. For the word रथ (ratha) the Nirukta-author says

रथो रंहतेर्गतिकर्मणः । स्थिरतेर्वा स्याद्विपरीतस्य। रममाणोऽस्मिंस्तिष्ठतीति ना, रपतेर्वा, रसतेर्वा । (ratho raṃhatergatikarmaṇaḥ | sthiratervā syādviparītasya| ramamāṇo 'smiṃstiṣṭhatīti nā, rapatervā, rasatervā |) (Ni. 9-11)

that is, it is formed either from the root रंह् (raṃh), meaning motion or speed; or, by a transposition of letters, from स्थिर (sthira) (firm); or from the root रम् (ram), meaning "sit in it and rejoice"; or from the root रप् (rap) or रस् (ras), meaning "make a sound". Quoting the ṛk वनस्पते वीड्वंगो (vanaspate vīḍvaṃgo) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-47-26) the Nirukta-author shows the derivation of the word रथ (ratha). But in the present ṛk, for it to be an adjective of the sacrificer, one of these meanings must be shown. The sacrificer is eager and active in performing the sacrifice; he is firm of mind, being consecrated (dīkṣita); he produces the sound of praise. Since for this very reason he has the epithet रास्सिनस्य (rāssinasya) (1-122-4), the adjective रथाय (rathāya) may apply to the sacrificer in any of the meanings stated above by the Nirukta-author.

p. 150

Both adjectives, रथाय (rathāya) and गृहाय (gṛhāya), indicate the greatness of the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice, and his divine position, which brings well-being to the whole world. Because the sacrifice itself is the cause of the origin and continuance of the world, and the sacrificer is the cause of such a sacrifice, the identity of the two is stated in many places. For this very reason identity is also stated between the sacrificer and Prajāpati. The supernatural power of the sacrificer is explained in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā as follows, and the point that he becomes the obtainer of a dwelling in heaven, the support of excess of happiness, is stated thus:

नाकसद्धिर्वै देवास्सुवर्गं लोकमायस्तन्नाकसदां नाकसत्त्वं यन्नाकसद उपदधाति नाकसद्धिरेव तद्यजमानस्सुवर्गं लोकमेति सुवर्गो वै लोको नाको यस्यैता उपधीयंते नास्मा अकं भवति यजमानायुतनं वै नाकसदो यन्नाकसद उपदधात्यायतनमेव तद्यजमानः कुरुते पृष्ठानां वा एतत्तेजः संभृतं यन्नाकसदो यन्नाकसदः । (nākasaddhirvai devāssuvargaṃ lokamāyastannākasadāṃ nākasattvaṃ yannākasada upadadhāti nākasaddhireva tadyajamānassuvargaṃ lokameti suvargo vai loko nāko yasyaitā upadhīyaṃte nāsmā akaṃ bhavati yajamānāyutanaṃ vai nākasado yannākasada upadadhātyāyatanameva tadyajamānaḥ kurute pṛṣṭhānāṃ vā etattejaḥ saṃbhṛtaṃ yannākasado yannākasadaḥ |) (Tai. Saṃ. 5-3-7-4)

In sentences like these the nature of the sacrificer's house and its special quality are described, and so is the excellent dwelling-place of which the sacrificer, skilled in building the altar and in the piling of the fire (agnicayana), becomes the cause. Gathering that very point together, the present ṛk conveys it by the adjective गृहाय (gṛhāya). Here the word गृह (gṛha) may mean either an earthly house endowed with every kind of wealth, or a dwelling in heaven endowed with excess of well-being.

Grammar
  • नावम्—णुद प्रेरणे धातुः । ग्लानुदिभ्यां डौः (उ. सू. २-२२२) इति डौ प्रत्ययः । डित्वसामर्थ्यात् धातोः टेः लोपः । औकारांतरब्धः भवति । प्रत्ययस्वरः भवति । द्वितीया अम् परे आवादेशः ।NOTE
  • गृहाय—ग्रह उपादाने धातुः । लोट् मध्यमपुरुष एकवचने हि आवेदः । छंदसि शायजपि (पा. सू. ३-१-८४) इति श्नाविकरणस्य शायचादेशः । अतो हेः इति हेः लुक् । व्यत्ययेन भत्वं न भवति ।NOTE
  • नित्यारित्राम्—नित्यं नियतं अरित्रं यस्याः सा । बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या पूर्वपदम् इति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः भवति ।

p. 151

Grammar
  • पद्वतीम् — पत् पादः अस्याः अस्ति इति पद्वत् । स्त्रीत्वे उगितश्च (पा. सू. ४-१-६) इति जीप् । ह्रस्वनुड्भ्यां मतुस् (पा.सू. ६-१-१७६) इति मतुस उदात्तस्वरः भवति । द्वितीयाविकवचनांतरूपम् ।
  • रासि — रा आदाने इति धातुः । लेट् मध्यमपुरुष एकवचनांतरूपम् । अतिजंतस्य परत्वात् निघातस्वरः भवति । राधातुः अत्र दानार्थे पठितः । दासति राशि (नि. ३-२००४) इति दानकर्मार्थेषु पठितः । NOTE
  • वीरान् — अज गतिक्षेपणयोः इति धातुः । स्थायितञ्चि—(उ. सू. २-१७०) इति रक् प्रत्ययः । धातोः वीभावः । प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तः भवति । द्वितीयाबहुवचनांतरूपम् ।
  • मघोनः — मघ अस्य अस्ति इति मघवा । छंदसी वनिपौ इति मत्वर्थे वनिप् प्रत्ययः । द्वितीयाबहुवचने परे श्वयुवमघोनामतद्दिते ( पा. सू. ६-४-१३३) इति वकारस्य संप्रसारणम् । पूर्वरूपम् । गुणः । एकादेशउदात्तेनोदात्तः (पा. सू. ८-२-५) इति ओकार उदात्तः भवति ।
  • पारयात् — पार तीर समाप्ति इति धातुः । लेट् प्रथमपुरुष एकवचने तिप् प्रत्ययः । सत्यापपाश—(पा. सू. ३-१-२५) इति स्वार्थे णिच् । इतश्चलोपः पर—(पा. सू. ३-४-९८) इति प्रत्ययस्य इकारस्य लोपः । लेटोऽडाट् (पा. सू. ३-४-९४) इति आडागमः । णिचः गुणः । अयादेशः । यच्छब्दस्य पूर्वत्वात् यद्वृत्तान्नित्यम् (पा. सू. ८-१-६६) इति निघातस्वरप्रतिषेधः भवति । णिच्स्वरः अवशिष्यते ।
  • वीरान्+उत — दीर्घादटि समानपादे (पा.सू. ८-३-९) इति नकारस्य रुत्वम् । आतोटिनित्यम् (पा. सू. ८-३-३) इति पूर्वस्य आकारस्य नित्यानुनासिकत्वम् ।

Ṛk 13

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

अ॒भी नो॑ अग्न उ॒क्तमिज्जु॑गुर्या॒ द्यावा॒क्षामा॒ सिंध॑वश्च॒ ॑ स्वगूर्ताः ।
गव्यं॒ यव्यं॒ यंतो॑ दी॒र्घाहेषं॒ वर॑मरु॒ण्यो॑ वरंत ॥१३॥

abhī no agna uktamijjuguryā dyāvākṣāmā siṃdhavaśca svagūrtāḥ | gavyaṃ yavyaṃ yaṃto dīrghāheṣaṃ varamaruṇyo varaṃta ‖13‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

अभि । नः । अग्ने । उकथं । इत् । जुगुर्याः! द्यावाक्षामा। सिंधवः । च । स्वगूर्ताः ।
गव्यं । यव्यं । यंतः । दीर्घा । अहा । इषं । वरं । अरुण्यः । वरंत ॥ १३ ॥

abhi | naḥ | agne | ukathaṃ | it | juguryāḥ! dyāvākṣāmā| siṃdhavaḥ | ca | svagūrtāḥ | gavyaṃ | yavyaṃ | yaṃtaḥ | dīrghā | ahā | iṣaṃ | varaṃ | aruṇyaḥ | varaṃta ‖ 13 ‖

p. 152

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे अग्ने न उकथं शस्त्रमभि जुगुर्याः । अभिमुख्येन स्तुहि प्रोत्साहय । सम्यक् शस्तमित्यंगीकुरु ॥ ग्य शब्दे । लिजि बहुलं छंदसीति विकरणस्य श्लुः । बहुलं छंदसीत्युत्वं ॥ तथा द्यावाक्षामा द्यावापृथिव्यावपि यज्ञ साधनसंपादनेन प्रोत्साह हयतां । तथा सिंधवः स्यंदनशीला नद्यश्च स्वगूर्ताः स्वयमेव गामिन्यो गव्यं गोसंभवं क्षीरादिकं गवां तृणाद्युत्पादनद्वारा यव्यं । उपलक्षणमेतत् । यवव्रीह्यादिजन्यं पुरोडाशादिकं यंतः प्रापयंतः प्रोत्साहयंतु । तथारुणो 5- रुणवर्णगोयुक्ताः मत्वर्थियो लुष्यते ॥ आरुण्यसाधनभूता उषसः । तद्देतुत्वात्ताच्छब्दं । दीर्घाहा सर्वाण्यहानि सर्वकालमिषमिष्यमाणमन्नरसादिकं वरं वरणीयं श्रेष्ठमन्यदपि यागसाधनं वरंत । प्रापयंतु ॥ वृज् संभक्तौ । अंतर्भावितण्यर्थाच्छांदसो लज् । व्यत्ययेन शप् ॥ साधयंतु । एतत्सर्वमग्नेः प्रसादादित्यग्नेरेव स्तुतित्वादाग्नेयत्वमविरुद्धं ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Agni, applaud our uktha (उकथं (ukathaṃ), recitation), शस्त्रं (śastraṃ)": praise it face to face, encourage it, accept it as well recited. The root ग्य (gya) is used of sound. Heaven and earth also should encourage us by providing the means of the sacrifice. Likewise the flowing rivers, स्वगूर्ताः (svagūrtāḥ), going of their own accord, should encourage us by bringing, through the growing of grass and the like for the cows, what comes from cows (milk and so on) and what comes from barley (यव्यं (yavyaṃ)); this is only an indication: the purodāśa and other offerings made of barley and rice are meant. The अरुण्यः (aruṇyaḥ) are the dawns, endowed with ruddy-coloured cows (the affix denoting "possessing" is dropped), or the dawns as the means of ruddiness, so called because they cause it. दीर्घाहा (dīrghāhā): on all days; इषं (iṣaṃ): food, sap and the like that is desired, at all times; वरं (varaṃ): choice, excellent; and any other means of sacrifice also, may they वरंत (varaṃta), bring about (root वृज् (vṛj), to share; a causative sense is implied). All this being through Agni's favour, the verse is praise of Agni alone, so its being addressed to Agni is not contradicted.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • अग्ने (agne)—O Agni
  • नः (naḥ)—our
  • उकं (ukaṃ)—hymn of praise
  • अभि जुगुर्याः (abhi juguryāḥ)—applaud it as excellent [declare your acceptance]
  • द्यावाक्षामा (dyāvākṣāmā)—may heaven and earth applaud
  • सिंधवः (siṃdhavaḥ)—those having the form of streams
  • स्वगूर्ताः च (svagūrtāḥ ca)—and the rivers that flow by their own nature
  • गव्यं (gavyaṃ)—(through growing and nourishing grass) the milk and the like of cows
  • यव्यं (yavyaṃ)—the purodāśa and the like made of barley
  • यंतः (yaṃtaḥ)—supplying (may they applaud our hymn)
  • अरुण्यः (aruṇyaḥ)—the dawns accompanied by golden-coloured cows
  • दीर्घाहा (dīrghāhā)—on all days
  • वरं (varaṃ)—excellent
  • इषं (iṣaṃ)—food
  • वरंत (varaṃta)—may they provide
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, applaud our hymn of praise as excellent and utter words of acceptance. May heaven and earth likewise applaud; may the rivers, flowing by their own nature, make grow the grass and the like which is the food of cows, and through it provide us the milk and the like of cows and the purodāśa and the like made of barley, and so applaud our hymn. May the dawns, accompanied by golden-coloured cows, provide excellent food on all days.

Printed English

Agni, be propitiated by this our earnest praise, and may heaven and earth, and the spontaneously-flowing (streams), provide for us the produce of

p. 153

the herd, and of the field ; and may the purple coursers (of the dawn) bestow upon us abundant food through a length of days.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

उक्तं अभि जुगुर्याः (uktaṃ abhi juguryāḥ)—"Praise our uktha as excellent": thus Agni is prayed to. Here Sāyaṇa has explained uktha as शस्त्रं (śastraṃ). Pointing out the subtle difference that exists in places between śastra and stotra, and the difference between the meaning "stotra" which Sāyaṇa gave to the word uktha in Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 4-3-3-7 and the meaning of the word uktha in sentences 4-2-3-6 to 9, he has explained this earlier. Here, since it is said that Agni and heaven and earth should applaud the sacrificer's uktha, we should understand a little what the greatness of this uktha is, which gladdens the gods.

The power of the uktha is very great, so that growth certainly comes to all who take refuge in it. There is a story in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa that once, when the Asuras took shelter in the uktha, great strength and growth came to them too, and Indra, being praised, came and drove them off.

ते वा असुरा मैत्रावरुणसोक्षमाश्रयंत सोऽब्रवीदिंद्रः कश्चाहं चेमानितोऽसुरान्नोत्स्यावहा इत्यहं चेत्यब्रवीद्वरुणस्तस्मादैंद्रावरुणं मैत्रावरुणस्कृतीयसवने शंसंतींद्रश्च हि तान्वरुणश्च ततो नुदेतां । (te vā asurā maitrāvaruṇasokṣamāśrayaṃta so 'bravīdiṃdraḥ kaścāhaṃ cemānito 'surānnotsyāvahā ityahaṃ cetyabravīdvaruṇastasmādaiṃdrāvaruṇaṃ maitrāvaruṇaskṛtīyasavane śaṃsaṃtīṃdraśca hi tānvaruṇaśca tato nudetāṃ |) The Asuras entered the Maitrāvaruṇa uktha. Then Indra asked who among them would help him drive the Asuras out of this uktha, and Varuṇa said that he would help. At that time the Maitrāvaruṇa, the assistant of the Hotṛ, at the third pressing recited the sūkta beginning with the Ṛk इंद्रावरुणा युवमध्वराय नो विशे जनाय महि शर्म यच्छतं (iṃdrāvaruṇā yuvamadhvarāya no viśe janāya mahi śarma yacchataṃ) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-82-1) and praised Indra and Varuṇa. Then Indra and Varuṇa drove those Asuras off with the Mitrāvaruṇa śastra.

ते वै ततोऽपहता असुरा ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिन उक्तमश्रयंत सोऽब्रवीदिंद्रः कश्चाहं चेमानितोऽसुरान्नोत्स्यावहा इत्यहं चेत्यब्रवीद्बृहस्पतिस्तस्मादैंद्राबार्हस्पत्यं ब्राह्मणाच्छंसी तृतीयसवने शंसतींद्रश्च हि तान्ब्रहस्पतिश्च हि ततो नुदेतां । (te vai tato 'pahatā asurā brāhmaṇācchaṃsina uktamaśrayaṃta so 'bravīdiṃdraḥ kaścāhaṃ cemānito 'surānnotsyāvahā ityahaṃ cetyabravīdbṛhaspatistasmādaiṃdrābārhaspatyaṃ brāhmaṇācchaṃsī tṛtīyasavane śaṃsatīṃdraśca hi tānbrahaspatiśca hi tato nudetāṃ |)

p. 154

The Asuras driven from there entered the uktha of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin. Then Indra rose and asked who would help him drive these Asuras out from here, and Bṛhaspati rose and said he would help. Then the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin at the third pressing recited the sūkta beginning with the Ṛk उदपुतो न वयो रक्षमाणा वावदतो अभ्रियस्येव घोषाः । गिरिभ्रजो नोर्मयो मदंतो बृहस्पतिमभ्यंकर्का अनावन् । (udaputo na vayo rakṣamāṇā vāvadato abhriyasyeva ghoṣāḥ | giribhrajo normayo madaṃto bṛhaspatimabhyaṃkarkā anāvan |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-68-1) and praised Indra and Bṛhaspati. Then Indra and Bṛhaspati together drove the Asuras off from there.

ते वै ततोऽपहता असुरा अच्छावाकस्योक्तमश्रयंत सोऽब्रवीदिंद्रः कश्चाहं चेमानितोऽसुरान्नोत्सावहा इत्यहं चेत्यब्रवीद्विष्णुस्तस्मादैंद्रावैष्णवमच्छावाकस्कृतीयसवने शंसतींद्रश्च हि तान्विष्णुश्च ततो नुदेतां । (te vai tato 'pahatā asurā acchāvākasyoktamaśrayaṃta so 'bravīdiṃdraḥ kaścāhaṃ cemānito 'surānnotsāvahā ityahaṃ cetyabravīdviṣṇustasmādaiṃdrāvaiṣṇavamacchāvākaskṛtīyasavane śaṃsatīṃdraśca hi tānviṣṇuśca tato nudetāṃ |) (I. Bra. 15-6) NOTE The Asuras driven out of the uktha of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin joined themselves to the uktha of the Acchāvāka. Then Indra rose and asked which of them would help him drive these out from here. Then Viṣṇu said he would help. At that time the Acchāvāka recited the sūkta beginning with the Ṛk — सं वां कर्मणा समिषा हिनोमींद्राविष्णू अपसस्पारे अस्य । जुषेथां यज्ञं द्रविणं च धत्तमरिष्टैर्नः पथिभिः पारयंता ॥ (— saṃ vāṃ karmaṇā samiṣā hinomīṃdrāviṣṇū apasaspāre asya | juṣethāṃ yajñaṃ draviṇaṃ ca dhattamariṣṭairnaḥ pathibhiḥ pārayaṃtā ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-69-1) and praised Indra and Viṣṇu. Then they drove the Asuras off from there too. This story is recited in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa (15-6). From it the power of the uktha, and the benefit that comes by it to the sacrificer who recites it, is understood.

Just as the power of the uktha is described at the time of sacrifices and other rites, so too in teaching spiritual knowledge the greatness of this uktha, of the nature of praise, is extolled. In the Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad: उक्कं प्राणो वा उक्कं प्राणो हीदं सर्वमुत्थापयत्युद्धास्मादुक्खविद्वीरस्तिष्ठत्युक्थस्य सायुज्यं सलोकतां जयति य एवं वेद (ukkaṃ prāṇo vā ukkaṃ prāṇo hīdaṃ sarvamutthāpayatyuddhāsmādukkhavidvīrastiṣṭhatyukthasya sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ jayati ya evaṃ veda) (Bṛ. U. 5-13-1) उक्तं तथोपासनांतरं । उक्तं शस्त्रं । तद्धि प्रधानं महाव्रते क्रत् । (uktaṃ tathopāsanāṃtaraṃ | uktaṃ śastraṃ | taddhi pradhānaṃ mahāvrate krat |) (Śāṅkara-bhāṣya) NOTE

p. 155

In the sacrifice of the form Mahāvrata, the uktha, the principal śastra, is itself the vital breath (prāṇa). By it rising up (utthāna) comes about. Therefore a son who knows the uktha is born and obtains likeness to it and equal honour. Thus the greatness of the uktha is told. When such an uktha is being recited, "Know its greatness and praise it" means: may it gladden you and become worthy of your praise.

अभि जुगुर्याः- अभिमुख्येन स्तुहि । प्रोत्साहय सम्यक्वस्तमित्यंगीकुरु (abhi juguryāḥ- abhimukhyena stuhi | protsāhaya samyakvastamityaṃgīkuru) means: speak words of acceptance, "it has been praised in a special manner". Or else, in the Ṛk प्र स्तोषदुप गासिषच्छवत्साम गीयमानं । अभि राधसा जुगुरत् (pra stoṣadupa gāsiṣacchavatsāma gīyamānaṃ | abhi rādhasā jugurat) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-81-5) the verb अभि जुगुरत् (abhi jugurat) has the sense अभिगृणातु स्वीकुरु (abhigṛṇātu svīkuru), "accept"; so here too the meaning may be "accept". The purport is the same.

स्वगूर्ताः (svagūrtāḥ)—स्वयमेव गामिन्यः (svayameva gāminyaḥ): Sāyaṇa has explained it as "flowing by their own nature". But the word गूर्त (gūrta) ordinarily means "worthy of praise, renowned"; it also means praisers, those who extol. For example, in the Ṛk तं गूर्तयो नेमन्निषः परीणसः समुद्रं न संचरणे सनिष्यवः । पतिं दक्षस्य विदथस्य नू सहो गिरिं न वेना अधिरोह तेजसा । (taṃ gūrtayo nemanniṣaḥ parīṇasaḥ samudraṃ na saṃcaraṇe saniṣyavaḥ | patiṃ dakṣasya vidathasya nū saho giriṃ na venā adhiroha tejasā |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-56-2) गूर्तयः (gūrtayaḥ) is explained as स्तोत्रारः (stotrāraḥ), and in तं वः सखायो मदाय प्रसानमभि गायक । शिशुं न यज्ञैः स्वदयंत गूर्तिभिः । (taṃ vaḥ sakhāyo madāya prasānamabhi gāyaka | śiśuṃ na yajñaiḥ svadayaṃta gūrtibhiḥ |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-105-1) गूर्तिभिः (gūrtibhiḥ) is explained as स्तुतिभिः (stutibhiḥ), "with praises"; and likewise in other places too the meaning "praiseworthy, renowned" occurs. Accordingly, in the present Ṛk too one may explain: rivers of praiseworthy or abundant flow.

Grammar
  • अभि — निपातस्य च (पा. सू. ६-३-१५६) इति संहितायां दीर्घः भवति ।
  • जुगुर्याः — ग्य शप्पे इति धातुः । लज् मध्यमपुरुष एकवचने सिप् । इतश्च इति इकारलोपः । बहुलं छंदसि इति विकरणस्य श्लु आदेशः । बहुलं छंदसि इति

p. 156

  • इति धातोः उत्वम् । उरणप्ररः इति रसरवागि भवति । श्लौ (पा. सू. ६-१-१०) इति धातोः द्वित्वम् । प्रत्ययस्य यासुटागमः । अतिजंतस्य परत्वात् निघातस्वरः भवति । NOTE
  • द्यावाक्षामा — दौश्च क्षामाश्च द्यावाक्षामा । दिवोद्यावा (पा. सू. ६-३-२९) इति उत्तरपदे परे द्यावादेशः । सुपां सुलुक्—(पा. सू. ७-१-३९) इति विभक्तेः (औ) आकारादेशः । देवताद्वंद्वे च (पा. सू. ६-२-१४१) इति उभयपदप्रकृतिस्वरः भवति । क्षामा भूमिपर्यायत्वेन वेदे पठितः ।
  • सिंधवः — स्यंदू प्रस्रवणे इति धातुः । स्यंदेस्संप्रसारणं धश्च (उ. सू. १-११) इति उन्‌प्रत्ययः । धातोः दकारस्य धकारादेशः । नित्त्वात् आद्युदात्तस्वरः भवति ।
  • गव्यम् — गोर्विकारः गव्यम् । गोपयसोर्यत् (पा. सू. ४-३-१६०) इति यत् प्रत्ययः । वांतोयि प्रत्यये (पा. सू. ६-१-७९) इति अवादेशः । यतोऽनावः (पा. सू. ६-१-२१३) इति आद्युदात्तस्वरः भवति । एवमेव यव्यम् इत्यत्रापि स्वरप्रत्ययाः भवंति ।
  • यंतः — इण् गतौ इति धातुः । प्रेरणात् अंतर्भानितण्यर्थकः धातुः । लडर्थे शतृप्रत्ययः । इणोयण् (पा. सू. ६-४-८१) इति धातोः यणादेशः । प्रत्ययस्य आद्युदात्तस्वरः भवति ।
  • अहा — शेश्छंदसि बहुलम् (पा सू- ६-१-७०) इति शेः लोसः ।
  • अरुण्यः — अत्र अरुणवर्णविशिष्टाः इति अर्थप्रतीतेः छांदसत्वेन मत्त्वर्थप्रत्ययः लुप्तः ।
  • वरंत — वृज् संभक्तौ इति धातुः । छंदसि लुज् लज् लिटः (पा. सू. ३-४-६) इति लोडर्थे लज् । प्रेरणात् अंतर्भानितण्यर्थकः धातुः । प्रथमपुरुषबहुवचने झ प्रत्ययः । अंतादेशः । शप् विकरणम् । धातोः गुणः । बहुलं छंदस्यमाज् योगेऽपि (पा. सू. ६-४-७५) इति अडागमः न भवति । अतिजंतस्य परत्वात् निघातस्वरः भवति ।

p. 157

Sūkta 141 (Maṇḍala 1)

Sāyaṇa's introduction (Sanskrit): this is the second sūkta, of thirteen Ṛks, beginning बळित्था (baḷitthā); its seer is Dīrghatamas; the metre is Jagatī, except that the last two Ṛks are Triṣṭubh; the deity is Agni. Its use in the Prātaranuvāka and in the Āśvina-śastra has been stated already.

Anuvāda. This sūkta beginning बळित्था (baḷitthā) is the second sūkta in the twenty-first anuvāka. It has thirteen Ṛks. Its seer is Dīrghatamas and its deity is Agni. The last two Ṛks are in the Triṣṭup metre; the other Ṛks are in the Jagatī metre. It was stated earlier that this sūkta is used at the time of reciting the Prātaranuvāka mantras and the Āśvina-śastra mantras.

Particulars: Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 21, Sūkta 141. Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Vargas 8, 9. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 13. Seer: Dīrghatamas Aucathya. Deity: Agni. Metre: Ṛks 1–11 Jagatī, Ṛks 12–13 Triṣṭup.

Ṛk 1

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

बळि॒त्था तद्वपु॑षे धायि दर्श॒तं दे॒वस्य॒ भर्गः॒ सह॑सो॒ यतो॒ ॑ जनि ।
यदी॒मुप॒ ह्वर॑ते॒ साध॑ते म॒तिर्ऋ॒तस्य॒ धेना॑ अनयंत स॒स्रुतः॑ ॥ १ ॥

baḷitthā tadvapuṣe dhāyi darśataṃ devasya bhargaḥ sahaso yato jani | yadīmupa hvarate sādhate matirṛtasya dhenā anayaṃta sasrutaḥ ‖ 1 ‖

p. 158

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

बट् । इत्था । तत् । वपुषे । धायि । दर्शतं । देवस्य । भर्गः । सहसः । यतः । जनि ।
यत् । ईं । उप । ह्वरते । साधते । मतिः । ऋतस्य । धेनाः। अनयंत। सऽस्रुतः ॥१॥

baṭ | itthā | tat | vapuṣe | dhāyi | darśataṃ | devasya | bhargaḥ | sahasaḥ | yataḥ | jani | yat | īṃ | upa | hvarate | sādhate | matiḥ | ṛtasya | dhenāḥ| anayaṃta| sa 'srutaḥ ‖1‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

देवस्य द्योतनशीलस्यादित्यस्य दर्शतं सर्वैर्दर्शनीयं तत् प्रसिद्धं भर्गस्तेज इत्तेत्थं सर्वैर्दृश्यमानप्रकारेण वपुषे शरीरव्यवहाराय दार्ढ्याय धायि । धार्यते सर्वैः । बळितेत्युभे अपि सत्यनामनी बट् श्रत् सत्रेत्थति तन्नामसु पाठात् । जातराग्निना भुक्तानां जरणेन शरीरधारणं प्रसिद्धं । तत्रोपपत्तिमाह । यतः सहसो जनि । यतः कारणान्मथनकाले बलेनोत्पन्नः अतो बलाय धार्यत इत्यर्थः । यदीं यदेतत्पसिद्धं लोकोपकार्यग्नेस्तेजो मतिर्मदीया बुद्धिरुप ह्वरते उपगच्छति उपगम्य वर्तते वा ॥ ह्व कौटिल्ये ॥ साधते च तेनैव तेजसा साधयति स्वाभीष्टं । किंच ऋतस्य यज्ञसाधकस्याग्नेस्तेजसा धेनाः सर्वप्राणिनां वाचः सस्रुतः समानं गच्छंत्यः सहैव प्रवर्तमानाः ॥ स्रवतेः कर्तरि क्विप् ॥ अनयंत । नयंति । निर्वहंति जगद्व्यवहारं ॥ व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदं ॥ यद्वा। ऋतस्य धेना यज्ञस्य संबंधिन्नो मंत्ररूपा वाचः सस्रुतो होत्रादिमुखेन सहैव प्रवर्तमाना अनयंत । नयंति । अग्ने स्तोत्रं निर्वहंति । अग्नेस्तेजसा वा यज्ञं निर्वहंति । तेजोमयिया वागिति श्रुतेः । छां. उ. ६_५_४ । अतः कारणान्मतिरुपह्वरत इत्यर्थः । धेनेति वाङ्णाम धेना ग्ना इति तन्नामसु पाठात् ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

Of the shining god, Āditya, that well-known brilliance (भर्गः (bhargaḥ)), visible to all, is sustained by everyone in this manner, for the firmness of the body, for bodily activity. बट् (baṭ) and इत्था (itthā) are both names of truth, since they are read among its names. The bodily support of food eaten, through its digestion by the digestive fire (जातराग्नि (jātarāgni)), is well known. He gives the reason: यतः सहसो जनि (yataḥ sahaso jani), that is, because Agni is born by force at the time of churning, he is held for the sake of strength. यदीं (yadīṃ): this well-known, world-benefiting brilliance of Agni: my mind (मतिः (matiḥ)) approaches it (उप ह्वरते (upa hvarate), from ह्व कौटिल्ये (hva kauṭilye)), or abides having approached, and by that very brilliance accomplishes its desire. Further, by the brilliance of Agni, who accomplishes the sacrifice (ऋतस्य (ṛtasya)), the धेनाः (dhenāḥ), the speech of all living beings, सस्रुतः (sasrutaḥ), flowing together, proceeding together, अनयंत (anayaṃta), carry on the business of the world (the middle voice is by vyatyaya). Or else: the धेनाः (dhenāḥ) connected with the sacrifice, the speech in the form of mantras, proceeding together through the mouths of the Hotṛ and the others, carry out the praise of Agni, or carry out the sacrifice by Agni's brilliance, according to the śruti "speech is made of brilliance" (Chā. U. 6-5-4). Therefore the mind approaches. धेना (dhenā) is a name of speech, since it is read among its names ("dhenā, gnāḥ").

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • देवस्य (devasya)—of the shining Āditya
  • दर्शतं (darśataṃ)—that which is visible (to all)
  • तत् (tat)—that well-known
  • भर्गः (bhargaḥ)—brilliance
  • इत्था (itthā)—in this manner
  • यतः (yataḥ)—for which reason
  • सहसः (sahasaḥ)—from strength
  • जनि (jani)—it was born (such a brilliance)
  • वपुषे (vapuṣe)—for the firmness of the body
  • धायि (dhāyi)—is held (by all)
  • यदीं (yadīṃ)—this well-known, world-benefiting brilliance which
  • मतिः (matiḥ)—my mind
  • उपह्वरते (upahvarate)—approaches (with effort)
  • साधते (sādhate)—accomplishes (its desired end)
  • ऋतस्य (ṛtasya)—of Agni, the accomplisher of the sacrifice (together with his brilliance)
  • धेनाः (dhenāḥ)—the speech of all living beings
  • ससुतः (sasutaḥ)—come together and unite
  • अनयंत (anayaṃta)—carry on (the business of the world)
  • [Or ऋतस्य (ṛtasya)—connected with the sacrifice; धेनाः (dhenāḥ)—these speeches in the form of mantras; ससुतः (sasutaḥ)—issuing from the mouths of the Hotṛ and the others; अनयंत (anayaṃta)—carry out (the praise of Agni).]

p. 159

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The brilliance of Āditya, visible to all and well known, has been born of strength in order to give firmness of body to all living beings; and for the very attainment of that firmness all beings hold it. My mind grasps this well-known, world-benefiting brilliance and accomplishes its desired end. At the time of the sacrifice, the speech filled with mantras, issuing from the mouths of the Hotṛ and the others, carries out the praise of this Agni.

Printed English

Verily, that visible radiance of the divine ( Agni ) has been so apprehended (by all, that it may be) for (the support of) the body, for which end it has been generated by ( bodily ) strength : and that my mind may apprehend and apply ( that radiance ), they address the sacred prayers associated with oblations (to Agni).

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

भर्गः (bhargaḥ)—तेजः (tejaḥ). The word भर्ग (bharga) is customarily used only for the brilliance of Agni (in the form of Āditya). In the Ṛk तत्सवितुर्वरेण्यं भर्गॊ देवस्य धीमहि । धियो यो नः प्रचोदयात् ॥ (tatsaviturvareṇyaṃ bhargò devasya dhīmahi | dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayāt ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-62-10) Sāyaṇa explains the word भर्ग (bharga) as अविद्यातत्कारयोर्भर्जनाद्भर्गः (avidyātatkārayorbharjanādbhargaḥ); that is, since it destroys ignorance and its effects, such as desire and delusion, the nature of Savitṛ is said to be expressed by the word भर्ग (bharga).

सहसः जनि (sahasaḥ jani)—Because he is born of strength at the time of churning the araṇi, he is described as सहसः जनि (sahasaḥ jani).

ऋतस्य धेनाः (ṛtasya dhenāḥ)—Here the word ऋत (ṛta) means sacrifice. Showing the construction that ऋतस्य (ṛtasya) means of the sacrifice-connected, or of Agni who accomplishes the sacrifice, धेनाः (dhenāḥ), he explains the word धेनाः (dhenāḥ) as सर्वप्राणिनां वाचः यद्वा यज्ञस्य संबंधिन्यः मंत्र-रूपा वाचः (sarvaprāṇināṃ vācaḥ yadvā yajñasya saṃbaṃdhinyaḥ maṃtra-rūpā vācaḥ), that is, the speech of all beings, or the speech in the form of mantras connected with the sacrifice, and he cites the Upaniṣadic sentence तेजोमयी वाक् (tejomayī vāk) (Chā. U. 6-5-4). From this quotation itself it is understood that the word धेना (dhenā) does not mean ordinary speech but speech that is supernatural, endowed with brilliance and sanctified by mantras.

p. 160

But since Sāyaṇa has in some places made a difference in meaning, it must be examined whether this word has one definite meaning or whether its meaning varies with the context.

सम्यक्स्रवंति सरितो न धेना अंतर्हृदा मनसा पूयमानाः । एते अर्षंत्यूर्मयो घृतस्य मृगा इव क्षिपणोरीषमाणाः । (samyaksravaṃti sarito na dhenā aṃtarhṛdā manasā pūyamānāḥ | ete arṣaṃtyūrmayo ghṛtasya mṛgā iva kṣipaṇorīṣamāṇāḥ |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-58-6) त्वमिंद्र स्रवितवा अपस्कः परिष्ठिता अहिना शूर पूर्वीः । त्वद्वावक्रे रथ्यो३ न धेना रेजंते विश्वा कृत्रिमाणि भीषा । (tvamiṃdra sravitavā apaskaḥ pariṣṭhitā ahinā śūra pūrvīḥ | tvadvāvakre rathyo3 na dhenā rejaṃte viśvā kṛtrimāṇi bhīṣā |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-21-3) In these Ṛks Sāyaṇa takes the word धेना (dhenā) as a flowing river. In the Ṛk मादयस्व हरिभिर्ये त इंद्र वि ष्यस्व शिप्रे वि सृजस्व धेने । आ त्वा सुशिप्र हरयो वहंतूशन्नव्यानि प्रति नो जुषस्व । (mādayasva haribhirye ta iṃdra vi ṣyasva śipre vi sṛjasva dhene | ā tvā suśipra harayo vahaṃtūśannavyāni prati no juṣasva |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-101-10) he explains पानसाधनभूते जिह्वोपजिह्विके (pānasādhanabhūte jihvopajihvike), that is, the tongue and the uvula (upajihvā), the instruments for drinking. The author of the Nirukta cites this same Ṛk (1-101-10), shows the derivation धेना दधातेः (dhenā dadhāteḥ), and gives the meaning of drinkable milk (Ni. 6-17). Apart from these, in the remaining Ṛks Sāyaṇa gives the meaning "speech". But if one examines the contexts in which this word is used, in the Saṃhitā and elsewhere, there seems to be no reason for any meaning other than speech in the form of praise. If one looks at the passage used in the Śrauta-sūtras in this connection, there too the same meaning seems to have more room.

When the Śrauta-sūtras give the list of the wives of the gods, the name धेना (dhenā) is well known for the wife of Bṛhaspati ("सेनेंद्रस्य, धेना बृहस्पतेः (seneṃdrasya, dhenā bṛhaspateḥ)"). In all these places the meaning is only speech in the form of praise; there is no room for other meanings. It would not be wrong to give this same meaning to the word in the Ṛks cited above. For example, in Ṛk 4-58-6, सम्यक्स्रवंति सरितो न धेना अंतर्हृदा मनसा पूयमानाः (samyaksravaṃti sarito na dhenā aṃtarhṛdā manasā pūyamānāḥ): "like rivers flowing without obstruction, धेनाः (dhenāḥ) purified within the heart and mind", it is fitting, and not wrong, to say that they are speeches in the form of praise, issuing naturally from the heart and with a purified mind. Moreover the words मनसा (manasā), अंतर्हृदा (aṃtarhṛdā) and पूयमानाः (pūyamānāḥ) agree naturally with धेनाः (dhenāḥ). Sāyaṇa's joining those words with the words एते धृतस्य ऊर्मयः (ete dhṛtasya ūrmayaḥ) does not give a natural sense.

p. 161

NOTE Similarly in Ṛk 1-101-10 also, the dual धेने (dhene) may indicate the two offerings, praise and oblation. But in the Ṛk पितुश्चिदूर्धजनुषा विवेद व्यस्य धारा असृजद्वि धेनाः । गुहा चरंतं सखिभिः शिवेभिर्दिवो यह्वीभिर्न गुहा बभूव । (pituścidūrdhajanuṣā viveda vyasya dhārā asṛjadvi dhenāḥ | guhā caraṃtaṃ sakhibhiḥ śivebhirdivo yahvībhirna guhā babhūva |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-1-9) it is reasonable that he has said that ऊधः (ūdhaḥ) is the atmosphere, धारा (dhārā) is the stream of rain, and धेनाः (dhenāḥ) is the roaring sound of thunder. Leaving aside these few examples, in the rest, namely विशंविशं मघवा पर्यशायत जनानां धेना अवचाकशद्वषा । यस्याह शक्रः सवनेषु रण्यति स तीव्रैः सोमैः सहते पृतन्यतः । (viśaṃviśaṃ maghavā paryaśāyata janānāṃ dhenā avacākaśadvaṣā | yasyāha śakraḥ savaneṣu raṇyati sa tīvraiḥ somaiḥ sahate pṛtanyataḥ |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-43-6) विरेण्यः क्रतुरिंद्रः सुशस्तिरुतापि धेना पुरुहूतमीट्टे । आर्दयद्वृत्रमकृणोदु लोकं ससाहे शक्रः पृतना अभिष्टिः ॥ (vireṇyaḥ kraturiṃdraḥ suśastirutāpi dhenā puruhūtamīṭṭe | ārdayadvṛtramakṛṇodu lokaṃ sasāhe śakraḥ pṛtanā abhiṣṭiḥ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-104-10) and the other Ṛks of this kind, Sāyaṇa has explained it everywhere as प्रीणयित्री स्तुतिवाक् (prīṇayitrī stutivāk). Likewise the word धेने (dhene) in Ṛk 1-101-10 cited above, and the word in the Ṛk स्त्रियो हि दास आयुधानि चक्रे किं मा करन्नबला अस्य सेनाः । अंतर्ह्यख्यदुभे अस्य धेने अथोप प्रैद्युधये दस्युमिंद्रः ॥ (striyo hi dāsa āyudhāni cakre kiṃ mā karannabalā asya senāḥ | aṃtarhyakhyadubhe asya dhene athopa praidyudhaye dasyumiṃdraḥ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-30-9) can, since the dual stands in both places, be taken to mean praise and oblation. In Ṛk 5-30-9 Sāyaṇa explains अस्य (असुरस्य) धेने उभे अंतः अख्युद्दि (asya (asurasya) dhene ubhe aṃtaḥ akhyuddi): both women of the Asura stood in the middle of the house, and then Indra fought Namuci face to face. Instead of taking धेना (dhenā) as "woman", it would fit better to say: when Namuci prepared an army in the form of women, praise and oblation entered Indra's inner heart and roused him to battle.

In the same way, in the present Ṛk also, for ऋतस्य धेना सस्रुवः (ṛtasya dhenā sasruvaḥ), rather than Sāyaṇa's first meaning, the speeches in the form of praise, connected with the sacrifice and flowing from the mouths of the Hotṛ and the others, that is, Sāyaṇa's second meaning, seems clear and correct.

p. 162

इत्था (itthā)—बट्, इत्था इत्युभे अपि सत्यनामनी । (baṭ, itthā ityubhe api satyanāmanī |) (Ni. 3-10). बट् (baṭ) and इत्था (itthā) are both included among the names of truth. The meaning is "certainly".

Grammar
  • इत्था — इदम्शब्दः । प्रकारार्थे इदमस्थमुः इत्यस्मात् थमुप्रत्ययः । व्यत्ययेन विभक्तेः डादेशः ।
  • धायि — डु धाञ् धारणपोषणयोः धातुः । छंदसि लुज् लज् लिटः (पा.सू. ३-४-६) इत्यस्मात् वर्तमानार्थे कर्मणि लुज् । लट् प्रथमपुरुषैकवचने तप्रत्ययः । चिण्‌भावकर्मणोः (पा. सू. ३-१-६६) इत्यस्मात् चिळेः चिणादेशः । चिणोलुक् (पा. सू ६-४-१०४) इत्यस्मात् तशब्दस्य लुक् । आतो युक् चिण् कृतोः (पा. सू. ७-३-३३) इत्यस्मात् धातोः युकागमः । बहुलं छंदस्यमाज्‌योगेऽपि इत्यस्मात् अडागमो न भवति । तिजंतनिघातस्वरो भवति ।
  • दर्शतम् — दृशिर् प्रेक्षणे धातुः । भ्रमृदृशि (उ. सू. ३-३९०) इत्यस्मात् कर्मणि अतच् प्रत्ययः । तं निमित्तीकृत्य धातोः इकः गुणः । उरणप्ररः इत्यस्मात् रपरत्वं भवति । प्रत्ययस्य चित्त्वात् चितः (पा. सू. ६-१-१६३) इत्यस्मात् अंतोदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
  • सहसः — सह मर्षणे धातुः । औणादिको असुन् प्रत्ययः । नित्त्वात् आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
  • जनि — जनी प्रादुर्भावे धातुः । पूर्ववत् छांदसो लुज् । प्रथमपुरुषैकवचनांतरूपम् । यद्योगात् निघातस्वरो न भवति ।
  • ह्वरते — हृ कौटिल्ये धातुः । लट् प्रथमपुरुषैकवचने तप्रत्ययः । टेः एत्वम् । शप् विकरणः । तं निमित्तीकृत्य धातोः इकः गुणः । रपरत्वं भवति । यद्योगात् निघातस्वरो न भवति । अदुपदेशात् परस्य लसार्वधातुकस्य तास्यनुदात्तेत्— (पा. सू. ६-१-१८६) इत्यस्मात् अनुदात्तत्वात् धातुस्वरः अवतिष्ठते । NOTE
  • साधते — साध संसिद्धौ धातुः । हेतुमति च इत्यस्मात् णिच् । लट् प्रथमपुरुषैकवचने तप्रत्ययः । टेः एत्वम् । शपः छंदस्युभयथा (पा. सू. ३-४-११७) इत्यस्मात् अर्धधातुकसंज्ञात्वात् शेरनिटि (पा. सू. ६-४-५१) इत्यस्मात् णिचो लोपः । तिजंतस्य परत्वात् निघातस्वरो न भवति । धामस्वरः अवतिष्ठते ।

p. 163

  • अनयंत — णीञ् प्रापणे धातुः । छंदसि लुज् लज् लिटः इत्यस्मात् वर्तमानार्थे लज् । व्यत्ययो बहुलम् इत्यस्मात् आत्मनेपदप्रत्ययो भवति । प्रथमपुरुषबहुवचनांतरूपम् । अतिजंतस्य परत्वात् निघातस्वरो भवति ।
  • सस्तुतः — समानं प्रवंति इति सस्तुतः । स्रु गतौ धातुः । क्विप् च (पा. सू. ३-२-७६) इत्यस्मात् कर्तरि क्विप् प्रत्ययः । ह्रस्वस्य पिति कृति तुक् (पा. सू. ६-१-७१) इत्यस्मात् तुकागमः । समानस्य सभावः । गतिकारकोपपदात् कृत् इत्यस्मात् कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति । प्रथमाबहुवचनांतरूपम् । NOTE

Ṛk 2

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

पृ॒क्षो वपुः॑ पितु॒मान्नित्य॒ आ श॑ये द्वि॒तीय॒मा स॒प्तशि॑वासु ॒॑ मातृषु ।
तृ॒तीय॑मस्य वृष॒भस्य॑ दो॒हसे॒ दश॑प्रमतिं जनयंत॒ योष॑णः ॥ २ ॥

pṛkṣo vapuḥ pitumānnitya ā śaye dvitīyamā saptaśivāsu mātṛṣu | tṛtīyamasya vṛṣabhasya dohase daśapramatiṃ janayaṃta yoṣaṇaḥ ‖ 2 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

पृक्षः । वपुः। पितुमान् । नित्यः। आ । शये । द्वितीयं । आ । सप्तशिवासु । मातृषु ।
तृतीयं । अस्य । वृषभस्य । दोहसे । दशप्रमतिं । जनयंत । योषणः ॥ २ ॥

pṛkṣaḥ | vapuḥ| pitumān | nityaḥ| ā | śaye | dvitīyaṃ | ā | saptaśivāsu | mātṛṣu | tṛtīyaṃ | asya | vṛṣabhasya | dohase | daśapramatiṃ | janayaṃta | yoṣaṇaḥ ‖ 2 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

आयमग्निः वृक्षोऽन्न साधकः पाकादिना वपुर्वपुष्माञ्चरीराभिवृद्धिहेतुः पितुमान् दनिर्लक्षणान्न युक्तो नित्यः शाश्वतः । ईदृशः सन् प्रथमं पृथिवीस्थानः सन्ना शये । आशेते । दाहपाकादि लौकिकं कर्म, यज्ञादि वैदिकं कर्म, च निर्वर्तयन्भवो भूमौ वर्तत इत्यर्थः । तथा सप्तशिवासु मातृषु सप्तलोकशिवकरीषु मातृस्थानीयासु हितकरीषु वृष्टिषु द्वितीयमाशेते । मध्यमस्थानो विद्युद्रूपो ना वर्तते । अस्य वृषभस्य वर्षितुरस्यैव वैद्युताग्नेः सहायत्वेन संबंधिने दोहसे दोग्य आदित्यस्थोदकस्य वर्षयित्र आदित्यरश्मये ॥ महेः कर्तर्यसुप्रत्ययः ॥ तत्पवृत्तये तृतीयमाशेते । म्यस्थानो वर्तते । यद्वा । अस्य वृषभस्य

Gist of the bhāṣya

This Agni, पृक्षः (pṛkṣaḥ) Here the printed bhāṣya has vṛkṣaḥ, is the accomplisher of food by cooking and the like. वपुः (vapuḥ): possessed of a body, the cause of the growth of bodies. पितुमान् (pitumān): endowed with food, by indication; नित्यः (nityaḥ): eternal. Being such, he first abides (आ शये (ā śaye), आशेते (āśete)) on earth, as one whose place is the earth: he is present on earth accomplishing both the worldly work, such as burning and cooking, and the Vedic work, such as sacrifice. Likewise he abides as the second form in the सप्तशिवासु मातृषु (saptaśivāsu mātṛṣu), that is, in the rains, which do good to the seven worlds and stand in the place of mothers, beneficent: being of the middle region, he exists in the form of lightning. अस्य वृषभस्य (asya vṛṣabhasya): of this shower-giver; दोहसे (dohase): for the sunbeam that rains down the water present in Āditya, to be milked, and connected as helper with this very lightning-fire (the suffix असु (asu) in the agent sense, from मह (maha)); for its activity he abides as the third form (…). Or else: अस्य वृषभस्य (asya vṛṣabhasya) … (the block breaks off here; the next window continues). NOTE

p. 164

वर्षितुः प्रसिद्धस्यादित्यस्य संबंधिने दोग्ने रश्मये तत्प्रवृत्त्यर्थं । आदित्यरश्मयो घर्मकाले भूमिस्थमुदकमाकृष्य सूर्यं प्रापय्य तत्र चिरकालां धृत्वा पुनरंतरिक्षं प्राप्य मेघेषु स्थित्वा वर्षकाले प्रवर्षंतीति प्रसिद्धं । अतो रश्मेर्दोर्ग्धत्वं । ईदृशं त्रिस्थानमग्निं महाभागं योषणो मिश्रणशीलाः सर्वा दिशोजनयंत ! उत्पादयंति । सर्वासु दिक्षु प्रसृत इत्यर्थः । कीदृशं तं । दशप्रमतिं । दशसु दिक्षु प्रकृष्टमननवंतं पूज्यत्वाय । यद्वा । मधनकाले दशभिरंगुलीभिरुत्पन्नं लोकत्रये दशदिक्षु च व्याप्तमित्यर्थः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

(Continuing the second explanation of दोहसे (dohase).) The ray belonging to the well-known Āditya, the showerer, is the one to be milked, and the milking is for the sake of its operation. It is well known that in the hot season the sun's rays draw up the water that lies on the earth and bring it to the sun. There they hold it for a long time. Then they reach the atmosphere, stay in the clouds, and pour it down in the rainy season. So the ray is the one that is milked. This Agni, who dwells in three stations and is of great share, is generated by the women who mingle, that is, by all the quarters of space. That means he spreads in all the quarters. What is he like? He is दशप्रमतिं (daśapramatiṃ): he has excellent thought in the ten quarters, so he is worthy of worship. Or else, at the time of churning he is produced by the ten fingers and pervades the three worlds and the ten quarters.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • अयं अग्निः (ayaṃ agniḥ)—this Agni
  • पृक्षः (pṛkṣaḥ)—as the one who nourishes food by cooking and the like (as the digester)
  • वपुः (vapuḥ)—as the one who promotes the growth of the body
  • पितुर्मा (piturmā)—as the one who has food in the form of the oblation
  • नित्यः (nityaḥ)—as the eternal one; being so
  • आ शये (ā śaye)—(first, in the form of fire, upon the earth) he lies spread out
  • द्वितीयं (dvitīyaṃ)—secondly (in the second form)
  • सप्तशिवासु (saptaśivāsu)—in those that are auspicious to the seven worlds
  • मातृषु (mātṛṣu)—in the regions of creation, which stand in the place of mothers
  • आ (शये) (ā (śaye))—(in the form of lightning) he lies spread out
  • तृतीयं (tṛtīyaṃ)—thirdly (in another form)
  • अस्य वृषभस्य (asya vṛṣabhasya)—belonging to Āditya, the maker of rain
  • दोहसे (dohase)—for the operation of the rays (of Āditya) that pour down rain (he lies spread out in the heavenly world)
  • दशप्रमतिं (daśapramatiṃ)—this Agni, who is worshipful and a giver of joy by illuminating the ten quarters, or who, produced with the help of the ten fingers, has spread to the ten quarters
  • योषणः (yoṣaṇaḥ)—all the united regions of space
  • जनयंत (janayaṃta)—cause to unfold
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni is the nourisher of food (the digester), the promoter of the body's growth, the possessor of food in the form of oblation, and the eternal one. First, he accomplishes the worldly acts such as cooking and the Vedic acts such as sacrifice, and lies spread out eternally upon the earth. Secondly, he lies spread out in the form of lightning in the regions of rain, which are auspicious to the seven worlds and stand in the place of mothers. Thirdly, he lies spread out in the heavenly world, for the operation of the rays of Āditya, who belongs to the rain-maker and pours down rain. All the united regions of space together cause to unfold this Agni, who is worshipful and a giver of joy because he illuminates the ten quarters.

Printed English

First, he reposes (on the earth) as the digestive (faculty), the embodied, the accepter of food, the eternal : secoudly, (he dwells) among the seven

p. 165

auspicious mothers (of fertility) : thirdly, the associated (regions) generate him, delighting in the ten (quarters) of space, for the sake of milking this showerer (of rain).

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk three kinds of manifestation of Agni are described. The Nirukta authors say that all the seers pay homage to the deity Agni, who is in the heavenly world in the form of Āditya, in the atmosphere in the form of lightning-fire, and on the earth in the form of fire. Then they explain the three forms in the three stations clearly, with examples from Saṃhitā passages. If the Nirukta passage is taken in the order of this Ṛk, first, in the sentence स्तोमेन हि यं दिवि देवा अग्निमजनयञ्क्तिभिः कर्मभिद्यार्वापृथिव्योः पूरणं तमकुर्वंस्त्रेधाभावाय पृथिव्यामंतरिक्षे दिवीति शाकपूणिः । (stomena hi yaṃ divi devā agnimajanayañktibhiḥ karmabhidyārvāpṛthivyoḥ pūraṇaṃ tamakurvaṃstredhābhāvāya pṛthivyāmaṃtarikṣe divīti śākapūṇiḥ |) (Ni. 7-28), the Nirukta authors, following Śākapūṇi's explanation, state that Agni manifests in the three stations — earth, atmosphere and heavenly world — in the three forms Agni, Jātavedas and Vaiśvānara. This order is set out in the Nirukta (Ni. 7-14 to 7-28) on the basis of Ṛks of the Ṛksaṃhitā such as मूर्धा भुवो भवति नक्तमग्निः (mūrdhā bhuvo bhavati naktamagniḥ) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-88-6). The same division is stated, in the order Pavamāna, Śuci and Pāvaka, in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā sentences अग्नये पवमानाय पुरोडाशमष्टाकपालं निर्वपेदग्नये पावका याग्नये शुचये । (agnaye pavamānāya puroḍāśamaṣṭākapālaṃ nirvapedagnaye pāvakā yāgnaye śucaye |) (Tai. Saṃ. 2-2-4). That Agni's threefold existence, and the threefold manifestation corresponding to it, reflect the fundamental principle of the world is known from the description in the Bṛhaddevatā: भवद्भूतस्य भव्यस्य जंगमस्थावरस्य च । अस्येके सूरमेवैकं प्रभवं प्रलयं विदुः ॥ एतद्भूतेषु लोकेषु अग्निभूतं स्थितं त्रिधा । ऋषयो गीर्भिरर्चंति व्यंजितं नामभिःस्त्रिभिः ॥ (bhavadbhūtasya bhavyasya jaṃgamasthāvarasya ca | asyeke sūramevaikaṃ prabhavaṃ pralayaṃ viduḥ ‖ etadbhūteṣu lokeṣu agnibhūtaṃ sthitaṃ tridhā | ṛṣayo gīrbhirarcaṃti vyaṃjitaṃ nāmabhiḥstribhiḥ ‖) (Bṛ. De. 1-61; 1-64) NOTE In these verses, in describing Agni's greatness, the authors of the Bṛhaddevatā say that Prajāpati, the womb of all beings, has obtained his existence in three stations, in three ways, in the form of Agni, as the source of creation and dissolution for all moving and unmoving beings in past, future and present.

p. 166

Continuing the praise of this same Agni, they say that the seers have spoken of this threefold manifestation of Agni by three names, as seen below: त्रिस्थानं चैनमर्चंति होत्रायां वृक्तबर्हिषः । इहैव पवमानोऽग्निर्मध्यमोऽग्निर्वनस्पतिः ॥ अमुष्मिन्नेव विप्रैस्तु लोकेऽग्निशुचिरुच्यते ॥ इहाग्निभूतस्त्वृषिभिर्लोके स्तुतिभिरीळितः ॥ जातवेदाः स्तुतो मध्यॆ स्तुतो वैश्वानरो दिवि ॥ (tristhānaṃ cainamarcaṃti hotrāyāṃ vṛktabarhiṣaḥ | ihaiva pavamāno 'gnirmadhyamo 'gnirvanaspatiḥ ‖ amuṣminneva vipraistu loke 'gniśucirucyate ‖ ihāgnibhūtastvṛṣibhirloke stutibhirīḷitaḥ ‖ jātavedāḥ stuto madhyè stuto vaiśvānaro divi ‖) (Bṛ. De. 1-65 to 67) Of these three, the Agni who manifests on the earth is known as Pavamāna Agni, the Agni of the middle world as Vanaspati, and the Agni of the heavenly world as Śuci. This same distinction is set out in all the Saṃhitās by the verse दिवस्परि प्रथमं जज्ञे अग्निरस्मद्वितीयं परि जातवेदाः । तृतीयमप्पु नृमणा अजस्रमिंधान एनं जरते स्वाधीः ॥ (divaspari prathamaṃ jajñe agnirasmadvitīyaṃ pari jātavedāḥ | tṛtīyamappu nṛmaṇā ajasramiṃdhāna enaṃ jarate svādhīḥ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-45-1; Vā. Saṃ. 12-18; Tai. Saṃ. 1-3-14-5). पृक्षः (pṛkṣaḥ)—the word पृक्ष (pṛkṣa) is read among the names of food (Ni. 3-9). Here अन्न साधकः पाकादिना (anna sādhakaḥ pākādinā) means: one who nourishes food by cooking and the like. पितुमान् (pitumān)—for this, हनिर्लक्षणान्नयुक्तः (hanirlakṣaṇānnayuktaḥ): the meaning is, possessed of food in the form of the oblation. सप्तशिवासु मातृषु (saptaśivāsu mātṛṣu)—सप्तलोकशिवकरीषु मातृस्थानीयासु हितकरीषु वृष्टिषु (saptalokaśivakarīṣu mātṛsthānīyāsu hitakarīṣu vṛṣṭiṣu): in the rains that do good to the seven worlds, that is, in the atmosphere, the place of the origin of rain; मध्यमस्थानो विद्युद्रूपो ना वर्तते (madhyamasthāno vidyudrūpo nā vartate): the meaning is that he is in the form of lightning. दशप्रमतिं (daśapramatiṃ)—दशसु दिक्कु प्रकृष्टमननवंतं पूज्यत्वाय (daśasu dikku prakṛṣṭamananavaṃtaṃ pūjyatvāya): one meaning is, one who is worshipful in the ten quarters and an object of meditation. Or else मंथनकाले दशभिरंगुलीभिरुत्पन्नं लोकत्रये दशदिक्षु च व्याप्तं (maṃthanakāle daśabhiraṃgulībhirutpannaṃ lokatraye daśadikṣu ca vyāptaṃ): at the time of churning, one produced with the help of the ten fingers and spread to the ten quarters — this is another possible meaning. For both kinds of meaning there are Vedic authorities. The description of Agni's origin, that the atmosphere, his original place, and the earth together caused the subtle Agni to manifest, is given in

p. 167

यं त्वा द्यावापृथिवी यं त्वापस्त्वष्ट्वा यं त्वा सुजनिमा जजान । पंथामनु प्रविद्वान्तित्रयाणं द्युमदग्ने समिधानो वि भाहि । (yaṃ tvā dyāvāpṛthivī yaṃ tvāpastvaṣṭvā yaṃ tvā sujanimā jajāna | paṃthāmanu pravidvāntitrayāṇaṃ dyumadagne samidhāno vi bhāhi |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-2-7) and similar passages, which explain that heaven and earth, comprising the ten quarters, are the source of Agni's origin. Moreover, in Ṛks such as द्विरं पंच जीजनन्तंवसानाः स्वसारो अग्निं मानुषीषु विक्षु । उषर्बुधमथर्यो ३न दंतं शुक्रं स्वासं परशुं न तिग्मं ॥ (dviraṃ paṃca jījanantaṃvasānāḥ svasāro agniṃ mānuṣīṣu vikṣu | uṣarbudhamatharyo 3na daṃtaṃ śukraṃ svāsaṃ paraśuṃ na tigmaṃ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-6-8) the manner of the origin of the earthly fire is described: the ten fingers of the two hands created Agni. Therefore in this context the word दश (daśa) may be taken to mean either the ten quarters that encompass earth and atmosphere, or the ten fingers engaged in the work of churning. योषणः (yoṣaṇaḥ)—मिश्रणशीलाः सर्वा दिशः (miśraṇaśīlāḥ sarvā diśaḥ): one meaning is, all the united regions of space; or else एकस्मिन् पाणौ संहृत्य अवस्थिताः (ekasmin pāṇau saṃhṛtya avasthitāḥ): the other meaning is, the ten fingers that are gathered together in one hand and stand in one place. वृषभस्य दोहसे (vṛṣabhasya dohase)—Since the lightning-fire has the power of pouring rain, the epithet वृषभ (vṛṣabha) (bull) is applied to him. The derivation and special sense of this word have been given earlier. Sāyaṇa explains the word दोहसे (dohase) thus: आदित्यरश्मयः घर्मकाले भूमिस्थमुदकमाकृष्य सूरं प्रापय्य तत्र चिरकालं धृत्वा पुनरंतरिक्षं प्राप्य मेघेषु स्थित्वा वर्ष काले प्रवर्षंतीति प्रसिद्धं । अतो रश्मेर्दोर्गृत्वं । (ādityaraśmayaḥ gharmakāle bhūmisthamudakamākṛṣya sūraṃ prāpayya tatra cirakālaṃ dhṛtvā punaraṃtarikṣaṃ prāpya megheṣu sthitvā varṣa kāle pravarṣaṃtīti prasiddhaṃ | ato raśmerdorgṛtvaṃ |). That is, in summer the rays of the sun attract the water on the earth and bring it to the sun, keep it there for some time, then make it enter the clouds in the atmosphere, and pour down rain in the rainy season. Therefore the word दोहसे (dohase) shows that the solar ray is the one that is milked.

Grammar
  • शये — शीज् स्वप्ने धातुः । लट् प्रथमपुरुष एकवचने त प्रत्ययः । टेः एत्वम् । लोपस्त आत्मनेपदेषु (पा. सू- ७-१-४१) इति तकारस्य लोपः । अदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शपः इति शपो लुक् । शीजः सार्वधातुकेगुणः (पा. सू. ७-४-२१) इति गुणः । अचि परे अयादेशः । अतिजंतात् परत्वान्निघातस्वरो भवति ।
  • पृक्षः — पृची संपर्के धातुः । असुन् प्रत्ययः सुडागमः । चोःकुः इति कुत्वम् । सकारस्य षत्वम् । व्यत्ययेन अंतोदात्तस्वरो भवति ।

p. 168

  • पितुमान् — ह्रस्वात् परत्वान्मतुप् प्रत्ययः । ह्रस्वनुड्भ्यां मतुप् (पा. सू. ६-१-१७६) इति तस्य उदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
  • नित्यः — त्यप् नेध्रुव इति व्यक्तव्यम् इति नि इत्यव्ययात् त्यप् प्रत्ययः । पित्तात् अयमनुदात्तो भवति ।
  • द्वितीयम् — द्वेस्तीयः (पा. सू ५-२-५४) इति तीय प्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्य आद्युदात्तस्वरेण ईकार उदात्तो भवति ।
  • तृतीयम् — त्रयसंप्रसारणं च इति त्रिशब्दात् तीय प्रत्यये संप्रसारणं विशेषेण भवति । इग्गणः संप्रसारणम् इति रेफस्य ऋकाररूपं संप्रसारणम् । पूर्ववत् स्वरो भवति ।
  • दोहसे — दुह प्रपूरणे धातुः । सर्वधातुभ्य असुन् इति कर्तरि असुन् प्रत्ययः । पुगंतलघूपधस्य च सूत्रेण प्रत्ययनिमित्तं गुणः । चतुर्थ्येकवचनांतरूपम् ।
  • जनयंत — जनी प्रादुर्भावे धातुः । हेतुमतिच (पा सू ३-१-२६) इति प्रयोजकव्यापारे णिच् । उपधावृद्धौ प्राप्तायां जनीज्यष्क्नसुरंजॊ— इति उपधाह्रस्वः । छंदसि लुज्लज्लिटः (पा. सू. ३-४-६) इति वर्तमानार्थे लज् । प्रथमपुरुषबहुवचनांतरूपम् । बहुलं छंदस्यमाज्जयोगेऽपि इति अडागमो न भवति । अतिजंतात् परत्वान्निघातस्वरो भवति । NOTE

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

ईमेनमग्निं यद्यस्मात्कारणान्महिषस्य । महन्नामैतत् । महिषोऽभ्य ऋभुक्षा इति तन्नामसु पाठात् । महतो यज्ञस्य बुधान्मूलादाधानादारभ्य वर्पसः । रूपनामैतत् । रूपस्योपक्रमोपसंहारात्मकस्य सिद्धय ईशानासः स्वकीयव्यापारसमर्थाः सूरयो मेधाविन ऋत्विजः शवसा बलेन मंत्रादिरूपेण शारीरेण वा निष्क्रंत निष्कर्वंति साधयंति उत्पादयंति काष्ठात् । यद्वा । एनमग्निं बुधनादादितो मथनादारभ्य महिषस्य वर्पसो महतो रूपस्याहुतिस्वीकारसमर्थस्य सिद्धये निष्कर्वंति ॥ करोतेश्चांदसे लुजि मंत्रे घसेति चेर्लुक् । व्यत्ययेनांतादेशः ॥ किंच यदीमेनमेवाग्निं प्रदिवः पुराणात् । अनादिकालमारभ्य न केवलमिदानीमेवेत्यर्थः । पूर्ववदिदानीं मध्यो मधुनो मधुसदृशस्याधव आधवने प्रक्षेपे निमित्ते सति गुहा संतं गुहायां वेद्यां काष्टेषु निगूढं संतं मातरिश्वांतरिक्षे चेष्टमानो वायुरनुक्रमेण मथायति चालयति । उद्योधयतीत्यर्थः । यद्वा । मातरि फलस्य मातरि यागे श्वासिति चेष्टत इति मातरिश्वा यजमनो गुहा संतमरण्योर्निगूढं संतं प्रादुर्भानायानुक्रमेण मथायति मथ्णाति । उत्पादयतीत्यर्थः। यस्मादेवंरूपस्तत्सोतव्य इत्यर्थः ॥

NOTE

(काष्ठदिंद) उत्पन्नवागुवंतॆ माडिदरो [ (अथवा) बुध्नात्-अरणिगळ मथनकालदिंदारंभिसि

Gist of the bhāṣya

ईं (īṃ) is this Agni; यत् (yat) means "for which reason". महिषस्य (mahiṣasya): महत् (mahat) is a name; since in the list of its names there is the reading महिषोऽभ्य ऋभुक्षा (mahiṣo 'bhya ṛbhukṣā), the word means "of the great sacrifice". बुध्नात् (budhnāt): from the root, that is, beginning from the setting up of the fire. वर्पसः (varpasaḥ): this is a name for form; the form consisting of the beginning and the conclusion. For its accomplishment, ईशानासः (īśānāsaḥ), those capable in their own functions, सूरयः (sūrayaḥ), the wise priests, शवसा (śavasā), by strength, in the form of mantra and the like or bodily, निष्क्रंत (niṣkraṃta), accomplish, produce, from the wood. Or else: this Agni, from बुध्न (budhna), from the beginning of the churning, for the accomplishment of the great form of the great one that is able to accept the oblation, they produce. He adds: yadīm, this very Agni, from प्रदिवः (pradivaḥ), from of old, from beginningless time, not only now, as before, now, मध्वः (madhvaḥ), of the honey-like, when the pouring in, आधवे (ādhave), is the occasion, being गुहा (guhā), in the hollow, in the altar, hidden in the pieces of wood, मातरिश्वा (mātariśvā), the wind that moves in the atmosphere, in due order मथायति (mathāyati), moves, that is, wakes him up. Or else: मातरिश्वा (mātariśvā) is the sacrificer, who strives in the mother of the fruit, that is, in the sacrifice. He churns in due order the Agni hidden in the two kindling sticks, for his manifestation; that is, he produces him. Because he is of such a form, he is to be praised.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • ईं (īṃ)—this Agni
  • यत् (yat)—for which reason
  • महिषस्य (mahiṣasya)—of the great sacrifice
  • बुध्नात् (budhnāt)—beginning from the time of setting up the fire
  • वर्पसः (varpasaḥ)—for the accomplishment of the form (consisting of beginning and conclusion)
  • ईशानासः (īśānāsaḥ)—capable in carrying out their own duties
  • सूरयः (sūrayaḥ)—the wise priests
  • शवसा (śavasā)—by strength in the form of mantra, or by bodily strength
  • निःक्रंत (niḥkraṃta)—caused to be produced (from the wood); [or: बुध्नात् (budhnāt), beginning from the time of churning the kindling sticks, महिषस्य वर्पसः (mahiṣasya varpasaḥ), for obtaining the extended form (fit for accepting the oblation), निः क्रंत (niḥ kraṃta), caused to be produced from the wood] (and)
  • गुहा संतं यदीं (guhā saṃtaṃ yadīṃ)—which this Agni, lying hidden in the wood
  • प्रदिवः (pradivaḥ)—from beginningless time (as being

p. 170

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • प्रदिवः (pradivaḥ)—(continued) as from time without beginning, so also now
  • मध्वः (madhvaḥ)—sweet like honey
  • आधवे (ādhave)—for the sake of placing the oblation (for offering it)
  • मातरिश्वा (mātariśvā)—the wind that moves in the atmosphere
  • मथायति (mathāyati)—as he blows and makes (him) blaze up. [Or: मातरिश्वा (mātariśvā)—the sacrificer, the performer of the sacrifice; मथायति (mathāyati)—as he causes (him) to be produced (from the wood); therefore this Agni is worthy of praise.]
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

From the time of the installation of the fire in the great sacrifice onward, in order that Agni may take on a form fit to receive the oblation and extended, the priests, who are capable in the discharge of their own duties and are wise, caused this Agni to be produced from wood by the power of their mantras and also by the strength of their bodies. And this Agni, lying hidden in the wood, is, as from time without beginning so now also, blown upon well and made to blaze up by the wind that moves in the atmosphere, in order that the honey-sweet oblation may be offered. Therefore this Agni is worthy of praise.

Printed English

As powerful priests extract by the force (of prayer), this Agni from his primitive seat, (for the evolvement) of his mighty form ; as the wind arouses him lurking in the hiding-place ( of the altar ), for the sake of offering oblations now as of old:

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

महिषस्य (mahiṣasya)—The word महिष (mahiṣa) is read among the names meaning "great" (Ni. 3-13). The author of the Nirukta, citing the Ṛk अपामुपस्थे महिषा अगृज्ञत विशो राजानमुप तस्थुर्यग्नियं । आ दूतो अग्निमभरद्विवस्वतो वैश्वानरं मातरिश्वा परावतः ॥ (apāmupasthe mahiṣā agṛjñata viśo rājānamupa tasthuryagniyaṃ | ā dūto agnimabharadvivasvato vaiśvānaraṃ mātariśvā parāvataḥ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-8-4), shows for the word महिष (mahiṣa) occurring there the meaning महत्यंतरिक्षे (mahatyaṃtarikṣe) or महांतो मरुतः (mahāṃto marutaḥ), and indicates that the idea of the present Ṛk is also found in the cited Ṛk. In the present Ṛk the commentator has shown one construction by joining the word महिषस्य (mahiṣasya) with बुध्नात् (budhnāt), and another kind of construction by joining it with वर्पसः (varpasaḥ). According to the first construction, महिषस्य बुध्नात् (mahiṣasya budhnāt) means "from the time of the installation of the fire in the great sacrifice"; according to the second, महिषस्य वर्षसः (mahiṣasya varṣasaḥ) means "of the extended form". NOTE ### Printed p. 171 To understand the explanation of this situation, the meaning of the word बुध्नात् (budhnāt) must be understood correctly. For the word बुध्नात् (budhnāt) the meaning "from the root, from the installation onward" has been given. In the Ṛk-Saṃhitā the word बुध्न (budhna) is used mostly as a synonym of the atmosphere. But even where it gives the meaning "atmosphere", it is because it holds and keeps the waters fixed, that is, because it is the support of the waters, that the atmosphere is called बुध्न (budhna) (Ni. 10-44). In the Ṛk इंद्राय गिरो अनिशितसर्गा अपः प्रेरयं सगरस्य बुध्नात् । यो अक्षेणेव चक्रिया शचीभिर्विष्वक्तस्तंभ पृथिवीमुत द्यां । (iṃdrāya giro aniśitasargā apaḥ prerayaṃ sagarasya budhnāt | yo akṣeṇeva cakriyā śacībhirviṣvaktastaṃbha pṛthivīmuta dyāṃ |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-89-4), सगरस्य बुध्नात् (sagarasya budhnāt) means "that which is the support of the atmosphere"; the meaning is the deep, root region of the atmosphere. The same meaning is to be taken in the present Ṛk also. Then the deep root of the sacrifice is either the time of the installation of the fire or the time of the churning of the araṇis. The purport is that from such an initial time the wise ones strove and made Agni to be produced and to be favourable to the sacrifice. ईशानासः (īśānāsaḥ)—capable in their own work; the meaning is capable in the discharge of their own duties. The word ईशान (īśāna) means lord, master. . अर्वद्भिरग्ने अर्वतो नृभिन्न र्न्नीर्वैर्विरान्वनुयामा त्वोताः । ईशानासः पितृवित्तस्य रायो वि सूरयः शतहिमा नो अश्वः । (. arvadbhiragne arvato nṛbhinna rnnīrvairvirānvanuyāmā tvotāḥ | īśānāsaḥ pitṛvittasya rāyo vi sūrayaḥ śatahimā no aśvaḥ |) NOTE (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-73-9) ईशानमस्य जगतः स्वर्दृशं । (īśānamasya jagataḥ svardṛśaṃ |) (Ai. Brā. 17-10) ईशानं भूतभव्यस्य । (īśānaṃ bhūtabhavyasya |) (Ka. U. 4-5) Just as in all such sentences the meaning is "lord", here too the sacrificer becomes the lord of his own works. Since ईशानासः सूरयः (īśānāsaḥ sūrayaḥ) is said, the purport is that the wise priests, performing their duty without omission, become lords of the fruit also. In the manner in which such wise ones cause the earthly Agni to be produced, Mātariśvan too makes the Agni that lay hidden blaze up; this is said by मातरिश्वा मथायति (mātariśvā mathāyati). The supernatural manifestation of Agni, who is the very self of the sacrifice, and his worldly production are described in many ways. ### Printed p. 172 That the manifestation of Agni, the father of the sacrifice, took place first in the form of lightning for the wind, is shown in the Ṛk-Saṃhitā in the Ṛk NOTE त्वमग्ने प्रथमो मातरिश्वन आविर्भव सुकृतूया विवस्वते । अरेजेतां रोदसी होतृपूर्येऽसघ्नोर्भारमयजो महो वसो । (tvamagne prathamo mātariśvana āvirbhava sukṛtūyā vivasvate | arejetāṃ rodasī hotṛpūrye 'saghnorbhāramayajo maho vaso |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-31-3) and in other such Ṛks: as said there, Mātariśvan, for the benefit of the sacrificers Bhṛgu and Manu, brought to the earth the Agni that was hidden in a distant region, and did good to all creatures on earth; this matter has been explained in detail earlier. In the present Ṛk also, the same point is stated by the qualifier गुहा संतं (guhā saṃtaṃ). Here, for the word मातरिश्वा (mātariśvā), besides the meaning अंतरिक्षे चेष्टमानो वायुः (aṃtarikṣe ceṣṭamāno vāyuḥ), a second meaning is given: मातरि फलस्य मातरि यागॆ श्वसिति चेष्टते इति मातरिश्वा यजमानो गुहा संतं अरण्योर्निगूढं संतं मथायति । (mātari phalasya mātari yāgè śvasiti ceṣṭate iti mātariśvā yajamāno guhā saṃtaṃ araṇyornigūḍhaṃ saṃtaṃ mathāyati |) — since the sacrificer acts in the sacrifice, which produces every kind of fruit, he is called Mātariśvan, and he, with effort, blows upon and makes blaze up the Agni that lies hidden in the araṇis. प्रदिवः (pradivaḥ)—The word प्रदिव (pradiva) is read among the names meaning "ancient" (Ni. 3-19). The author of the Nirukta, citing the Ṛk मरुत्वा इंद्र वृषभो रणाय पिबा सोममनुष्पधं मदाय । आ सिंचस्व जठरे मध्व ऊर्मिं त्वं राजासि प्रदिवः सुतानां । (marutvā iṃdra vṛṣabho raṇāya pibā somamanuṣpadhaṃ madāya | ā siṃcasva jaṭhare madhva ūrmiṃ tvaṃ rājāsi pradivaḥ sutānāṃ |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-47-1) (Ni. 4-8), gives for the word प्रदिवः (pradivaḥ) there the meaning पूर्वेष्टपृहस्सु (pūrveṣṭapṛhassu), "as (pressed) on former days". NOTE In the present Ṛk too the purport is: just as the oblation has been offered from time without beginning, so now also, in order to offer it in the same way.

Grammar
  • बुधात्—बध बंधने धातुः । बंधे ब्रधिबुधीच ( उ. सू. २-२८५) इति नक् प्रत्ययः । धातोः बुधि आदेशः । प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तः । सप्तमीएकवचनांतरप NOTE
  • महिषस्य—महधातुः । अविमह्योष्टिषच् (उ. सू. १-४५) इति टिषच् प्रत्ययः । चितः (पा. सू. ६-१-१९३) इति अंतोदात्तस्वरो भवति । षष्ठीएकवचनांतरूपम् ।
  • वर्पसः—वृज् संभक्तौ धातुः । वृज्‌शीज्‌भ्यांरूप स्वांगयोः पुट् च (उ.सू. ४-६४०) इति रूपार्थे असुन् प्रत्ययः । धातोः पुटागमः । प्रत्ययनिमित्तत्वेन धातोः इकः गुणः । नित्त्वात् आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति । ### Printed p. 173
  • ईशानासः—ईश ऐश्वर्ये धातुः । ताच्छील्यवयोवचनेषु चानश् (पा. सू. ३-२-१२९) इति चानत् प्रत्ययः । चितः (पा. सू. ६-१-१६३) इति अंतोदंतस्वरो भवति । जस् परे आज्जसेरसुक् इति तस्य असुकागमः ।
  • क्रंत—डुकृञ् करणे । छंदसि लुज् लज् लिटः (पा सू. ३-४-६) इति वर्तमानार्थे लुज् । प्रथमपुरुषबहुवचने झा प्रत्ययः । जिलुजि इति ज्जीविकरणे आगते मंत्रेघसह्यर—(पा. सू. २-४-८०) इति जिळे लुक् । अनकारस्य परे झु आगते अपि व्यत्ययेन तस्य अंतादेशो भवति । प्रत्ययस्य जित्वात् गुणो न भवति । यणादेशः । बहुलं छंदस्यमाङ् योगेपि (पा सू. ६-४-२५) इति अडागमो न भवति । यद्योगत्वात् निघातस्वरो न भवति । प्रत्ययस्य आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति । NOTE
  • सूरयः—सूज् प्राणिप्रसवे धातुः । सूज्‌क्रिः इति क्ति प्रत्ययः । कित्त्वात् गुणो न भवति । प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तो भवति । प्रथमाबहुवचनांतरूपम् ।
  • प्रदिवः—प्रगता विवो दिवसा यस्मात् सः । गतिकारकोपपदात् कृत् इति कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति ।
  • गुहा—सप्तमीविभक्तौ परायां सुपां सुलुक् (पा सू. ७-१-३९) इति तस्य लुक् ।
  • संतम्—तस भुवि धातुः । लडर्थे शतृप्रत्ययः । अदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शपः इति शपि लुक् । श्नसोरल्लोपः (पा. सू. ६-४-१११) इति धातोः अकारस्य लोपः । प्रत्ययस्य आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति । द्वितीयाविकवचने नुमागमः ।
  • मातरिश्वा—मातरि स्वयतीति मातरिश्वा । श्वन्दुक्सन् (उ. सू. १-१५६) इति कनि प्रत्ययांतः निपातितः । प्रत्ययस्य आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
  • मथायति—मंथ विलोडने धातुः लट् प्रथमपुरुष एकवचने तिप् प्रत्ययः । छंदसि शायजपि (पा. सू. ३-९-८४) इति त्वाविकरणस्य शायचादेशः । सार्वधातुकमपित् इति तस्य जित्वात् अनिदितां हल—सूत्रेण धातोः उपधा नकारस्य लोपः । यद्योगत्वात् निघातप्रतिषेधो भवति । शायच् चित्त्वात् अंतोदात्तस्वरो भवति ।

p. 174

Ṛk 4

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

प्र यत्पि॒तुः प॑र॒मान्नी॒यते॒ पर्या पृ॒क्षुधो॑ वी॒रुधो॒ दंसु॑ रोहति ।
उ॒भा यद॑स्य ज॒नुषं॒ यदिन्व॑त॒ आदिद्यवि॑ष्टो अभनद्घृ॒णा ॑ शुचिः ॥ ४ ॥

pra yatpituḥ paramānnīyate paryā pṛkṣudho vīrudho daṃsu rohati | ubhā yadasya januṣaṃ yadinvata ādidyaviṣṭo abhanadghṛṇā śuciḥ ‖ 4 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

प्र । यत् । पितुः । परमात् । नीयते । परि । आ । पृक्षुधः । वीरुधः । दंऽसु । रोहति ।
उभा । यत् । अस्य । जनुषं । यत् । इन्वतः । आत् । इत् । यविष्ठः । अभवत् ।
फृणा । शुचिः ॥ ४ ॥

pra | yat | pituḥ | paramāt | nīyate | pari | ā | pṛkṣudhaḥ | vīrudhaḥ | daṃ 'su | rohati | ubhā | yat | asya | januṣaṃ | yat | invataḥ | āt | it | yaviṣṭhaḥ | abhavat | phṛṇā | śuciḥ ‖ 4 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

यद्यस्मात्पुरन्नस्य पशुलक्षणस्य ॥ षष्ठीस्थाने प्रथमा ॥ तस्य परमात् परमत्वाद्धेतोः । उत्कृष्टत्वायेत्कर्थः । तदर्थं प्र परि णीयते प्रकर्षण हरितो नीयते । पर्यग्निक्रियत इत्यर्थः । यद्वा । पितुरुत्पादकात्परमादुत्कृष्टाद्दार्हपत्यलक्षणस्याग्नेः सकाशादाहवनीयं प्रति प्र परि णीयते प्रकर्षण नीयते । पर्यनर्थकः । किंच पृक्षुधः पशुपुरोडाशादिषु दाहमध्यॆ धीयमानाः । यद्वा॥ प्रशब्दस्य संप्रसारणं । क्षुध बुभुक्षायां । क्विप् ॥ प्रक्षोध्याः प्रकर्षण बुभुक्षिता भोक्तुमिष्यमाणाः । वीरुधो दंसु वंतेषु मध्य आ रोहति । आरोहंति । प्रविशंतीत्यर्थः । यद्यस्मादुभोभावध्वर्युयजमान् उभे अरणी वास्याग्नेर्जनुषं जन्मोत्पत्तिमिन्वतः व्याप्तुतः । स्वीकुरुत इत्यर्थः ॥ इवि व्याप्तौ । इदित्तान्नुम् ॥ आदिदत एव कारणाच्छुचिः शुद्धोऽयमग्निर्घृणा यजमानेष्पनुग्रहेण । यद्वा । फृणा फृणो दीप्तिमान् ॥ मत्वर्थो लुप्यते ॥ दीप्ता वा यविष्टो युवतमोऽभवत् । संपन्नः । स्वीकारसमर्थोऽभवदित्यर्थः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

यत् (yat) means "because". पितुः (pituḥ) is the animal-form food, the nominative standing in the place of the genitive. Because that food is परम (parama), supreme, for the sake of its excellence प्र परि णीयते (pra pari ṇīyate): it is led forward around, that is, the fire is carried round it (the rite of carrying the fire round the animal). NOTE Or else: from the supreme, excellent Gārhapatya fire, the "father", the producer, प्र परि णीयते (pra pari ṇīyate), he is carried forward to the Āhavanīya; परि (pari) is without meaning. Further, पृक्षुधः (pṛkṣudhaḥ) are (the branches) placed in the midst of the burning in the animal, the purodāśa and other offerings. Or else, by contraction of प्र (pra) (sampraṣāraṇa), from the root क्षुध (kṣudha) in the sense of desire to eat, with kvip: "those greatly hungry", wishing to eat. वीरुधो (vīrudho) (the plants) दंसु (daṃsu) — in the midst of the teeth (the flames) आ रोहति (ā rohati) ascend, that is, enter. NOTE Since both, the adhvaryu and the sacrificer, or the two araṇis, इन्वतः (invataḥ) (root इवि (ivi) in the sense of pervading) pervade, that is, accept, the birth, the origin, of this Agni, for that very reason this Agni is pure, घृणा (ghṛṇā) through favour towards the sacrificers; or else फृणा (phṛṇā) means "radiant", the possessive suffix being dropped; यविष्टो (yaviṣṭo) means "most youthful", अभवत् (abhavat): he became accomplished, capable of acceptance.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • यत् (yat)—for which reason
  • पितुः (pituḥ)—the food in the form of an animal
  • परमात् (paramāt)—because of its being excellent
  • प्र परि नीयते (pra pari nīyate)—(this Agni) is carried round in circumambulation. Or else [परमात् (paramāt)—from the excellent one; पितुः (pituḥ)—from the original one, the Gārhapatya fire; प्र परि नीयते (pra pari nīyate)—is carried far (to the neighbourhood of the Āhavanīya fire)] ### Printed p. 175
  • प्रक्षुधः (prakṣudhaḥ)—(in the animal, purodāśa and so on) those that rise up in the manner of burning, or those that are eager to consume the oblations NOTE
  • वीरुधः (vīrudhaḥ)—the branches that spread (upward) in the form of creepers
  • दंसु (daṃsu)—amidst the flames that are like teeth
  • आरोहंति (ārohaṃti)—ascend upward
  • यत् (yat)—for which reason
