ईळितः सर्वैः स्तुत्यः इळ् नामकः त्वं (īḷitaḥ sarvaiḥ stutyaḥ iḷ nāmakaḥ tvaṃ) — it is explained as Agni, who is praised by all and famed by the name Iḷa. ईळॆ ईट्टेः स्तुतिकर्मणः ; इंथते र्वा (īḷè īṭṭeḥ stutikarmaṇaḥ ; iṃthate rvā): it may be formed either from the root īḍ, meaning praise, or from the root indh, meaning to blaze. (Ni. 8-8). Having shown this derivation of the word, the Nirukta-writers quote Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-3 and explain the right meaning of the word.NOTE

First, like the word samidh, this word too seems to have no separate indication as a deity, but to be used only as an epithet of Agni. Since Agni's help and support must be complete at the time of performing the sacrifice, he is by nature worthy of praise. At the beginning Agni must be (1) kindled. Afterwards, (2) under the name Tanūnapāt or Narāśaṃsa, he must make the oblations of the sacrifice full of honey. Then he must bring the gods to the sacrifice. For this work he must indeed be worthy of praise (īḍya). Therefore in this setting he is (3) īḷita, "prayed to", by the sacrificers.

In the Āprī hymns this word, derived from the root īḍ, is used of Agni in nine places in all: in eight as an epithet meaning "one who is praised" or "worthy of praise", and in one as an epithet showing Agni's function as messenger. And in the Āprī verse composed by Viśvāmitra, प्र दीधितिर्विश्ववारा जिगाति होतारमिळः प्रथमं यजध्यै । (pra dīdhitirviśvavārā jigāti hotāramiḷaḥ prathamaṃ yajadhyai |) अच्छा नमोभिर्वृषभं वंदध्यै स देवान्यक्षदिषितो यजीयान् । (acchā namobhirvṛṣabhaṃ vaṃdadhyai sa devānyakṣadiṣito yajīyān |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-4-2) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-4-3) only here does it mean food in the form of oblation. Even so, it is related to Agni, the chief deity of that verse. This meaning differs from the tradition of the Āprī hymn. But in the Praiṣa hymn it is only a synonym of Agni.

p. 243

होतायक्षदग्निमिड ईडितो देवो देवाग्ं आवक्षद्दूतो हव्यनाडमूरः । उपेमं यज्ञमुपेमां देवो देवहूतिमवतु नेत्वाज्यस्य होतरज । (hotāyakṣadagnimiḍa īḍito devo devāgṃ āvakṣaddūto havyanāḍamūraḥ | upemaṃ yajñamupemāṃ devo devahūtimavatu netvājyasya hotaraja |) (Tai. Brā. 3-6-2-1) On this passage the commentator says इडेत्येतन्नामकमग्निं तृतीयप्रयाजदेवं (iḍetyetannāmakamagniṃ tṛtīyaprayājadevaṃ), thus giving it as a synonym of Agni. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa: इळो यजत्यन्नं वा इळोऽन्नमेव तत्प्रीणात्यन्नं यजमाने दधाति । (iḷo yajatyannaṃ vā iḷo 'nnameva tatprīṇātyannaṃ yajamāne dadhāti |) (Ai. Brā. 2-4) It says that iḷa is the food in the form of oblation to be offered in the sacrifice, and that as a result of offering this food the sacrificer too obtains food.

As explained above, the connection that Yāska shows between this word and the root indh is not clearly understood. Here Yāska does not state Kātkaśya's view. In the Bṛhaddevatā: इळस्त्वषिकृतं रूपं ईडेश्व स्तुतिकर्मणः । इळावांस्तेन वोक्तोग्निरिडिना वृद्धिकर्मणा ॥ (iḷastvaṣikṛtaṃ rūpaṃ īḍeśva stutikarmaṇaḥ | iḷāvāṃstena voktogniriḍinā vṛddhikarmaṇā ‖) (Bṛ. De. 3-4) By these sentences it is shown that this word is of the seers (ārṣeya) and a synonym of Agni, and that the word ilāvān is an epithet of Agni.NOTE गोमा अग्नेऽविमा आश्वी यज्ञो नृवत्सखा सदमिदप्रमृष्यः । इळाना एषो असुर प्रजावान्दीर्घो रयिः पृथुबुध्नः सभावान् । (gomā agne 'vimā āśvī yajño nṛvatsakhā sadamidapramṛṣyaḥ | iḷānā eṣo asura prajāvāndīrgho rayiḥ pṛthubudhnaḥ sabhāvān |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-2-5) In this verse the word इळार्वा (iḷārvā) is an epithet of Agni, so the Bṛhaddevatā points out that item.NOTE

Although such differences of tradition appear in the explanations, it can be said on the whole that it is a synonym of the deity Agni, holding the fourth place in the Āprī hymn.

मतिः—मनसाधना स्तुतिरूपा नाक् (matiḥ—manasādhanā stutirūpā nāk) — it means speech that is meditative and in the form of praise.

Grammar
  • ईळितः — ईड स्तुत् धातुः । कर्मणि निष्ठा इति क्त प्रत्ययः । अर्धधातुकस्लेड्वलाडेः इति इडागमः । प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तो भवति ।

p. 244

Grammar
  • वह — वह प्रापणे धातुः । लोट् मध्यमपुरुषैकवचने वह इति रूपं भवति । अतिजंतस्य परत्वात् निघातस्वरो भवति ।
  • चित्रं — चिञ् चयने धातुः । अमिचिमिदिशसिभ्यः क्रः (उ. सू. ४-६०३) इति क्र प्रत्ययः । कित्त्वात् गुणनिषेधो भवति । प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तो भवति ।
  • मतिः — मनु अवबोधने धातुः । स्त्रियां क्तिन् (पा. सू. ३-३-९४) इति क्तिन् प्रत्ययः । मंत्रेवृषेषपचमन-(पा.सू. ३-३-९६) इति क्तिन् उदात्तो भवति ।
  • अच्छा — निपातस्य च (पा. सू. ६-३-१३९) इति संहितायां दीर्घो भवति ।
  • सुजिह्व — शोभनाः जिह्वाः यस्य सः सुजिह्वः । गोस्त्रियोरुपसर्जनस्य इति समासे ह्रस्वो भवति । संबुद्धौ अमंत्रितस्य च (पा. सू. ८-१-१९) इति निघातस्वरो भवति ।
  • हि — पादपूरणे चवैतुहि इति अत्र हि इति पादपूरणे आगतः ।
  • वच्यते — वच परिभाषणे धातुः । कर्मणि लट् प्रथमपुरुषैकवचने त प्रत्ययः । टेः एत्वं । सार्वधातुके यक् (पा. सू. ३-१-६७) इति यक् । संप्रसारणे प्राप्ते वा छंदसि इति संप्रसारणं न भवति । हि इत्यस्य संबंधत्वात् हिच (पा. सू. ८-१-३४) इति निघातस्वरप्रतिषेधो भवति । अदुपदेशात् परस्मिन् लसार्वधातुकस्य आगतत्वात् तत् अनुदात्तं भवति तदा यक्स्वरः अवशिष्यते ।NOTE

Ṛk 5

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

स्त्र॒णा॒नासो॑ य॒तस्रु॑चो ब॒र्हिर्य॒ज्ञे स्व॑ध्व॒रे ।
वृं॒जे दे॒वव्य॑चस्तम॒मिंद्रा॑य॒ शर्म॑ स॒प्रथः॑ ॥ ५ ॥

straṇānāso yatasruco barhiryajñe svadhvare | vṛṃje devavyacastamamiṃdrāya śarma saprathaḥ ‖ 5 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

स्त्रणानासः । यतस्रुचः । बर्हिः । यज्ञे । सुअध्वरे ।
वृंजे । देवव्यचःतमं । इंद्राय । शर्म । सप्रथः ॥ ५ ॥

straṇānāsaḥ | yatasrucaḥ | barhiḥ | yajñe | suadhvare | vṛṃje | devavyacaḥtamaṃ | iṃdrāya | śarma | saprathaḥ ‖ 5 ‖

p. 245

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

स्वध्वरे शोभनप्रायणीयाद्यनांतरयागवति यज्ञे सोमयागे बर्हिर्दर्भान् स्तृणानास आस्तरंतो यतस्रुचो नियमितजुह्वादिपात्रा ऋत्विजो देवव्यचस्तममतिशयेन देवगामिनं सप्रथः सर्वतो विस्तीर्णं शर्म सुखसाधनं गृहमिंद्राय वृंजे । विवर्जयंति । संपादयंतीत्यर्थः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

In the well-conducted (su-adhvara) sacrifice, the Soma sacrifice, which has fine preparatory rites such as the prāyaṇīya and the rites that follow, the priests (ṛtvij) strew the barhis, the darbha grass, and hold ladles and other vessels in check (yatasruc). For Indra they वृंजे (vṛṃje), that is, set apart, meaning prepare, a dwelling (śarma), a means of comfort, that is most god-frequented (devavyacastama, most reaching to the gods) and spread out on every side (sapratha).

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • स्वध्वरे (svadhvare)—in this (sacrifice) accompanied by excellent, introductory rites such as the prāyaṇīya
  • यज्ञी (yajñī)—in this Soma sacrificeNOTE
  • बर्हिः (barhiḥ)—the seats of darbha
  • स्तृणानासः (stṛṇānāsaḥ)—strewing
  • यतस्रुचः (yatasrucaḥ)—the priests, who hold the ladles and other vessels for the sacrifice
  • देवव्यचस्तमं (devavyacastamaṃ)—that which, calling the gods, worships them exceedingly
  • सप्रथः (saprathaḥ)—that which is extended
  • शर्म (śarma)—that which is a means of comfort, the sacrificial house
  • इंद्राय (iṃdrāya)—for Indra
  • वृंजे (vṛṃje)—they prepare
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

In this Soma sacrifice, accompanied by excellent introductory rites such as the prāyaṇīya, the priests have strewn the darbha seats and hold the ladles and other vessels for the sacrifice. And for Indra they prepare the sacrificial house, which calls the gods and again and again worships them exceedingly, which is extended, and which is a means of comfort.

Printed English

The priests, bearing ladles, are strewing the sacred grass in this holy sacrifice, to prepare a god-frequented and well-spread abode for Indra.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

बर्हिः (barhiḥ)—This implement has a more concrete form than the notions of idhma and Iḷa. Barhis means simply a darbha seat. The doors are given a divine aspect (देवीः द्वारः (devīḥ dvāraḥ)), but nothing of the kind is done for barhis. Only the sense of a seat for the gods is suggested. Moreover, the doors are prayed to open of themselves, without other help, and make a way for the gods to come. Lifeless doors cannot open of themselves and make a wide path unless they have divine power; but for barhis there is no attribution of this power. The priests must spread it. Not only in this verse but in the other verses of the Āprī hymns too, it is stated clearly that the barhis is to be strewn only with the help of the priests and others. For example—

p. 246

प्राचीनं बर्हिरोजसा सहस्रवीरमस्तृणन् । यत्रादित्या विराजथ । (prācīnaṃ barhirojasā sahasravīramastṛṇan | yatrādityā virājatha |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-188-4) In this verse likewise, and in Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-5-4, बर्हिः प्राचीनमोजसा पवमानः स्तृणन् हरिः । (barhiḥ prācīnamojasā pavamānaḥ stṛṇan hariḥ |), there is the description that the priests strew the barhis. In the same way, in the verses of the other Āprī hymns too, the barhis is said to be an earthly and lifeless thing, yet a place that is a sacred seat for the gods. Only in the Praiṣa hymn: होता यक्षद्बर्हिः सुष्टरीनोर्णम्रदा अस्मिन्यज्ञे वि च प्र च प्रथताग्ं स्वासस्थं देवेभ्यः । एमेनदद्य वसवो रुद्रा आदित्याः सदंतु प्रियमिंद्रस्यास्तु वेत्वाज्यस्य होतरज ॥ (hotā yakṣadbarhiḥ suṣṭarīnorṇamradā asminyajñe vi ca pra ca prathatāgṃ svāsasthaṃ devebhyaḥ | emenadadya vasavo rudrā ādityāḥ sadaṃtu priyamiṃdrasyāstu vetvājyasya hotaraja ‖) (Tai. Brā. 3-6-2-1) with बर्हिर्नामकं चतुर्थप्रयाजदेवमग्निं (barhirnāmakaṃ caturthaprayājadevamagniṃ), it is said to be a seat that is a synonym of Agni and of divine nature. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa, बर्हिर्यजति, पशवो वै बर्हिः पशूनेव तत्प्रीणाति पशून्यजमाने दधाति । (barhiryajati, paśavo vai barhiḥ paśūneva tatprīṇāti paśūnyajamāne dadhāti |) (Ai. Brā. 2-4) it is explained as the animal that grazes on grass and is covered with grass. But it is seen that this meaning has not the slightest scope.NOTE

The Nirukta-writers say बर्हिः परिबर्हणात् (barhiḥ paribarhaṇāt): because it grows quickly, darbha is named barhis. (Ni. 8-8). In the Bṛhaddevatā, बर्हिरेवायमग्निस्तु सर्वं हि परिब्बंहितं । अन्नेन यद्भुतो ना सन्निध्मेन परिबृंहितः ॥ (barhirevāyamagnistu sarvaṃ hi paribbaṃhitaṃ | annena yadbhuto nā sannidhmena paribṛṃhitaḥ ‖) (Bṛ. De. 3-5) it states identity: since all food is pervaded by him, and since after the oblation he is filled with fuel, Agni himself is in the form of barhis.

Although in many matters the authors of the Bṛhaddevatā follow the sentences of the Nirukta, in this context they show a slight difference: what the Nirukta-writers call barhis, simply a seat for the gods, they explain as a seat of divine nature and a synonym of Agni.

स्तृणानासः (stṛṇānāsaḥ) Printed स्प्राणासरि (sprāṇāsari)—आस्तरंत (āstaraṃta): those who strew.NOTE सप्रथः (saprathaḥ)—सप्रथाः सर्वतः पृथुः (saprathāḥ sarvataḥ pṛthuḥ): it means spread out broadly all around, as the Nirukta-writers explain (Ni. 6-8).

p. 247

Grammar
  • स्त्रणानासः — स्त्र-ञ् अच्छादने इति धातुः । क्र्यादिः । लडर्थे शानच् प्रत्ययः । क्र्यादिभ्यः श्ना (पा. सू ३-१-८) इति श्ना विकरणम् । प्वादीनां ह्रस्वः (पा. सू. ७-३-८०) इति धातोर्ह्रस्वः । ह्रस्वऋकारस्य परत्वात् णत्वम् । प्रत्ययस्य चित्त्वादंतोदात्तो भवति । जस्परे आज्जसेरसुक् (पा. सू. ६-१-५०) इति तस्य असुक् आगमः । सकारस्य रुत्वविसर्गौ । NOTE
  • यतस्रुचः — यताः स्रुचः यैस्ते यतस्रुचः । बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या पूर्वपदम् (पा. सू. ६-२-१) इति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति । प्रथमाबहुवचनांतरूपम् ।
  • स्वध्वरे — शोभनः अध्वरः यस्मिन् सः स्वध्वरः । नञ्सुभ्याम् (पा. सू. ६-२-१७२) इति उत्तरपदस्य अंतोदात्तस्वरो भवति । सप्तमीएकवचनांतरूपम् ।
  • वृज्जि — वृजी वर्जने इति धातुः । अदादिः । इदित्त्वान्नुमागमः । लट् प्रथमपुरुषबहुवचने व्यत्ययेन बहुवचनस्थाने एकवचनं त प्रत्ययः । टेः एत्वम् । लोपस्त आत्मनेपदेषु (पा. सू. ७-१-४१) इति प्रत्ययतकारस्य लोपः । पादादित्वान्निघातस्वरो न भवति । प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तो भवति ।
  • सप्रथः — प्रथ प्रख्याने इति धातुः । सर्वधातुभ्य असुन् इति असुन् प्रत्ययः । प्रथसा सह वर्तत इति सप्रथः । तेन सहेति तुल्ययोगे (पा. सू. २-२-२८) इति समासः । वोपसर्जनस्य (पा. सू. ६-३-८२) इति सह इत्यस्य सभावः । गतिकारकोपपदात्‌कृत् (पा. सू. ६-२-१३९) इति कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति ।

p. 248

Ṛk 6

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

वि श्र॑यंतामृता॒वृधः॑ प्र॒यै दे॒वेभ्यो॑ म॒हीः ।
पा॒व॒कासः॑ पुरु॒स्पृहो॒ द्वारो॑ दे॒वीर॑स॒श्चतः॑ ॥ ६ ॥

vi śrayaṃtāmṛtāvṛdhaḥ prayai devebhyo mahīḥ | pāvakāsaḥ puruspṛho dvāro devīrasaścataḥ ‖ 6 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

वि । श्रयंतां । ऋतवृधः । प्रय्यै । देवेभ्यः । महीः ।
पावकासः । पुरुस्पृहः । द्वारः । देवीः । असश्चतः ॥ ६ ॥

vi | śrayaṃtāṃ | ṛtavṛdhaḥ | prayyai | devebhyaḥ | mahīḥ | pāvakāsaḥ | puruspṛhaḥ | dvāraḥ | devīḥ | asaścataḥ ‖ 6 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

द्वारो देवीर्यज्ञस्य द्वाराभिमानिन्नो देवता वि श्रयंतां । विविधं श्रयंतु । विवृता भवंतु । किमर्थ० । देवेभ्यः प्रयै प्रयातुं देवानां प्रापणाय ॥ प्रयै रोहिष्यॆ अव्यथिष्यॆ । पा. ३-४-१० । इति निपातितः ॥ कीदृश्यस्ताः । ऋतवृधो यज्ञस्य वर्धयित्र्यः पूज्याः महीर्महत्यः पावकास शोधयित्र्यः पुरुस्पृहो बहुस्वहणीयाः असश्च तोर्ऽसज्यमानाः परस्परविप्रकृष्टा इत्यर्थः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

The doors (द्वारो देवीः (dvāro devīḥ)), the deities who preside over the doors of the sacrifice, are to open out in various ways (वि श्रयंतां (vi śrayaṃtāṃ)), that is, to stand open. For what purpose? प्रयै (prayai) means "in order to go", that is, to bring the gods to the sacrifice; it is a form irregularly accepted. What are they like? They increase the sacrifice (ऋतवृधः (ṛtavṛdhaḥ)), they are worshipful, great (महीः (mahīḥ)), purifying (पावकासः (pāvakāsaḥ)), desired by many (पुरुस्पृहः (puruspṛhaḥ)), and असश्चतः (asaścataḥ), that is, not clinging to one another, standing far apart from each other.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • ऋतवृधः (ṛtavṛdhaḥ)—those who make the sacrifice grow
  • मही (mahī)—those of great form
  • पावकासः (pāvakāsaḥ)—those having the power of purifying
  • पुरुस्पृहः (puruspṛhaḥ)—those desired by many
  • असश्चतः (asaścataḥ)—those who stand apart, not clinging
  • द्वारोदेवी: (dvārodevī:)—the deities presiding over the doors (of the sacrificial house)
  • देवेभ्यः (devebhyaḥ)—for the gods
  • प्रयै (prayai)—for entering
  • विश्रयंतां (viśrayaṃtāṃ)—let them move apart, far away, and make a way
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the door-deities of the sacrificial house, who are the cause of the sacrifice's growth, of great form, having the power of purifying, desired by many, and standing apart without clinging to one another, move apart and far away and make a way for the gods to enter.

Printed English

Let the bright, separable doors, the augmenters of sacrificial, the purifiers of rites, the desired of many, be set open for the gods to enter.

p. 249

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

द्वारो देवीः (dvāro devīḥ)—Sāyaṇa explains this as the deities presiding over the doors of the sacrificial house. There is a difference of opinion whether these doors are really the doors of the sacrificial house or whether this is merely an ornamental usage. If the word does not mean house-doors here, then in the matter of the deities of the Āprī hymns too, points different from those just stated would have to be assumed. From the standpoint of ritual procedure, only two things, the barhis and the svāhākṛti, are without attribution of divinity; though merely earthly, they are described with qualities of supernatural purity because they are connected with the sacrifice. In तिस्रो देवीः (tisro devīḥ) all are called deities together, because Sarasvatī has a pure divine element and the other two rivers are mentioned along with that river. In the same way in दैवौ होतारौ (daivau hotārau) the earthly hotṛ is also meant as a deity, because he is with Agni, who is of divine nature. But in देवी द्वारः (devī dvāraḥ) there is no room for this. If these doors are the doors of the sacrificial house, the question arises why they should have a special place that the barhis and svāhākṛti do not have. If only some of the implements that are parts of the sacrifice are to be viewed as divine, then the most important of all, the altar (vedi), is not named at all.

Another point to be noticed here is that the word is in the plural, "doors". In the verse of an Āprī hymn, सप्त होत्राणि मनसा वृणाना इन्वंतो विश्वं प्रति यन्नृतेन । नृपेशसो विदथेषु प्र जाता अभीमं यज्ञं वि चरंत पूर्विः ॥ (sapta hotrāṇi manasā vṛṇānā invaṃto viśvaṃ prati yannṛtena | nṛpeśaso vidatheṣu pra jātā abhīmaṃ yajñaṃ vi caraṃta pūrviḥ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-4-5) the adjective पूर्विः (pūrviḥ) is also in the plural. And if we examine the duties of these door-deities: 1) "Open out, ye sacrifice-increasing divine doors, unclinging" (वि श्रयंतां ऋतावृधो द्वारो देवीरसश्वतः (vi śrayaṃtāṃ ṛtāvṛdho dvāro devīrasaśvataḥ)), meaning "take them apart for the convenience of the sacrificer", in the verse Ṛ. 1-13-6; 2) दुरो धृतान्यक्षरन् (duro dhṛtānyakṣaran), "they poured out waters", in 1-188-5; 3) प्र प्र यज्ञं प्रणीत न (pra pra yajñaṃ praṇīta na), "they fill the sacrifice with fruit", in 5-5-5; 4) इन्वंतो विश्वं प्रति यन्नृतेन (invaṃto viśvaṃ prati yannṛtena), "they quicken the whole world with water", in 3-4-5.

p. 250

Thus their duties are indicated in many other ways. Some hold that many of these actions are attributed to them merely ornamentally and figuratively, and that there is no truth in them. Moreover, समिद्दो अस्य मनुषो दुरोणे देवो देवान् यजसि जातवेदः । आ च वह मित्रमहश्चि कित्वान्त्वं दूतः कविरसि प्रचेताः ॥ (samiddo asya manuṣo duroṇe devo devān yajasi jātavedaḥ | ā ca vaha mitramahaści kitvāntvaṃ dūtaḥ kavirasi pracetāḥ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-1) In this verse, since it says मनुषो दुरोणे (manuṣo duroṇe), "in the house of man", this figurative language applied to merely worldly house-doors may even look like an excessive flight of fancy. Some critics also hold that adjectives such as नृपेशसः (nṛpeśasaḥ), ऋतावृधः (ṛtāvṛdhaḥ), पावका (pāvakā) are not fitting. Here, whether to support or to refute these opinions, it is good to learn the views of the Vedic scholars who are the foundation for keeping up the Vedic tradition.

In the verse of the Āprī hymn स्वाध्यो३ वि दुरो देवयंतोऽशिश्रयू रथयुर्देवताता । पूर्वि शिशुं न मातरा रिहाणे समग्रुवो न समनेष्वंजन् । (svādhyo3 vi duro devayaṃto 'śiśrayū rathayurdevatātā | pūrvi śiśuṃ na mātarā rihāṇe samagruvo na samaneṣvaṃjan |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-2-5) they state clearly, यज्ञगृहद्वाराणि इत्यर्थः (yajñagṛhadvārāṇi ityarthaḥ), that it means the doors of the sacrificial house. Likewise some other scholars explain that for the verb व्यशिश्रयुः (vyaśiśrayuḥ) the subject is यजमानाः (yajamānāḥ), and that the construction is that they stood taking shelter at the door of the sacrificial house. The English scholars Oldenberg, Grassman and Ludwig also approve this explanation, and in the verse विराट्संम्राड्विभ्रीः प्रभ्वीर्बह्वीश्च भूयसीश्च याः । दुरो धृतान्यक्षरन् । (virāṭsaṃmrāḍvibhrīḥ prabhvīrbahvīśca bhūyasīśca yāḥ | duro dhṛtānyakṣaran |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-188-5) they say the words विराट् (virāṭ) and संम्राट् (saṃmrāṭ) are the names of two door-leaves. The scholar Max Muller says these are the gates of heaven by which the gods descend from heaven (History of Ancient Sanskrit Literature, p. 245). In the Praiṣa hymn, होतायक्षद्दुर ऋष्वाः कवष्टोऽकोषधावनीरुदाताभिर्जिहतां वि पक्षोभिः श्रयंतां । सुप्रायणा अस्मिन्यज्ञे विश्रयंतामृतावृधो वियंत्वाज्यस्य होतर्यज । (hotāyakṣaddura ṛṣvāḥ kavaṣṭo 'koṣadhāvanīrudātābhirjihatāṃ vi pakṣobhiḥ śrayaṃtāṃ | suprāyaṇā asminyajñe viśrayaṃtāmṛtāvṛdho viyaṃtvājyasya hotaryaja |) (Tai. Brā. 3-6-2-2)

p. 251

— what is said in these sentences the commentator explains as दुरो द्वारसंज्ञकाः पंचमप्रयाजदेवतास्तद्रूपमग्निं दैवो होता यजतु (duro dvārasaṃjñakāḥ paṃcamaprayājadevatāstadrūpamagniṃ daivo hotā yajatu). In these sentences the words आताभिः (ātābhiḥ) and उज्जिहतां (ujjihatāṃ) are important; this to some extent opposes the opinion above. From this one view is that it can be said that "door" meaning the doors of the sacrificial house is ornamental. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa, दुरो यजति वृष्टिर्वै दुरो वृष्टिमेव तत्प्रीणाति वृष्टिमन्नाद्यं यजमाने दधाति । (duro yajati vṛṣṭirvai duro vṛṣṭimeva tatprīṇāti vṛṣṭimannādyaṃ yajamāne dadhāti |) (Ai. Brā. 2-4) NOTE the meaning "rain" is given in place of "door". How this meaning arises is not made clear. The Nirukta author says द्वारो जवतेर्वा प्रवतेर्वा पारयतेर्वा (dvāro javatervā pravatervā pārayatervā): that it is formed either from the root जु (ju) meaning "press forward", or from the root द्रु (dru) meaning "advance", or from the root वृ (vṛ) meaning "separate". Quoting the verse व्यचस्वतीरुर्विया वि श्रयंतां पतिभ्यो न जनयः शुंभमानाः । देवीर्द्वारो बृहतीर्विश्वमिन्वा देवेभ्यो भवत सुप्रायणाः । (vyacasvatīrurviyā vi śrayaṃtāṃ patibhyo na janayaḥ śuṃbhamānāḥ | devīrdvāro bṛhatīrviśvaminvā devebhyo bhavata suprāyaṇāḥ |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-5) and explaining the meaning of the word द्वार (dvāra), he states a difference of opinion: गृहद्वार इति कात्थक्यः । (gṛhadvāra iti kātthakyaḥ |) according to Kātthakya it is a house-door, and अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः । (agniriti śākapūṇiḥ |) according to Śākapūṇi it is Agni (Ni. 8-10). In the Bṛhaddevatā, द्वारस्तु देव्यो याः प्रोक्ता विश्वेषां तास्तु पत्नयः । अग्नायीमनुवर्तंते तथाग्नाय्क्यग्निमेव च ॥ अग्नौ ध्रुवं स्थितास्तास्तु संस्तूयंतेऽग्निना सह । प्राधान्यं तासु चैवाग्ने स्तुतिष्टेव हविष्णु च ॥ (dvārastu devyo yāḥ proktā viśveṣāṃ tāstu patnayaḥ | agnāyīmanuvartaṃte tathāgnāykyagnimeva ca ‖ agnau dhruvaṃ sthitāstāstu saṃstūyaṃte 'gninā saha | prādhānyaṃ tāsu caivāgne stutiṣṭeva haviṣṇu ca ‖) (Bṛ. De. 3-6 to 7) it says that these doors are wives of the gods; that they follow Agnāyī, who follows Agni; and that, being firmly established in Agni, they are praised together with Agni. This explanation is reasonable.

असश्चतः (asaścataḥ)—असज्यमानाः परस्परं विप्रकृष्टाः । (asajyamānāḥ parasparaṃ viprakṛṣṭāḥ |) It means those who stand apart, not clinging to one another.

p. 252

Grammar
  • श्रयंताम् — श्रिञ् सेवायां धातुः । लोट् प्रथमपुरुषबहुवचनांतरूपम् । अतिजंतस्य परत्वान्निघातस्वरो भवति ।
  • ऋतावृधः — ऋतं वर्धयंति इति ऋतवृधः । वृधु वृद्धौ धातुः । प्रयोजकव्यापारदर्शनादंतर्भावितण्यर्थको धातुः । क्विप् च (पा. सू. ३-२-७६) इति क्विप् प्रत्ययः । उपपदसमासः । अन्येषामपि दृश्यते (पा. सू. ६-३-१३७) इति पूर्वपदस्य संहितायां दीर्घो भवति । गतिकारकोपपदात्‌कृत् इति कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति ।
  • प्रयै — या प्रापणे इति धातुः । प्रयै रोहिष्यै अव्यथिष्यै (पा. सू. ३-४-१०) इति निपातितम् । कृन्मेजंतः इति अव्ययसंज्ञा भवति ।
  • महीः — महतीः इत्यत्र छांदसत्वेन अतः लोपः । विभक्तौ परस्यां सुपां सुलुक् (पा. सू. ७-१-३९) इति पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घः ।
  • पावकासः — जसि परे आज्जसेरसुक् (पा. सू. ७-१-५०) इति तस्य असुक् आगमः ।
  • पुरुस्पृहः — स्पृह ईप्सायां धातुः । क्विप् प्रत्ययः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति ।
  • असश्चतः — ग्लुञ्च षस्ज गतौ धातुः । जकारस्य व्यत्ययेन चकारः । अस्मात् लडर्थे शतृ प्रत्ययः । न विद्यंते सश्चंतः गच्छंतः येषु असश्चतः । नञ्सुभ्याम् (पा. ६-२-१७२) इति उत्तरपदांतोदात्तस्वरो भवति ।

Ṛk 7

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

आ भंद॑माने॒ उपा॑के॒ नक्तो॒षासा॑ सु॒पेश॑सा ।
य॒ह्वी ऋ॒तस्य॑ मा॒तरा॒ सीद॑तां ब॒र्हिरा सु॒मत् ॥ ७ ॥

ā bhaṃdamāne upāke naktoṣāsā supeśasā | yahvī ṛtasya mātarā sīdatāṃ barhirā sumat ‖ 7 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

आ । भंदमाने इति । उपाके इति । नक्तोषसा । सुपेशसा ।
यह्वी इति । ऋतस्य । मातरा । सीदतां । बर्हिः । आ । सुमत् ॥ ७ ॥

ā | bhaṃdamāne iti | upāke iti | naktoṣasā | supeśasā | yahvī iti | ṛtasya | mātarā | sīdatāṃ | barhiḥ | ā | sumat ‖ 7 ‖

p. 253

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

भंदमाने सर्वैः स्तूयमाने उपाके वरस्परं सन्निहिते सुपेशसा शोभनरूपे । पेश इति रूपनाम । यह्वी महत्वा अपत्यरूपे वा प्रतिदिनं जायमानत्वात् । यहुरित्यपत्यनाम यहुः सूनुरिति तन्नामसु पाठात् । ऋतस्य मातरा यज्ञस्य निर्मात्र्यौ । ताभ्यामागमनाद्यज्ञस्य संपूर्तेयज्ञमातृत्वमुपचर्यते । यद्वा । अतिरात्रादीनामहोरात्रसाध्यत्वात् । नक्तोषासा उक्तगुणविशिष्टे अहोरात्रदेवते सुमत् स्वयमेव । आस्माभिरप्रार्थिते इत्यर्थः । यद्वा । सुमद्बर्हिरास्कृतं दर्भमा समंतादा सीदतां । उपविशतां । यद्वा । ऋतस्यॆति कर्मणि षष्ठी । यज्ञ मा सीदतां । आसाद्य च बर्हिरास्कृतं दर्भं स्वयनेवा सीदतां ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

भंदमाने (bhaṃdamāne) means praised by all; उपाके (upāke) means near each other; सुपेशसा (supeśasā) means of beautiful form, पेश (peśa) being a name for form. यह्वी (yahvī) means either great, or of the form of offspring because they are born every day; he supports this from the list of names, where यहु (yahu) is a name for offspring ("yahuḥ sūnuḥ"). ऋतस्य मातरा (ṛtasya mātarā) means the two who produce the sacrifice; because the sacrifice is completed by their coming, the sacrifice is figuratively said to have them as mothers. Or else, because rites such as the atirātra are accomplished by day and night, नक्तोषासा (naktoṣāsā) are the deities of day and night, endowed with the stated qualities. सुमत् (sumat) means of their own accord, unasked by us. Or else sumat barhiḥ is the prepared darbha grass: let them sit down upon it all around, let them be seated. Or else ऋतस्य (ṛtasya) is a genitive in the sense of the object: let them come to the sacrifice, and having come, let them of their own accord sit on the prepared darbha grass.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • आ छंदमाने (ā chaṃdamāne)—those who are called upon by all NOTE
  • उपाके (upāke)—those who are close to each other
  • सुपेशसा (supeśasā)—those of charming form
  • यह्वी (yahvī)—those of great form; or (because born daily) those of the form of offspring
  • ऋतस्य (ṛtasya)—of the sacrifice
  • मातरा (mātarā)—the two who are the cause of making
  • नक्तोषासा (naktoṣāsā)—the deities of night and day
  • सुमत् (sumat)—(even if we do not pray) of your own accord
  • बर्हिः (barhiḥ)—upon the darbha seat
  • आ सीदतां (ā sīdatāṃ)—sit down facing it
  • अथवा सुमत् (athavā sumat)—widely spread
  • बर्हिः (barhiḥ)—upon the darbha seat
  • आ सीदतां (ā sīdatāṃ)—sit down facing it
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O deities of day and night, praised by all, near each other, of charming form, of great form, and makers of the sacrifice: even though we have not prayed, of your own accord and with kindly regard, be pleased to sit upon our widely spread darbha seats.

Printed English

Beautiful night and morning, ever hymned, ever associated, progeny (of time), parents of sacrifice, sit down of your own good-will on the sacred grass.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

(आ) भंदमाने ((ā) bhaṃdamāne)—सर्वैः स्तूयमाने । (sarvaiḥ stūyamāne |) "Praised by all": an adjective of the deities called नक्तोषासा (naktoṣāsā). Since it is read among the names of the act of worship, अर्चति (arcati), गायति (gāyati) and so on (Ni. 3-19), भंदमाना (bhaṃdamānā) means the object of worship. भंदनाः । (bhaṃdanāḥ |)

p. 254

The Nirukta says that भंदना भंदतेः स्तुतिकर्मणः । (bhaṃdanā bhaṃdateḥ stutikarmaṇaḥ |) (Ni. 5-2): the word is formed from the root भंद् (bhaṃd) and means an act of praise. The Nirukta cites two Ṛks:

आ विवेश रोदसी भूरिर्वपसा पुरुप्रियो भंदते धामभिः कविः । (ā viveśa rodasī bhūrirvapasā purupriyo bhaṃdate dhāmabhiḥ kaviḥ |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-3-4)

स भंदना उदियर्ति प्रजावतीर्विश्वायुर्विश्वाः सुभरा अहर्दिवि । (sa bhaṃdanā udiyarti prajāvatīrviśvāyurviśvāḥ subharā ahardivi |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-86-41.)

and thereby shows that the word is fitting in contexts where excellent praise is made. (Ni. 5-2)

सुमत् (sumat)—स्वयमेव । अस्माभिरप्रार्थिते इत्यर्थः। (svayameva | asmābhiraprārthite ityarthaḥ|) That is, "even if we do not pray, of your own accord"; it indicates the generosity and the self-respect of Uṣāsānaktā. सुमत्स्वयमित्यर्थः (sumatsvayamityarthaḥ) (Ni. 6-22): the Nirukta explains the word सुमत् (sumat) as स्वयं (svayaṃ), that is, "of itself". It is also understood that this is not the only meaning of the word; it is also a synonym of the words कल्याण (kalyāṇa), शोभन (śobhana) or भद्र (bhadra). Since many words such as सुमद्रथः (sumadrathaḥ), सुमद्गणः (sumadgaṇaḥ), सुमदंशुः (sumadaṃśuḥ) are in use, one looks at the meaning of those words. In the Ṛk

अमेव नः सुहवा आ हि गंतन नि बर्हिषि सदतना रणिष्टन । (ameva naḥ suhavā ā hi gaṃtana ni barhiṣi sadatanā raṇiṣṭana |) अथा मंदस्व जुजुषाणो अंधसस्त्वष्टर्देवेभिर्जनिभिः सुमद्गणः । (athā maṃdasva jujuṣāṇo aṃdhasastvaṣṭardevebhirjanibhiḥ sumadgaṇaḥ |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-36-3)

the word सुमद्गणः (sumadgaṇaḥ) is explained as शोभनगणः (śobhanagaṇaḥ); and in

विभावा देवः सुरणः परि क्षितीरग्निर्बभूव शवसा सुमद्रथः । (vibhāvā devaḥ suraṇaḥ pari kṣitīragnirbabhūva śavasā sumadrathaḥ |) तस्य व्रतानि भूरिपोषिणो वयमुप भूषेम दम आ सुवृक्तिभिः । (tasya vratāni bhūripoṣiṇo vayamupa bhūṣema dama ā suvṛktibhiḥ |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-3-9)

सुमद्रथः (sumadrathaḥ) is explained as शोभनरथः (śobhanarathaḥ). In all these places the word सुमत् (sumat) is a synonym of शोभन (śobhana) and कल्याण (kalyāṇa). Likewise here too, since the coming of the deities Uṣāsānaktā is excellent and auspicious, the fitness of this word can be understood.

उपाके (upāke)—this word is read among the words for "near" (Ni. 3-9); परस्परं सन्निहिते । (parasparaṃ sannihite |) It means those who are close to each other.

सुपेशसा (supeśasā)—पेश इति रूपनाम । पिंशतेर्विपिशितं भवति । (peśa iti rūpanāma | piṃśatervipiśitaṃ bhavati |) The Nirukta, citing this very Ṛk, shows that the word is formed from the root पिश् (piś), which gives the sense "refined, polished", and means "possessing beauty" (Ni. 8-11). The purport is: those whose form is exceedingly beautiful.

p. 255

यह्वी (yahvī)—महत्यौ अपत्यरूपे वा । (mahatyau apatyarūpe vā |) It means: those of a very great nature, or those of the form of children. In the Nirukta this word is read among the words for "great" (Ni. 3-13) and also among the words for offspring, तुक् (tuk), तोकं (tokaṃ) and so on (Ni. 3-1). Both kinds of nature can be seen in the description of Uṣas. For example:

उप व एषे वंद्येभिः शूष्यैः प्र यह्वी दिवश्चि तयद्भिरर्कैः । (upa va eṣe vaṃdyebhiḥ śūṣyaiḥ pra yahvī divaści tayadbhirarkaiḥ |) उषासानक्ता विदुषीव विश्वमा हा वहतो मर्त्याय यज्ञं । (uṣāsānaktā viduṣīva viśvamā hā vahato martyāya yajñaṃ |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-41-7)

उत योषणे दिव्ये मही न उषासानक्ता सुदुघेव धेनुः । (uta yoṣaṇe divye mahī na uṣāsānaktā sudugheva dhenuḥ |) बर्हिषदा पुरुहूते मघोनी आ यज्ञये सुविताय श्रयेतां । (barhiṣadā puruhūte maghonī ā yajñaye suvitāya śrayetāṃ |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-2-6)

In these and similar Ṛks the great nature of the deities Uṣāsānakta is described. And in

द्वे विरूपे चरतः स्पर्धे अन्यान्या वत्समुप धापयेते । (dve virūpe carataḥ spardhe anyānyā vatsamupa dhāpayete |) हरिरन्यस्यां भवति स्वधावाञ्चुक्रो अन्यस्यां ददृशे सुवर्चाः ॥ (hariranyasyāṃ bhavati svadhāvāñcukro anyasyāṃ dadṛśe suvarcāḥ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-95-1)

पुनः पुनर्जायमाना पुराणी समानं वर्णमभिशुंभमाना । श (punaḥ punarjāyamānā purāṇī samānaṃ varṇamabhiśuṃbhamānā | śa) श्वघ्नीव कृत्नुर्विज आमिनाना मर्तस्य देवी जरयंत्यायुः ॥ (śvaghnīva kṛtnurvija āminānā martasya devī jarayaṃtyāyuḥ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-92-10)

and similar Ṛks, the point is also described that Night and Uṣas, being born again and again, are of the form of children. Therefore, for the word यह्वी (yahvī) either of the two meanings above may be given.

नक्तोषसा (naktoṣasā)—among the other epithets of these deities the epithet ऋतस्य मातरा (ṛtasya mātarā) is very important.

द्रवतां त उषसा वाजयंती अग्ने वातस्य पथ्याभिरच्छ । (dravatāṃ ta uṣasā vājayaṃtī agne vātasya pathyābhiraccha |) यत्स्रीमंजंति पूर्व्यं हविर्भिरा वंधुरेव तस्थतुर्दुरोणे ॥ (yatsrīmaṃjaṃti pūrvyaṃ havirbhirā vaṃdhureva tasthaturduroṇe ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-14-3)

In this Ṛk the constant relation between the sacrifice and them is described. In all the Ṛks that invite them (there are about twenty such Ṛks) they are prayed to come with the other deities and sit on the sacred-grass seat. Moreover, they have a very close relation with Agni, who is kindled at dawn and at evening. For that very reason the figurative description that they bear and hold Agni between them,

p. 256

नक्तोषासा वर्णमामेम्याने धापयेते शिशुमेकं समीची । (naktoṣāsā varṇamāmemyāne dhāpayete śiśumekaṃ samīcī |) द्यावाक्षामा रुक्मो अंतर्नि भाति देवा अग्निं धारयन्द्रविणोदां ॥ (dyāvākṣāmā rukmo aṃtarni bhāti devā agniṃ dhārayandraviṇodāṃ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-96-5)

and similar Ṛks, tells that they help Agni, who is of the form of a child, to drink the oblation. Because of this relation they are said to be near the sacrificers. In general this description is repeated in the Āprī-sūktas too. For example:

अ सुष्वयंती यजते उपाके उषासानक्ता सदतां नि योन् । (a suṣvayaṃtī yajate upāke uṣāsānaktā sadatāṃ ni yon |) दिव्ये योषणे बृहती सुरुक्मे अधि श्रियं शुक्रपिशं दधाने ॥ (divye yoṣaṇe bṛhatī surukme adhi śriyaṃ śukrapiśaṃ dadhāne ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10.118-6)

In this Ṛk of an Āprī-sūkta the same matter is stated.

From this it is understood that the deities Uṣāsānaktā are not given a subordinate place in the sacrificial acts but obtain a most important place. This obtaining of a principal place is indicated in the mantra of the Praiṣa-sūkta,

होता यक्षदुषासानक्ता बृहती सुपेशसा नृग्ं पतिभ्यो योनिं कृण्वाने ॥ (hotā yakṣaduṣāsānaktā bṛhatī supeśasā nṛgṃ patibhyo yoniṃ kṛṇvāne ‖) सग्ंस्मयमाने इंद्रेण देवैरेदं बर्हिः सीदतां वीतामाज्यस्य होतरज ॥ (sagṃsmayamāne iṃdreṇa devairedaṃ barhiḥ sīdatāṃ vītāmājyasya hotaraja ‖) (Ḍvai Brā. 3-6-21)NOTE

in which Uṣā-naktā are prayed to sit on the sacred-grass seat not only with Agni but also with the other deities beginning with Indra. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa they are addressed as अहोरात्रे (ahorātre). In Ni. 8, 11 the Nirukta-author has described the nature of these deities. What the Nirukta-author says of the derivation of the two words उषस् (uṣas) and नक्त (nakta) and of the nature of these deities has been told earlier. In the Bṛhaddevatā too they are described in this way:

नक्तोषासौ च ये देव्यावाग्नेय्यावेव ते स्मृते । (naktoṣāsau ca ye devyāvāgneyyāveva te smṛte |) श्याव्याग्नेयी हि कालस्य तस्यैवोषाः कलेव तु॥ (śyāvyāgneyī hi kālasya tasyaivoṣāḥ kaleva tu‖) (Bṛ. Je. 3-8)NOTE

It is well known that these two deities, Uṣas and Nakta, are related to Agni. Of these, Śyāvī (the night-deity, 1-71-1) has a close relation with Agni; and from the Nirukta sentence उषः कस्मादुच्छतीति सत्या रात्रेरपरः कालः (uṣaḥ kasmāducchatīti satyā rātreraparaḥ kālaḥ) (Ni 2-18) it is known that Uṣas is the later part of that night.

तम उच्छत्युषा नक्तानक्तीमां हिमबिंदुभिः । (tama ucchatyuṣā naktānaktīmāṃ himabiṃdubhiḥ |) अपि नाव्यक्तवर्णेति नइद् पूर्वाइच्चेरिदं भवेत् ॥ (api nāvyaktavarṇeti naid pūrvāicceridaṃ bhavet ‖) (Bṛ. De. 3-9)

p. 257

Of these two, Uṣas drives away the darkness. Night makes everything wet and pervaded by drops of dew. Or, since she has no distinct colour, the root अञ् (añ) joins with the particle नञ् (nañ) and gives the sense "of indistinct colour".

सा हि दोषा भवत्यादौ निशीथे सा तमस्वती । (sā hi doṣā bhavatyādau niśīthe sā tamasvatī |) नाम्मा भवत्युषाश्चैव सैषा प्रागुदयाद्रवेः ॥ (nāmmā bhavatyuṣāścaiva saiṣā prāgudayādraveḥ ‖) (Bṛ De. 3-10)

At the beginning this deity is named (Pra)doṣā, at midnight Tamasvatī, and before sunrise Uṣas. दोषा (doṣā), तमस्वती (tamasvatī), श्यावी (śyāvī), नक्ता (naktā) are all names of night, as read in the Nighaṇṭu (Nighaṇṭu 1-7).

Elsewhere in the Ṛk-saṃhitā, by epithets such as तंतुं ततं संवयंती (taṃtuṃ tataṃ saṃvayaṃtī) (2.3-6), the help of Uṣāsānaktā in the extension of the sacrifice is described.

Grammar
  • भंदमाने—भवि कल्याणे । सुखे च । धातुः । भ्यादिः । लिटि शानचादेशः । इदितोनुम्धातोः इति सुमागमः । शप् विकरणः । आनेमुक् (पा. सू. ७-२-८२) इति मुकागमः । अदुपदेशात् परं लसार्वधातुकस्यागतत्वात् तास्यनुदात्तेत्—(पा. सू. ६-१-१८६) इति तदनुदात्तं भवति । तेन धातुस्वरः शिष्यते । सप्तम्येकवचनांतरूपम् ।NOTE
  • उपाके—अंतोदात्तस्वरे प्राप्ते व्यत्ययेन आद्युदात्तं भवति ।
  • नक्तोषसा—नक्तं च उषाश्च नक्तोषसा । द्विवचनस्य औकारविभक्तेः सुपां सुलुक्—(पा.सू. ७-१-३९) इति आकारादेशः । पूर्वपदस्य मकारस्य लोपः उत्तरपदे दीर्घश्च छांदसतया भवतः ।
  • सुपेशसा—शोभनं पेशः रूपं ययोस्ते । पूर्ववत् आकारादेशः । नञ्सुभ्याम् (पा. सू. ६-२-१६२) इति उत्तरपदांतोदात्तस्वरे प्राप्ते तस्यापवादतया आद्युदात्तं द्व्यच्छंदसि (पा. सू. ६-२-११९) इति उत्तरपदमाद्युदात्तस्वरं भवति ।
  • मातरा—सुपां सुलुक्—(पा. रू. ७-३९) इति विभक्तेः आकारादेशः ।NOTE
  • सीदताम्—षद्ल्य विशरणगत्यवसादनेषु । लोट्प्रथमपुरुषद्विवचने लज्ञद्भावत्वात् तामादेशः । पाघ्राध्मा—(पा. सू. ७-३-७८) इति सीदादेशः । अदुपदेशात् परं प्रत्ययस्यागतत्वात् तास्यनुदात्तेत्—सूत्रेण तदनुदात्तं भवति । तेन धातुस्वरः शिष्यते । पादादौ आगतत्वात् निघातस्वरो न भवति ।

p. 258

Ṛk 8

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

मं॒द्रजि॑ह्वा जुगु॒र्वणी॒ होता॑रा॒ दैन्व्या॑ क॒वी ।
य॒ज्ञं नो॑ यक्षतामि॒मं सि॒ध्रम॒द्य दि॑वि॒स्पृशं॑ ॥ ८ ॥

maṃdrajihvā jugurvaṇī hotārā dainvyā kavī | yajñaṃ no yakṣatāmimaṃ sidhramadya divispṛśaṃ ‖ 8 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

मंद्रजिह्वा । जुगुर्वणे इति । होतारा । दैव्या । कवी इति ।
यज्ञं । नः । यक्षतां । इमं । सिद्धं । अद्य । दिविस्पृशं ॥ ८ ॥

maṃdrajihvā | jugurvaṇe iti | hotārā | daivyā | kavī iti | yajñaṃ | naḥ | yakṣatāṃ | imaṃ | siddhaṃ | adya | divispṛśaṃ ‖ 8 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

मंद्रजिह्वा देवानां मादनज्वाल् जुगुर्वणी भृशं गृणतां स्तुवतां यजमानानां संभक्तारौ ॥ गृणतेर्यज्लुगंतात् क्विपि च्छांदसी रूपसिद्धिः । तस्मिन्नुपदे वनतेश्चंदसि वनसनरक्षिमथामितीन्प्रत्ययः ॥ कवी मेधाविनौ क्रांतदर्शिनौ दैव्या होतारा देवसंबंधिनौ होतार् अयं च मध्यमस्थानश्चेत्युभौ सिद्ध्रं फल. साधनभूतं ॥ सिधेः स्थायितंचीत्यादिना रक् ॥ दिविस्पृशं द्युलोकनासिदेवान् स्पृशंतं । तैर्हनिषः स्वीक्रियमाणत्पादिति भावः । ईदृशं नोऽस्मदीयमिमं यज्ञमद्य यक्षतां । अनुतिष्ठतां पूजयतां ना । सम्यङ्निर्वाहयतामित्यर्थः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

मंद्रजिह्वा (maṃdrajihvā): those whose flames gladden the gods. जुगुर्वणी (jugurvaṇī): those who bestow (संभक्तारौ (saṃbhaktārau)) on the sacrificers who greatly praise and extol; the form is explained as an irregular (Vedic) formation from the root गृण (gṛṇa) in the intensive-luk, with kvip.NOTE कवी (kavī): the two who are wise and far-seeing. दैव्या होतारा (daivyā hotārā): the two Hotṛs related to the gods; he says that these two are this (terrestrial) Agni and the one who has the middle region as his place. सिद्ध्रं (siddhraṃ): the instrument of the fruit. दिविस्पृशं (divispṛśaṃ): touching the dwellers of the heavenly world, the gods; the idea is that the oblations are accepted by them.NOTE Let them today perform (यक्षतां (yakṣatāṃ)) such a sacrifice of ours: carry it out, worship it, bring it to proper completion.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • मंद्रजिह्वा (maṃdrajihvā)—those whose flames cause delight (to the gods)
  • जुगुर्वणी (jugurvaṇī)—those who favour the sacrificers who offer praise
  • कवी (kavī)—the wise ones
  • दैव्या होतारा (daivyā hotārā)—the two forms of Agni, who call the gods (to the sacrifice)
  • सिद्धं (siddhaṃ)—that which gives fruit
  • दिविस्पृशं (divispṛśaṃ)—that which reaches (the gods) in the world of the gods
  • नः इमं यज्ञं (naḥ imaṃ yajñaṃ)—this sacrifice of ours
  • अद्य (adya)—now
  • यक्षतां (yakṣatāṃ)—let them perform
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the two forms of Agni, whose flames gladden the gods and who favour the devoted sacrificers, now perform this sacrifice of ours, which gives fruit and reaches the gods in the world of the gods.

p. 259

Printed English

May the two pleasing-tongued receivers of praise, the divine and sage invokers (of the gods), officiate to-day at this our sacrifice, which confers (rewards) and attains heaven.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

दैव्या होतारा (daivyā hotārā)—देवसंबंधिनौ होतारौ। अयं च मध्यमस्थानश्च इत्युभौ। (devasaṃbaṃdhinau hotārau| ayaṃ ca madhyamasthānaśca ityubhau|) Sāyaṇa has explained these as the two forms of Agni: the terrestrial Agni and the Agni of the atmosphere, both related to the gods and both Hotṛs. Some modern scholars have given a different meaning and have also shown differences of opinion among themselves. The scholar Goldner has explained them as the Hotṛ who is the sacrificer and his Agni; Hang as the Hotṛ and the Adhvaryu; Oldenberg as the Hotṛ and his assistant, the Maitrāvaruṇa. None of these is reasonable.

That the performing of the sacrifice is the chief duty of these Hotṛs is stated in the Ṛks 1-13-8 and 1-18-7 by यज्ञं नो यक्षतामिमं । (yajñaṃ no yakṣatāmimaṃ |) and in the Ṛk 2-3-7 by देवान्यजंतावृतुथा । (devānyajaṃtāvṛtuthā |) This reminder of duty should apply to the human Hotṛ, and Agni is addressed figuratively. In the same way, in

देव्या होतारा प्रथमा सुवाचा मिमाना यज्ञं मनुषो यजध्यै । (devyā hotārā prathamā suvācā mimānā yajñaṃ manuṣo yajadhyai |) प्रचोदयंता विदथेषु कारू प्राचीनं ज्योतिः प्रदिशा दिशंता । (pracodayaṃtā vidatheṣu kārū prācīnaṃ jyotiḥ pradiśā diśaṃtā |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-111-7)

it is the opinion of some scholars that the description "producers of the sacrifice" or "those who measure the sacrifice" also suggests the same idea.

Thus some epithets, though common to both Hotṛs, suggest only the duty of the human Hotṛ; other epithets, again common to both, describe only the duties of Agni, the divine Hotṛ. For example:

देव्या होतारा प्रथमा न्यृंजे सप्त पृक्षासः स्वधया मदंति । (devyā hotārā prathamā nyṛṃje sapta pṛkṣāsaḥ svadhayā madaṃti |) ऋतं शसंत ऋतमित्त आहुरनु व्रतं व्रतसा दीध्यानाः ॥ (ṛtaṃ śasaṃta ṛtamitta āhuranu vrataṃ vratasā dīdhyānāḥ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-4-7)

In this Ṛk there is no doubt that the epithet प्रथमा (prathamā) refers to Agni, the divine Hotṛ.

p. 260

In 1-13-4 too, होता मनुर्हितः (hotā manurhitaḥ) is an epithet of Agni. The precise difference between these two hotṛs is stated in the Praiṣa-sūkta thus: होता यक्षद्देव्या होतारा मंद्रा पोतारा कवी प्रचेतसा । स्विष्टमिद्यान्यः करदिषा स्वभिगूर्तमन्य ऊर्जा सतवसेमं यज्ञं दिवि देवेषु धत्तां वीतामाज्यस्य होतर्यज । (hotā yakṣaddevyā hotārā maṃdrā potārā kavī pracetasā | sviṣṭamidyānyaḥ karadiṣā svabhigūrtamanya ūrjā satavasemaṃ yajñaṃ divi deveṣu dhattāṃ vītāmājyasya hotaryaja |) (Tai. Brā. 3-6-2-2) In this sentence it is indicated that one hotṛ is to make the sacrifice acceptable with the oblation in the form of food, and the other is to establish this sacrifice in heaven among the gods. This exchange of functions shows the difference between the human hotṛ and Agni, the divine hotṛ. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa: दैन्या होतारा यजति प्राणापानौ वै दैन्या होतारा प्राणापानावेव तत्प्रीणाति प्राणापानौ यजमाने दधाति । (dainyā hotārā yajati prāṇāpānau vai dainyā hotārā prāṇāpānāveva tatprīṇāti prāṇāpānau yajamāne dadhāti |) (Ai. Brā. 2-4) Thus the identity of these hotṛs with prāṇa and apāna is stated, and it is said that the one who recites this mantra secures for the sacrificer the well-being of prāṇa and apāna. In the Nirukta: दैन्या होतारा दैन्य होतारावयं चाग्निरस् च मध्यमः (dainyā hotārā dainya hotārāvayaṃ cāgniras ca madhyamaḥ) (Ni. 8-12) Thus, in passages that support Sāyaṇa's meaning, the two are said to be the terrestrial Agni and the Agni of the atmosphere. In the Bṛhaddevatā too, approving the same view: दैव्याविति तु होतारावग्नी पार्थिवमध्यम् । दिन्यादग्नीर्हि जज्ञाते दैन्यौ तेनेह जन्मना ॥ (daivyāviti tu hotārāvagnī pārthivamadhyam | dinyādagnīrhi jajñāte dainyau teneha janmanā ‖) (Bṛ. De. 3-11) It is said that both these hotṛs are the terrestrial and the middle (atmospheric) Agnis.

Jugurvaṇī—भृशं गृणतां यजमानानां संभक्तारौ (bhṛśaṃ gṛṇatāṃ yajamānānāṃ saṃbhaktārau): the two who favour the sacrificers who praise them; that is the meaning.

Sidhram—सिद्धं फलसाधनभूतं (siddhaṃ phalasādhanabhūtaṃ): that which yields fruit; that is the meaning. The Nirukta author: द्यावा नः पृथिवी इमं सिध्रमद्य दिविस्पृशं । यज्ञं देवेषु यच्छतां । (dyāvā naḥ pṛthivī imaṃ sidhramadya divispṛśaṃ | yajñaṃ deveṣu yacchatāṃ |) NOTE

p. 261

Having cited this Ṛk, he explains the word siddha as meaning "instrument". In the present Ṛk it means the sacrifice that is the means of the fruit.

Mandrajihvā—देवानां मादनज्वाल् (devānāṃ mādanajvāl): those whose flames bring delight to the gods; that is the meaning. The words mandra and mandrajihva are explained in the Special Topics of Ṛk 1-141-12 of this same volume. Since it is impossible for the word mandrajihvā to be an epithet of the human hotṛ, it shows that दैव्य होतारौ (daivya hotārau) must be the two forms of Agni. Only then is this epithet appropriate.

Grammar
  • मंद्रजिह्वा — मदी हर्ष धातुः । स्थायितञ्च—(उ. सू. २-१७०) इति रक् प्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तो भवति । मंद्रा जिह्वा ययोस्ते मंद्रजिह्वा । बहुव्रीहौ—(पा.सू. ६-२-१) इति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति । सुपां सुलुक्—इति सूत्रेण विभक्तेः आकारादेशः ।
  • जुगुर्वणी — ग्य शब्द धातुः । भृशार्थे धातोरेकाचः—(पा. सू. ३-१-२२) इति यज् प्रत्यये आगते यजोचिच (पा. सू. २-४-७४) इति तस्य अनैमित्तिके लुकि आगते छांदसत्वेन जुगुर् इति रूपं भवति । वन संभक्तौ धातुः । जुगुर् इति उपपदे सति छंदसिवनसनरक्षिमथाम् (पा. सू. ३-२-२७) इति इन् प्रत्ययः । जुगुर्णि इति रूपं भवति । अट् कुप्वाज्—इति धातुनकारस्य णत्वं । द्विवचनांतरूपं ।
  • होतारा — दु दानादनयोः धातुः । कर्तरि तृन् प्रत्ययः । नित्त्वात् आम्यदात्तस्वरो भवति । द्विवचने सुपां सुलुक्—इति आकारादेशः ।
  • दैव्या — देव शब्दात् संबंधार्थे ष्यज् प्रत्ययः । इत्त्वात् तद्धितेष्वचामादेः इति आदिवृद्धिः । यस्येति च इति अकारलोपः । आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति । पूर्ववत् विभक्तेः आकारादेशः ।
  • यक्षताम् — यज देवपूजासंगतिकरणदानेषु धातुः । लोट् प्रथमपुरुषद्विवचने लङ्वद्भावात् तामादेशः । शप् विकरणः । सिब्बहुलं लेटि (पा. सू. ९-१-१९७) इत्यत्र बहुलग्रहणसामर्थ्यात् इहापि सिप् आगच्छति । चोःकुः इति जकारस्य कुत्वं । खरिच इति तस्य चर्त्वं । आदेश प्रत्यययोः इति सिपः सकारस्य पत्त्वं । अतिजंतस्य परत्वात् निघातस्वरो भवति । NOTE

p. 262

  • सिध्रम् — षिध गत्याम् धातुः । स्थायितंचिवं—(उ. सू २-१७०) इति रक् प्रत्ययः । धात्वादेः षः सः (पा. सू. ६-१-६४) इति आदेः सत्वं । प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तो भवति ।
  • दिविस्पृशम् — दिवि स्पृशति इति दिविस्पृक् । क्विप् च इति क्विप् प्रत्ययः । तत्पुरुषे कृति बहुलम् (पा. सू. ६-३१४) इति विभक्तेः अलुक् । गतिकारकोपपदात् इति कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति । ॥ ८ ॥ NOTE

Ṛk 9

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

शुचि॑र्दे॒वेष्वर्पि॑ता॒ होत्रा॑ म॒रुत्सु॒ भार॑ती ।
इळा॒ सर॑स्वती म॒ही ब॒र्हिः सी॑दंतु य॒ज्ञियाः॑ ॥ ९ ॥

śucirdeveṣvarpitā hotrā marutsu bhāratī | iḷā sarasvatī mahī barhiḥ sīdaṃtu yajñiyāḥ ‖ 9 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

शुचिः । देवेषु । अर्पिता । होत्रा । मरुत्सु । भारती ।
इळा । सरस्वती । मही । बर्हिः । सीदंतु । यज्ञियाः ॥ ९ ॥

śuciḥ | deveṣu | arpitā | hotrā | marutsu | bhāratī | iḷā | sarasvatī | mahī | barhiḥ | sīdaṃtu | yajñiyāḥ ‖ 9 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

शुचिः शुद्धा मरुत्तु विरुद्धलक्षणयामरणेषु देवेषु द्योतनशीलेषु स्तोतृषु मरुत्तु ऋत्विक्षु वार्पिता नियता होत्रा होमनिष्पादिका भारती भरतस्यादित्यस्य संबंधिनी द्युस्थाना वाक् तथेळा पार्थिवी प्रैषादिरूपा मही महती सरस्वती । सर इत्युदकनाम । तद्वती स्तनितादिरूपा माध्यमिका च वाक् एतास्तिस्रस्त्रिस्थानवागभिमानिदेवता यज्ञिया यज्ञार्हाः सत्यो बर्हिः स्तीर्णं सीदंतु । उपविशंतु ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

Śuci means pure. मरुत्सु (marutsu) is explained, with a phrase that is garbled in the text, as "among the Maruts" in the sense of the deathless NOTE. देवेषु (deveṣu) means among the radiant worshippers (stotṛs), or मरुत्सु (marutsu) among the officiating priests (ṛtvijs). Arpitā means fixed, appointed. Hotrā is the accomplisher of the offering (homa). Bhāratī is the speech of the heavenly region, belonging to Bharata, that is Āditya. Likewise Iḷā is the terrestrial speech, of the form of the praiṣa and the like. Mahī means great, an epithet of Sarasvatī. Sara is a name for water; she who has it is the speech of the atmosphere, in the form of thunder and the like. These three, the presiding deities of the speech of the three regions, being worthy of the sacrifice, are to sit on the spread sacred grass (barhis).

p. 263

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • मरुत्सु (marutsu)—among the deathless ones
  • देवेषु (deveṣu)—among the radiant ones, whether the worshippers, or the Maruts, or the priests
  • अर्पिता (arpitā)—she who is appointed
  • शुचिः (śuciḥ)—she who is pure of self
  • होत्रा (hotrā)—she who accomplishes the offering
  • भारती (bhāratī)—the goddess of speech who dwells in the heavenly world and belongs to Āditya
  • इळा (iḷā)—the goddess of speech who dwells on earth
  • मही (mahī)—she who is of great form
  • सरस्वती (sarasvatī)—the goddess of speech of the middle region, that is, who dwells in the atmosphere
  • यज्ञियाः (yajñiyāḥ)—being worthy of the sacrifice
  • बर्हिः (barhiḥ)—upon the seat of darbha grass
  • सीदंतु (sīdaṃtu)—let them sit
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Among the deathless and radiant ones, whether the worshippers, the Maruts or the priests, the goddess of speech who is appointed, who accomplishes the offering, who dwells in the heavenly world and belongs to Āditya; the goddess of speech who dwells on earth; and she who is of great form, the speech of the middle region: these deities presiding over speech in the three places, being worthy of the sacrifice, let them come and sit on the darbha seat in the sacrificial house of ours.

Printed English

May the pure Hotra, placed among the gods, and Bharati, among the Maruts, and may the adorable Ila, Saraswati, and Mahi, sit down upon the sacred grass.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk a group of three deities is addressed and requested to come to the sacrifice. In all the Āprī hymns except the present hymn and hymn 1-18, these deities are put together and collectively designated तिस्रो देवीः (tisro devīḥ); Iḷā, Sarasvatī and Bhāratī are these three. There is much disagreement about the nature of these deities. In this hymn the goddess Bhāratī has the epithets hotrā, śuciḥ and arpitā (marutsu, deveṣu), and the goddess Sarasvatī has the epithet mahī. In some hymns the word mahī is not an epithet but is used as a synonym of the goddess Bhāratī. Whether the nature of these deities can be determined exactly here may be considered by taking Śruti and similar texts as authority. If we examine the mantra that designates these deities in the Praiṣa-sūkta, which collects the main points of the Āprī hymns:—

p. 264

होतायक्षत्तिस्रो देवीरपसामपस्तमा अच्छिद्रमद्येदमपस्तन्वतां । देवेभ्यो देवीर्देवमपो वियंत्वाज्यस्य होतरज ॥ (hotāyakṣattisro devīrapasāmapastamā acchidramadyedamapastanvatāṃ | devebhyo devīrdevamapo viyaṃtvājyasya hotaraja ‖) (Śai. Brā. 3-6-2-2) NOTE Thus the original has only तिस्रो देवीः (tisro devīḥ). Explaining this in the Bhāṣya: इडा, सरस्वती, भारतीत्येवंरूपास्ति स्रोऽष्टमप्रयाजदेव्यस्तद्रूपमग्निं दैव्यो होता यजतु । (iḍā, sarasvatī, bhāratītyevaṃrūpāsti sro 'ṣṭamaprayājadevyastadrūpamagniṃ daivyo hotā yajatu |). It is said that the three eighth-prayāja goddesses, Iḍā, Sarasvatī and Bhāratī, are deities that mirror Agni. Further, अपसां अपस्तमाः (apasāṃ apastamāḥ), कर्मवतीनां मध्येऽतिश येन कर्मवत्यः । (karmavatīnāṃ madhye 'tiśa yena karmavatyaḥ |): by this epithet they are declared to be the most excellent of those who have work. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa: तिस्रो देवीर्यजति प्राणो वा अपानो व्यानस्तिस्रो देव्यस्ता एव तत्रिणाति ता यजमाने दधाति । (tisro devīryajati prāṇo vā apāno vyānastisro devyastā eva tatriṇāti tā yajamāne dadhāti |) (Ai. Brā. 2-4) Thus the identity of these three deities with the life-principles prāṇa, apāna and vyāna is stated. The Nirukta author cites the Ṛk 10-110-8, आ नो यज्ञं (ā no yajñaṃ), and gives its explanation thus: एतु नो यज्ञं भारती क्षिप्रं । भरत आदित्यस्तस्य भा इळा च मनुष्यवदिह चेतयमाना तिस्रो देव्यः बर्हिरिदं सुखं सरस्वती च सुकर्माण असीदंतु । (etu no yajñaṃ bhāratī kṣipraṃ | bharata ādityastasya bhā iḷā ca manuṣyavadiha cetayamānā tisro devyaḥ barhiridaṃ sukhaṃ sarasvatī ca sukarmāṇa asīdaṃtu |) (Ni. 8-13). Let the deity who is the radiance of Bharata (the sun), Iḷā and Sarasvatī adorn the barhis. In the Bṛhaddevatā: तिस्रस्तु देव्यो याः प्रोक्तास्त्रि स्थानैवेह सा तु वाक् । त्रिविधेनोच्यते नाम्ना ज्योतिषु त्रिषु वर्तिनी ॥ आग्निमेवानुगेळा तु मध्यं प्राप्ता सरस्वती । अमू स्थिताधि लोकं तु भारती भवति ह्यसौ ॥ सैषा तु त्रिविधा वाग्वै दिवि च व्योम्मि चेह च व्यस्ता चैव समस्ता च भजत्यग्नीनिमानपि ॥ (tisrastu devyo yāḥ proktāstri sthānaiveha sā tu vāk | trividhenocyate nāmnā jyotiṣu triṣu vartinī ‖ āgnimevānugeḷā tu madhyaṃ prāptā sarasvatī | amū sthitādhi lokaṃ tu bhāratī bhavati hyasau ‖ saiṣā tu trividhā vāgvai divi ca vyommi ceha ca vyastā caiva samastā ca bhajatyagnīnimānapi ‖) (Bṛ. Pe. 3-12 to 14) NOTE त्रिस्रो देव्यः (trisro devyaḥ) means the deities presiding over speech who dwell in all three worlds. [The three forms of speech are explained in Bṛ. De. verses 2-7 to 82.] NOTE अयं प्रयोगस्त्वेतेषां ज्योतिषां त्रिषु वर्ततां । (ayaṃ prayogastveteṣāṃ jyotiṣāṃ triṣu vartatāṃ |) (Bṛ. De. 1-91)

p. 265

As is said there, the different deities in the three worlds are transformations of one deity presiding over speech. Among them Iḷā followed the terrestrial Agni, Sarasvatī occupied the middle world, and Bhāratī came to dwell in the heavenly world. Yet, as stated in the sentence देव्यस्ति स्रः श्रिताश्चैनं त्वष्टा चैवैतदाश्रयः (devyasti sraḥ śritāścainaṃ tvaṣṭā caivaitadāśrayaḥ) (Bṛ. De. 1-108) these deities of the three worlds also serve the terrestrial Agni alone; thus everything is concluded in favour of Agni.

Mahī—महती (mahatī), of great form: an epithet of Sarasvatī. In some places it is understood as a separate deity named Mahī. Some hold that it is an epithet common to all three deities. In the Āprī hymns Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-2-6 and 9-5-6 it is an epithet of उषासानक्ता (uṣāsānaktā). Moreover, in the Ṛk इळा सरस्वती मही तिस्रो देवीर्मयोभुवः । बर्हिः सीदन्त्वस्रिधः ॥ (iḷā sarasvatī mahī tisro devīrmayobhuvaḥ | barhiḥ sīdantvasridhaḥ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-13-9) and in Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-5-8, which has the same sequence, there is no mention of Bhāratī, so Sāyaṇa has said that mahī is a synonym of the deity Bhāratī. In the present Ṛk, and in भारती पवमानस्य सरस्वतीळा मही । इमं नो यज्ञमा गमनिस्तो देवीः सुपेशसः ॥ (bhāratī pavamānasya sarasvatīḷā mahī | imaṃ no yajñamā gamanisto devīḥ supeśasaḥ ‖) (Miṃ. Saṃ. 9-5-8) NOTE it is likewise an epithet.

Iḷā—Since the Bṛhaddevatā says अग्निमेवानुगेळा (agnimevānugeḷā) (3-13), that Iḷā followed the terrestrial Agni; and since in the Ṛk प्र दीधितिर्विश्ववारा जिगाति होतारमिळः प्रथमं यजध्यै । अच्छा नमोभिर्वृषभं वंदध्यै स देवान्यक्षदिषितो यजीयान् । (pra dīdhitirviśvavārā jigāti hotāramiḷaḥ prathamaṃ yajadhyai | acchā namobhirvṛṣabhaṃ vaṃdadhyai sa devānyakṣadiṣito yajīyān |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-4-3) the word iḷa is explained as food in the form of an oblation; and since Ṛk 7-16-8 has the epithet dhṛtahastā and 10-20-8 the epithet dhṛtapadī, it appears that iḷā may be explained as oblation. Perhaps for this very reason,

p. 266

उत्तानायामव भरा चिकित्वान्स्सद्यः प्रवीता वृषणं जजान । अरुषस्तूपो रुशदस्य पाज इळायास्पुत्रो वयुनेऽजनिष्ट ॥ (uttānāyāmava bharā cikitvānssadyaḥ pravītā vṛṣaṇaṃ jajāna | aruṣastūpo ruśadasya pāja iḷāyāsputro vayune 'janiṣṭa ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-29-3) in this Ṛk Agni is also called the son of Iḷā.

Bhāratī—In the Nirukta it is said to be the radiance of Āditya (भरतः आदित्यः तस्य भाः (bharataḥ ādityaḥ tasya bhāḥ)). The scholar Macdonell, in his work Vedic Mythology (p. 87), explains it as the oblation offered by the descendants of Bharata, and Grassmann as the goddess of speech. Or it may be explained as belonging to Agni. तस्मा अग्निर्भारतः शर्म यंसज्यो र्क्षश्यात्सूर्यमुच्चरंतं । य इंद्राय सुनवामेत्याह नरे नर्याय नृतमाय नृणां । (tasmā agnirbhārataḥ śarma yaṃsajyo rkṣaśyātsūryamuccaraṃtaṃ | ya iṃdrāya sunavāmetyāha nare naryāya nṛtamāya nṛṇāṃ |) (Muṃ. Saṃ. 4-25-4) NOTE In this Ṛk, since bhāratah is an epithet of Agni, some hold that the deity related to him may be named Bhāratī.

Sarasvatī—सर इत्युदकनाम । तद्वती स्तनितादिरूपा माध्यमिका च वाक् । (sara ityudakanāma | tadvatī stanitādirūpā mādhyamikā ca vāk |) The word sara means water. Sāyaṇa explains her as a transformation of the goddess of speech of the atmosphere, who has water and has the sound of thunder and the like. Some hold that Sarasvatī is a river that is divine in nature. Or, because it is said देव्यस्ति स्रः श्रिताश्चैनं (devyasti sraḥ śritāścainaṃ) (Bṛ. De. 1-108), that these three have resorted to Agni; because Agni exists in three forms in earth, atmosphere and heaven; because Bhāratī is said to be the radiance of the sun; because Sarasvatī is said to be the deity of lightning and thunderbolt; and because Iḷā too has a direct connection with Agni, some hold that these three are transformations of Agni. That तद्रूपमग्निं (tadrūpamagniṃ) occurs in the explanation of the Praiṣa-sūkta has been said above.

Grammar
  • अर्पिता — उंभादीनां च (पा. सू. ६-१-१६०) इति अमृतात्तस्करो भवति । NOTE
  • इळा — ईड स्तुतौ धातुः । छांदसत्वेन धातोः प्रस्वो भवति । क्विप् च इति क्विप् प्रत्ययः । धातुस्वरो भवति । टापंचैव हलंतानां यथा वाचा दिरा निशा (कौ. २-४-८२) इति हलंतत्वेऽपि टाप् भवति ।
  • सरस्वती — सृ गत् धातुः । असुन् प्रत्ययः । सरस्‌शब्दो नित् प्रत्ययांतत्वात् आद्युदात्तो भवति । सरः अस्या अस्ति इति । तदस्यास्ति—इति मतुप् प्रत्ययः । तसौ म

p. 267

  • त्वर्थे (पा. सू. १-४-१९) इति भसंज्ञात्वात् रुत्वादयो न भवंति । उगितश्च (पा. सू. ४-१-६) इति स्त्रीत्वविवक्षायां जीप्—मतुप्, जीप् पित्त्वात् अनुदात्तो भवति ।
  • मही — महती इत्यत्र छांदसत्वेन तकारलोपो भवति । यस्येति च—(पा. सू. ६-४-१४८) इति अकारलोपः । उदात्तनिवृत्तिस्वरेण जीप् उदात्तो भवति ।
  • सीदंतु — षदलृ विशरणगत्यवसादनेषु धातुः । लोट् प्रथमपुरुषबहुवचने झि प्रत्ययः । एरुः इति उत्वं । अंतादेशः । साघ्राध्मा—(पा. सू. ३-३-७८) इति धातोः सीदादेशः । अतिजंतस्य परत्वात् निघातस्वरो भवति ।
  • यज्ञियाः — यज्ञर्त्विग्भ्यां घखञ् (पा.सू. ५-१-७१) इति अर्हार्थे घ प्रत्ययः । आयनेयी—(पा. सू. ७-१-२) इति तस्य इयादेशः । यस्येति च इति अकारलोपः । प्रत्ययस्य आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति । ॥ ९ ॥

Ṛk 10

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

तन्न॑स्तु॒रीप॒मद्भु॑तं पु॒रु वारं॑ पु॒रु त्मना॑ ।
त्वष्टा॒ पोषा॑य॒ वि ष्य॑तु रा॒ये नाभा॑ नो अस्म॒युः ॥ १० ॥

tannasturīpamadbhutaṃ puru vāraṃ puru tmanā | tvaṣṭā poṣāya vi ṣyatu rāye nābhā no asmayuḥ ‖ 10 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

तत् । नः । पुरीपं । अद्भुतं । पुरु । वा । अरं । पुरु । त्मना ।
त्वष्टा । पोषाय । वि । स्यतु । राये । नाभा । नः । अस्मयुः ॥ १० ॥

tat | naḥ | purīpaṃ | adbhutaṃ | puru | vā | araṃ | puru | tmanā | tvaṣṭā | poṣāya | vi | syatu | rāye | nābhā | naḥ | asmayuḥ ‖ 10 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

नोऽस्मदर्थं तत्तादृशं तुरीपं तूर्णं व्याप्यद्भुतं सद्य आविर्भवदभूतमिव सत् । यद्वा । महन्ना मैतत् । सारतो महत् । पुरु वारं बहूनां प्राणिनामर्थायैवारमलं समर्थं । यद्वा । पुरु वारं बहु प्रभूतं च । वाशब्दश्चार्थे ।

Gist of the bhāṣya

"For us" (नः (naḥ)); तत् (tat) is "of that kind"; तुरीपं (turīpaṃ) is swiftly pervading; अद्भुतं (adbhutaṃ) is that which, being manifested at once, is as if it had not been (abhūtamiva sat). Or else: महन्ना मैतत् (mahannā maitat), "great in essence" (सारतो महत् (sārato mahat)) NOTE. पुरु वारं (puru vāraṃ): बहूनां प्राणिनामर्थायैवारमलं समर्थं (bahūnāṃ prāṇināmarthāyaivāramalaṃ samarthaṃ), that is, capable, for the sake of many living beings. Or else: पुरु वारं (puru vāraṃ) is much and abundant, the word वा (vā) being in the sense of "and" (च (ca)).

p. 268

अरं अलं । त्मनात्मना पुरु । बहुक्रियानिशेषणमेतत् । ईदृशमुदकं त्वष्टा वृष्ट्यादेः कर्ता । त्वष्टशब्दो यास्केनैवं व्याख्यातः । तृष्णा तूर्णमश्नुत इति नैरुक्तास्विषेर्वा स्याद्वृद्धिकर्मणस्त्वक्षतीर्वा स्यात्करोतिकर्मणः । नि. ८-१३ । इति । तन्नामको वैद्युतोऽग्निरस्मयुरस्मान्यामयमानो देवो नः पोषायास्मत्तुष्टये राये समृद्धये च नाभा नाभौ वृष्टेबंधके मेघस्यनाभिस्थानेऽवस्थितमुक्तलक्षणमुदकं वि ष्यतु । विविधं गमयतु ॥ षोऽंतकर्मणि । ओतः श्यनीत्योकारलोपः । उपसर्गात्सुनोतीति षत्वं ॥ यद्वा । नो नाभास्मत्संबंधियज्ञनाभावुत्तरवेद्यां राये ॥ षष्ठ्यर्थे चतुर्थी ॥ रायो गवादिधनस्य पोषाय पुष्टये ॥ स्यतिरुपसृष्टो विमोचनार्थः ॥ उक्तलक्षणां वृष्टिं मुंचतु ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

The block completes the gloss begun on the previous page. अरं (araṃ) means "enough" (अलं (alaṃ)). त्मना (tmanā) means "by itself". पुरु (puru) is an adverb of much action. Water of this kind is made by Tvaṣṭṛ, the maker of rain and the like. Yāska explains त्वष्ट (tvaṣṭa) in the Nirukta (Ni. 8-13): the Nirukta writers say he "quickly pervades"; or the word may come from the root त्विष् (tviṣ) (to grow), or from त्वक्ष (tvakṣa) (to make). The deity so named is the lightning Agni, "desirous of us" (अस्मयुः (asmayuḥ)), who, for our nourishment (पोषाय (poṣāya)) and prosperity (राये (rāye)), is to send forth variously (वि ष्यतु (vi ṣyatu)) the water of the stated kind that stands नाभा (nābhā), in the navel, the place that holds the rain, the centre of the cloud. ष्यतु (ṣyatu) is from the root षो (ṣo) (to end); the ओ (o) is dropped, and the ष (ṣa) comes after the preposition. Alternatively: नाभा (nābhā) is the navel of our sacrifice, the northern altar; राये (rāye) is a dative used for the genitive, "of wealth such as cattle", पोषाय (poṣāya) "for the increase". The verb स्यतु (syatu) with the preposition has the sense of release: "let him release the rain of the stated kind".

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • त्वष्टा (tvaṣṭā)—Agni, maker of rain in the form of lightning
  • अस्मयुः (asmayuḥ)—being favourably disposed towards us
  • नः (naḥ)—our
  • पोषाय (poṣāya)—for nourishment
  • राये (rāye)—for prosperity
  • नाभा (nābhā)—from the central part of the cloud. (Or: नः (naḥ)—our; नाभा (nābhā)—on the northern altar, the navel of the sacrifice; राये (rāye)—for wealth such as cattle; पोषाय (poṣāya)—for protection)
  • नः (naḥ)—for us
  • तत् (tat)—that well-known
  • तुरीपं (turīpaṃ)—swiftly falling
  • अद्भुतं (adbhutaṃ)—wonderful
  • पुरुवारं (puruvāraṃ)—sufficient for many creatures, or very abundant
  • त्मना पुरु (tmanā puru)—the rain that of itself does much good
  • वि ष्यतु (vi ṣyatu)—let him pour down in various ways
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Agni in the form of lightning, favourably disposed towards us, pour down abundantly, for our nourishment and for our prosperity, from the middle of the cloud, that well-known rain, swiftly falling, wonderful, sufficient for many creatures and very abundant.

Printed English

May Twashtri, favourably disposed towards us, send to us, for our nourishment and prosperity, the quick (falling) wonderful, abundant (water), in the centre (of the cloud, effecting) of itself much (good).

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

त्वष्टा (tvaṣṭā)—The Praiṣa-sūkta describes him as "Tvaṣṭṛ, the deity of the ninth Prayāja". In the Praiṣa-sūkta the nature of this deity is shown by four or five epithets.

p. 269

Among the śruti passages giving individual opinions about the deity Tvaṣṭṛ, the following, which refer to the deity of the Āprī-sūkta alone, are quoted: होतायक्षत्त्वष्टारमचिष्टुमपाकग्ं रेतोधां विश्रवसं यशोधां । पुरुरूपमकामकर्शनग्ं सुपोषः पोपैः स्यात्सुवीरो वीरैर्वेत्वाज्यस्य होतरज । (hotāyakṣattvaṣṭāramaciṣṭumapākagṃ retodhāṃ viśravasaṃ yaśodhāṃ | pururūpamakāmakarśanagṃ supoṣaḥ popaiḥ syātsuvīro vīrairvetvājyasya hotaraja |) (Tai. Brā. 3-6-2-2) In this mantra there are the epithets अचिष्टु (aciṣṭu), अपाकं (apākaṃ), रेतोधां (retodhāṃ), विश्रवसं (viśravasaṃ), यशोधां (yaśodhāṃ), पुरुरूपं (pururūpaṃ), अकामकर्शनं (akāmakarśanaṃ). Among them: अचिष्टुं (aciṣṭuṃ) means "without agitation, without fickleness, steady": one who is steady, not fickle. अपाकं (apākaṃ) means "not a child, wise": not a child but wise. रेतोधां (retodhāṃ) is explained as पुत्रादिबीजस्य यजमाने धारयितारं (putrādibījasya yajamāne dhārayitāraṃ): one who sows the seed of sons and the like in the sacrificer. विश्रवसं (viśravasaṃ) is explained as विविधकीर्तियुक्तं (vividhakīrtiyuktaṃ): endowed with fame of many kinds. यशोधां (yaśodhāṃ) means यजमाने य.शसः धारयितारं (yajamāne ya.śasaḥ dhārayitāraṃ): one who makes the sacrificer a sharer in fame. पुरुरूपं (pururūpaṃ) is explained as बहुरूपं (bahurūpaṃ): having forms of many kinds. अकामकर्शनं (akāmakarśanaṃ) means कामानां अनाशयितारं (kāmānāṃ anāśayitāraṃ): one who brings the sacrificer's desired ends to fulfilment. These epithets show the personal nature of Tvaṣṭṛ. The Nirukta writers, showing the derivation of the word त्वष्ट (tvaṣṭa) (8-14): त्वष्टा तूर्णमश्नुत इति नैरुक्ताः । त्विषेर्वा स्याद्दीप्तिकमणस्त्वक्षतेर्वा स्यात् करोटिकर्मणः । (tvaṣṭā tūrṇamaśnuta iti nairuktāḥ | tviṣervā syāddīptikamaṇastvakṣatervā syāt karoṭikarmaṇaḥ |) It is the view of the Nirukta writers that the name is because he pervades swiftly; or it may be formed from the root त्विष् (tviṣ) meaning "to shine", or from the root त्वक्ष (tvakṣa) meaning "to make". From these explanations it is understood that Tvaṣṭṛ is one who pervades swiftly, who shines, and who is a maker. To show to which world this deity belongs: माध्यमिकस्त्वष्टेत्याहुर्मध्यमे च स्थाने समाम्नातः । अग्निरिति शाकपूणि (mādhyamikastvaṣṭetyāhurmadhyame ca sthāne samāmnātaḥ | agniriti śākapūṇi). The views are given that some say he belongs to the group of deities of the atmosphere, and Śākapūṇi says he is Agni. In the Bṛhaddevatā, approving the first view,

p. 270

त्वष्टा रूपविकर्ता च योऽसौ माध्यमिके गणे । स्तुतः स च निपातेन सूक्तं तस्य न विद्यते ॥ (tvaṣṭā rūpavikartā ca yo 'sau mādhyamike gaṇe | stutaḥ sa ca nipātena sūktaṃ tasya na vidyate ‖) (Bṛ. De. 3-25) this verse says that he belongs to the group of deities of the middle world. Before this: त्वष्टा तु यस्त्वयमेव पार्थिवोऽग्निरिति स्तुतिः । पार्थिवस्यास्य वर्चः स्युः कस्याप्यक् चार्तवेषु च ॥ श्वषितस्त्वक्षतेर्वा स्यात् तूर्णमश्नुत एव वा । कर्मसूत्तारणो वेति तेन नामैतदश्नुते ॥ यः सहस्रतमो रश्मी रवेश्चंद्रमुपाश्रितः । सोऽपि त्वष्टारमेवाग्निं परं चेह च यन्मधु ॥ (tvaṣṭā tu yastvayameva pārthivo 'gniriti stutiḥ | pārthivasyāsya varcaḥ syuḥ kasyāpyak cārtaveṣu ca ‖ śvaṣitastvakṣatervā syāt tūrṇamaśnuta eva vā | karmasūttāraṇo veti tena nāmaitadaśnute ‖ yaḥ sahasratamo raśmī raveścaṃdramupāśritaḥ | so 'pi tvaṣṭāramevāgniṃ paraṃ ceha ca yanmadhu ‖) (Bṛ. De. 3-15 to 17) The praise that is for the terrestrial Agni is addressed to Tvaṣṭṛ also; there is also a suggestion in some places that he is a deity connected with the earth; in the hymns to the seasons too he is described as a part of Agni. Then the derivation of the word त्वष्ट (tvaṣṭa) in the Nirukta is repeated. It is also described that the thousandth ray of the sun, resting on the moon, pervades in honey, in the other world and on the earth, and is likewise in Tvaṣṭṛ. The authors of the Bṛhaddevatā, mainly, approve in this matter Śākapūṇi's view stated in the Nirukta. In the Nighaṇṭu Tvaṣṭṛ is placed first with the Āprī deities (5-2), then with the deities of the atmosphere (5-5), and thirdly with the deities of the heavenly world (5-6). The story of Tvaṣṭṛ and the sage Dadhīci is given in the special topics of Sūkta 1-139. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa: त्वष्टारं यजति वाग्वै त्वष्टा वाग्फिदं सर्वं । त्वाष्ट्रीं वाचमेव तत्प्रीणाति वाचं यजमाने दधाति । (tvaṣṭāraṃ yajati vāgvai tvaṣṭā vāgphidaṃ sarvaṃ | tvāṣṭrīṃ vācameva tatprīṇāti vācaṃ yajamāne dadhāti |) (Ai. Brā. 2-4) By this sentence, the identity of Tvaṣṭṛ with Speech is stated; this too is one view. य इमे द्यावापृथिवी जनित्रि रूपैरपिंशद्भवनानि विश्वा । तमद्य होतरिषितो यजीयान् देवं त्वष्टारमिह यक्षि विद्वान् । (ya ime dyāvāpṛthivī janitri rūpairapiṃśadbhavanāni viśvā | tamadya hotariṣito yajīyān devaṃ tvaṣṭāramiha yakṣi vidvān |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-9) In this Ṛk it is praised that this deity has a divine birth, and that therefore even at the times of creation he shows his antiquity. The idea that Tvaṣṭṛ is most ancient

p. 271

is known from the epithets अग्रिय (agriya) and अग्रज (agraja) in the Ṛks: इह त्वष्टारमग्रियं विश्वरूपमुपद्वये । अस्माकमस्तु केवलः ॥ (iha tvaṣṭāramagriyaṃ viśvarūpamupadvaye | asmākamastu kevalaḥ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-13-10) त्वष्टारमग्रजां गोपां पुरोयानानमा हुवे । इंदुरिंद्रो वृषा हरिः पवमानः प्रजापतिः ॥ (tvaṣṭāramagrajāṃ gopāṃ puroyānānamā huve | iṃduriṃdro vṛṣā hariḥ pavamānaḥ prajāpatiḥ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-5 9) NOTE त्वष्टा रूपाणि हि प्रभुः पशून्विश्वान्स्मानजे । तेषां नः स्नातिमा यज । (tvaṣṭā rūpāṇi hi prabhuḥ paśūnviśvānsmānaje | teṣāṃ naḥ snātimā yaja |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-188-9) तृप्ता रूपाणि विकरोति । (tṛptā rūpāṇi vikaroti |) (Tai. Saṃ. 1-5-9-2) Such passages praise the work of creation of Tvaṣṭṛ. Moreover he has the epithet "of all forms" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-13-10). तुरीपं (turīpaṃ)—If only the etymology of the word तुरीप (turīpa) is considered, it means तूर्णं व्यापि (tūrṇaṃ vyāpi), "that which pervades swiftly"; that is, falling or pervading swiftly. According to the commentator it may be rain or it may be seed. In this Ṛk the commentator has made the word an epithet of rain. But तन्न स्तुरीपमध पोषयित्नु देव त्वष्टर्वि रराणः स्यस्व । यतो वीरः कर्मण्यः सुदक्षो युक्तग्रावा जायते देवकामः ॥ (tanna sturīpamadha poṣayitnu deva tvaṣṭarvi rarāṇaḥ syasva | yato vīraḥ karmaṇyaḥ sudakṣo yuktagrāvā jāyate devakāmaḥ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-4-9) in this Ṛk the word तुरीप (turīpa) is explained as generative seed. Since in the Praiṣa-sūkta the epithet रेतोधां (retodhāṃ) states a special quality of Tvaṣṭṛ, this meaning appears sound. त्वष्टे स्वाहा, त्वष्टे पुरीपाय स्वाहा, त्वष्टे पुरुरूपाय स्वाहा । (tvaṣṭe svāhā, tvaṣṭe purīpāya svāhā, tvaṣṭe pururūpāya svāhā |) (Kṛ. Saṃ. 7-3-15) NOTE In this Saṃhitā passage too, where the identity of Tvaṣṭṛ and तुरीप (turīpa) is stated, the word is explained as seed. The scholar Keith explains this mantra as "To Tvashtra, the Seminal". Or, since he is a deity of the middle world, he may be called the cause of the fall of rain.

p. 272

Grammar
  • अरम् — वालमूल-(पा. सू. ८-२-१८) इति लकारस्य रेफादेशः । अलं इति स्वरूपम् ।
  • त्मना — आत्मना इति रूपे मंत्रेष्वाज्यादेरात्मनः (पा सू. ६-४-१४१) इति अवर्णस्य लोपो भवति ।
  • त्वष्वा — त्वष दीप्तौ धातुः । अथवा त्वक्षू तनूकरणे धातुः । तस्मात् कर्तरि तृन् प्रत्ययः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति । स्कोःसंयोगाद्योरंतेच इति ककारस्य लोपः । प्रथमाएकवचनांतरूपम् ।
  • पोषाय — पुष पुष्टौ धातुः । हलश्च (पा. सू. ३-३-१२१) इति घ् प्रत्ययः । पुगंतलघूपधस्यच (पा. सू. ७-३-८६) इति धातोर्लघूपधस्य गुणः । प्रत्ययस्य इत्त्वादाद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति । चतुर्थीविकवचनांतरूपम् । NOTE
  • वि ष्यतु — षोंतकर्मणि धातुः । लोट् प्रथमपुरुषएकवचने ति प्रत्ययः । एरः इति उत्वम् । दिवादिभ्यःश्यन् इति श्यन् विकरणम् । ओतः श्यसि (पा. सू. ७-३-२१) इति धातोरोकारस्य लोपः । धात्वादेःषः सः (पा. सू. ६-१-६४) इति आदेः सत्वम् । स्यतु इति रूपं भवति । वि इत्युपसर्गे निमित्तसत्त्वात् उपसर्गात् सुनोति—(पा. सू. ८-३-६५) इति धातुसकारस्य षत्वम् । अतिजंतस्य परत्वात् तिजंतनिघातस्वरो भवति । द्वितीयव्याख्याने उपसर्गेण धात्वर्थः बलादन्यः प्रतीयते इति वचनात् वि उपसर्गयोगे विमोचनार्थं ददाति ।
  • राये — रै शब्दः । चतुर्थीएकवचनांतरूपम् । ऊडिदं पदादि—(पा. सू ६-१-१७१) इति विभक्तेरुदात्तस्वरो भवति । द्वितीयव्याख्याने षष्ठ्यर्थे चतुर्थी आगता । नाभा सुपां सुलुक् (पा. सू. ७-१-३९) इति विभक्तेः डादेशः । वित्त्वात् टिलोपः ।
  • अस्मयुः — आस्मान् आत्मनः इच्छति इत्यर्थविवक्षायां सुप आत्मनः क्यच् (पा. सू. ३-१-८) इति इच्छार्थे क्यच् । क्याच्छंदसि (पा. सू. ३-२-१७०) इति क्यजंतादुप्रत्ययः । अतो लोपः (पा. सू. ६-४-४८) इति सूत्रादकारलोपः । प्रत्ययस्वरेणांतोदात्तो भवति । ॥ १० ॥

p. 273

Ṛk 11

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

अ॒व॒सृ॒जन्नुप॒ त्मना॑ दे॒वान्य॑क्षि वनस्पते ।
अ॒ग्निर्ह॒व्या सु॑षूदति दे॒वो दे॒वेषु॒ मेधि॑रः ॥ ११ ॥

avasṛjannupa tmanā devānyakṣi vanaspate | agnirhavyā suṣūdati devo deveṣu medhiraḥ ‖ 11 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

अव्यसृजन् । उप । त्मना । देवान् । यक्षि । वनस्पते ।
अग्निः । हव्या । सुसूदति । देवः । देवेषु । मेधिरः ॥ ११ ॥

avyasṛjan | upa | tmanā | devān | yakṣi | vanaspate | agniḥ | havyā | susūdati | devaḥ | deveṣu | medhiraḥ ‖ 11 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे वनस्पते वनानां पालक यूपाभिमानिदेवाग्ने अवसृजन् स्वैरं वर्तयन्नृत्विजः स्वस्वकर्मसु व्यापारयन् त्मनात्मना देवान्हविर्भुज उप यक्षि । उपेत्य यज ॥ बहुलं छंदसीति शपो लुक् ॥ देवो द्योतमानो मेधिरो मेधावानग्निराहवनीयो देवेषूभयेषां मध्यॆ हव्या हवींषि सुसूदति । प्रेरयति । स्वीकरोति ॥ षूद क्षरणे । बहुलं छंदसीति शपः श्लुः । लेटोऽडाटावित्यडागमः ॥ यद्वा । यूपाग्निरेव परोक्षेणोच्यते । सोऽग्निर्हवींषि सुष्टु स्वीकरोति ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Vanaspati, protector of woods, Agni who presides over the sacrificial post: sending forth (अवसृजन् (avasṛjan)), that is, moving freely, setting the priests to their several duties, do you of yourself (त्मना (tmanā)) come to the gods, the eaters of the oblation, and sacrifice (उप यक्षि (upa yakṣi), "approach and sacrifice")." यक्षि (yakṣi) has the loss of śap (by बहुलं छंदसीति (bahulaṃ chaṃdasīti)). The shining (देवः (devaḥ)), wise (मेधिरः (medhiraḥ)) Agni, the Āhavanīya, among both sets of gods (देवेषु (deveṣu)), सुसूदति (susūdati) the oblations (हव्या (havyā)): he sends them on, or accepts them. The root is षूद (ṣūda) in the sense of flowing; śap is replaced by श्लु (ślu), and leṭ takes the augment aḍ. Or else: the Agni of the sacrificial post is meant indirectly; that Agni well accepts the oblations.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • वनस्पते (vanaspate)—O Agni, the deity presiding over the sacrificial post
  • अवसृज (avasṛja)—setting (the priests) to their several duties
  • त्मना (tmanā)—you yourself (coming)
  • देर्वा (dervā)—the gods
  • उप (upa)—approaching
  • यक्षि (yakṣi)—perform the sacrifice
  • देवः (devaḥ)—shining
  • मेधिरः (medhiraḥ)—wise
  • अग्निः (agniḥ)—Agni
  • देवेषु (deveṣu)—among the gods
  • हव्या (havyā)—the oblations
  • सुसूदति (susūdati)—accepts. Or: distributes the oblations among the gods
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, the deity presiding over the sacrificial post, setting the priests to their several duties, come of yourself to the house of sacrifice and perform the sacrifice for the gods. The shining and wise Agni accepts the oblation in order to distribute it to the gods.

p. 274

Printed English

Vanaspati, here present of your own accord, convey our offerings to the gods; the divine and intelligent Agni accepts (the oblations) for the deities.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

वनस्पते (vanaspate)—What the true nature of Vanaspati is must be understood after much investigation. On the basis of this word some modern Western scholars have concluded that the violent animal sacrifice was prevalent in the Vedic period, and that the Āprī hymns are the Prayāja mantras connected with such a sacrifice.

Viewed superficially, Vanaspati means the sacrificial post (yūpa) to which the sacrificial animal is tied. But on the question whether it is really the post that binds the sacrificial animal, one may first examine the Śruti passages and then determine the nature of Vanaspati on their basis.

In the Praiṣa hymn, for the mantra होता यक्षद्वनस्पतिमुपावस्रक्षद्धियो जोष्टारग्ं शशमं नरः। स्वदात्स्वधितिर्युतुथाद्य देवो देवेभ्यो हव्यावाड्वेत्वाज्यस्य होतरज । (hotā yakṣadvanaspatimupāvasrakṣaddhiyo joṣṭāragṃ śaśamaṃ naraḥ| svadātsvadhitiryututhādya devo devebhyo havyāvāḍvetvājyasya hotaraja |) (Tai. Brā. 3 6-2 2) the commentary runs thus: वनस्पतिं यूपाधारभूतं दशमप्रयाजदेवतात्मकमग्निं दैव्यो होता यजतु (vanaspatiṃ yūpādhārabhūtaṃ daśamaprayājadevatātmakamagniṃ daivyo hotā yajatu). That is: Vanaspati is the support of the yūpa and is Agni, who is the deity of the tenth Prayāja; let the Hotṛ sacrifice to him. Vanaspati has the epithets धियो जोष्टा (dhiyo joṣṭā), स्वदात् स्वधितिः (svadāt svadhitiḥ), देवेभ्यः ऋतुधा हव्यवाह् (devebhyaḥ ṛtudhā havyavāh), यज्ञस्य आयुः कल्पमानः (yajñasya āyuḥ kalpamānaḥ). Among these epithets, धियो जोष्टा (dhiyo joṣṭā) is explained as बुद्धेः प्रीणयितारं (buddheḥ prīṇayitāraṃ), "one who gladdens the intellect"; स्वधितिः (svadhitiḥ) means "one fashioned by the svadhiti (the thunderbolt, or) divine weapon"; for ऋतुथा (ṛtuthā) the gloss given is ऋत् विहिते कालविशेषे आद्य अस्मिन्कर्मणि स्वदादस्माभिर्दीयमानं हविः स्वदयतु । किंच देवो वनस्पतिर्देवेभ्यो देवार्थं हव्याहवींष्यवाड्वहतु (ṛt vihite kālaviśeṣe ādya asminkarmaṇi svadādasmābhirdīyamānaṃ haviḥ svadayatu | kiṃca devo vanaspatirdevebhyo devārthaṃ havyāhavīṃṣyavāḍvahatu)NOTE. The sense of the mantra is: "at the time of this sacrifice let him offer to the gods the oblations offered by us." And by the epithet यज्ञस्य आयुः कल्पमानः (yajñasya āyuḥ kalpamānaḥ) the meaning is "one who prolongs the life of the sacrifice." By such epithets the Praiṣa hymn states the identity of Agni and Vanaspati. The Aitareya Brāhmaṇa points to it by the sentence प्राणो वै वनस्पतिः (prāṇo vai vanaspatiḥ) (2-4). The author of the Nirukta first gives the etymology of the word Vanaspati and then, in dealing with the Āprī hymn,

p. 275

explains what the nature of Vanaspati is. In explaining Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-37-3, showing the etymology of the word Vanaspati found in it (Ni. 8-3), he says वनानां पाता ना पालयिता वा । वनं वनोतेः (vanānāṃ pātā nā pālayitā vā | vanaṃ vanoteḥ): Agni is famed as Vanaspati either because he is lord of the forests or because he is their protector, and the word is formed from the root van, which gives the sense "to obtain". Then, discussing the nature of the deities of the Āprī hymn (8-18), he states two opinions: तत् को वनस्पतिः, यूस इति कात्मक्यः अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः । (tat ko vanaspatiḥ, yūsa iti kātmakyaḥ agniriti śākapūṇiḥ |), and in support of the view of Kātthakya he cites the Ṛk अंजंति त्वामध्वरे देवयंतो वनस्पते मधुना दैव्येन । यदूर्ध्वस्तिष्ठा द्रविणेह धत्ताद्यद्वा क्षयो मातुरस्या उपस्थे । (aṃjaṃti tvāmadhvare devayaṃto vanaspate madhunā daivyena | yadūrdhvastiṣṭhā draviṇeha dhattādyadvā kṣayo māturasyā upasthe |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-8-1). In this Ṛk Sāyaṇa has addressed the word Vanaspati as the yūpa itself. Then, to support the view of Śākapūṇi, the author of the Nirukta cites the Ṛk वनस्पते रशनया नियूया देवानां पाथ उप वक्षि विद्वान् । स्वदाति देवः कृणवद्वनींष्यवतां द्यावापृथिवी हवं मे ॥ (vanaspate raśanayā niyūyā devānāṃ pātha upa vakṣi vidvān | svadāti devaḥ kṛṇavadvanīṃṣyavatāṃ dyāvāpṛthivī havaṃ me ‖) (10-70-1) (10-20-10)NOTE. Sāyaṇa has explained this too as the yūpa; but the view of the author of the Nirukta is that it is the Agni within the yūpa. Durgācārya, explaining this Ṛk in the Nirukta, says: एवमग्निर्वनस्पतिः । यत् पुनरेतदुक्तं यूपांजनीयायां ' यूपे वनस्पतिशब्दः ' इति । अत्र ब्रूमः—अग्नि रेवासौ यूपांतर्गतो यूपात्मना वर्तमानो यूपांजनीयायां वनस्पतिशब्देनोच्यते । (evamagnirvanaspatiḥ | yat punaretaduktaṃ yūpāṃjanīyāyāṃ ' yūpe vanaspatiśabdaḥ ' iti | atra brūmaḥ—agni revāsau yūpāṃtargato yūpātmanā vartamāno yūpāṃjanīyāyāṃ vanaspatiśabdenocyate |). Here he has established that Vanaspati means Agni who is within the yūpa and nothing else. The author of the Bṛhaddevatā says: वनस्पतिं तु यं प्राहुरयं सोग्निर्वनस्पतिः । अयं वनानां हि पतिः पाता पालयतीति ना ॥ अग्निर्गृत्समदेनायं वनस्पतिरितीळितः । मंदस्वेत्यस्य सूक्तस्य षळ्यचस्य तृतीयया ॥ यूपवत्तरुवच्चैव स्तुतिर्यास्य प्रसंगजा । सर्वॆणांजति सूक्तेन तृतीये सा तु मंडले ॥ (vanaspatiṃ tu yaṃ prāhurayaṃ sognirvanaspatiḥ | ayaṃ vanānāṃ hi patiḥ pātā pālayatīti nā ‖ agnirgṛtsamadenāyaṃ vanaspatiritīḷitaḥ | maṃdasvetyasya sūktasya ṣaḷyacasya tṛtīyayā ‖ yūpavattaruvaccaiva stutiryāsya prasaṃgajā | sarvèṇāṃjati sūktena tṛtīye sā tu maṃḍale ‖) (Bṛ. De. 3-26 to 28)

p. 276

By these statements he discusses the nature of the Āprī deity addressed in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-13-11, and shows that Vanaspati here means the terrestrial Agni; that in Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-37-2 Gṛtsamada too has addressed this same terrestrial Agni by the word Vanaspati; and that only in some Ṛks of the third maṇḍala does it mean the yūpa or a tree, and that too only incidentally. Besides this, इहैष पवमानोग्निर्मध्यमोग्निर्वनस्पतिः । अमुष्मिन्नेव विप्रैस्तु लोकेग्निश्युचिरुच्यते ॥ (ihaiṣa pavamānognirmadhyamognirvanaspatiḥ | amuṣminneva vipraistu lokegniśyucirucyate ‖) (Bṛ. De. 7-66) shows that Vanaspati there means the Agni of the middle world; and he has determined that, except in a few places of the Ṛksaṃhitā, in the many other places this word indicates Agni, and that there is no doubt about it.

In the Ṛk 10-70-10 cited above, by रशनया नियूय देवानां उपवक्षि । (raśanayā niyūya devānāṃ upavakṣi |) the prayer "bind the oblation firmly and carry it to the gods" cannot possibly be addressed to the yūpa; nor is there any room to explain it as "bind and unbind the sacrificial animal". Moreover, even on a careful examination of all the Āprī hymns, no Ṛk anywhere refers to a sacrificial animal. And in the Ṛks 1-13-11, 2-3-10 and 3-2-10 the offering into the sacrifice is called havis; in the present hymn havya; in 1-188-10 and 5-5-10 havyāni; in the Ṛks 10-70-10 and 10-110-10 havīṃṣi—it is indicated by the common word applied to offerings of ghee and the like, and the offering is nowhere indicated by a word connected with offerings of animals and the like.

As for the use of the word śamitā in support of explaining Vanaspati as yūpa: in ordinary usage this word means "one who kills, destroys". Apart from the Āprī hymns this word is used in four Ṛks of the Ṛksaṃhitā. In Ṛks 1-162-9 and 10 it has the common meaning of cutting; in 5-43-4 it means cutting the soma plant, and in 5-85-1 it is merely a simile, a cobbler cutting leather. Nowhere is this word used as a synonym of the animal-slayer who lives by cutting up animals. Besides, if we take the very examples from the Āprī hymns in which this word is used: वनस्पतिरवसृजन्नुपस्थादग्निर्हविः सूदयाति प्र धीभिः । त्रिधा समःकं नयतु प्रजानन्वेवेभ्यो दैव्यः शमितोप हव्यं । (vanaspatiravasṛjannupasthādagnirhaviḥ sūdayāti pra dhībhiḥ | tridhā samaḥkaṃ nayatu prajānanvevebhyo daivyaḥ śamitopa havyaṃ |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-3-12)

p. 277
