in this Ṛk śamitā means हविषः संस्कर्ता, यद्वा दैव्यः शमितैतन्नामकोऽग्निः । अग्निर्वै देवानां शमिता इति श्रूयते । (haviṣaḥ saṃskartā, yadvā daivyaḥ śamitaitannāmako 'gniḥ | agnirvai devānāṃ śamitā iti śrūyate |)—a word synonymous with Agni; and in the Ṛk उपावसृज त्मन्या समंजन् देवानां पाथ ऋतुथा हवींषि । वनस्पतिः शमिता देवो अग्निः स्वदंतु हव्यं मधुना घृतेन ॥ (upāvasṛja tmanyā samaṃjan devānāṃ pātha ṛtuthā havīṃṣi | vanaspatiḥ śamitā devo agniḥ svadaṃtu havyaṃ madhunā ghṛtena ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-10) Sāyaṇa explains: शमिता एतन्नामकः देवः यद्वा शामित्रः अग्निः (śamitā etannāmakaḥ devaḥ yadvā śāmitraḥ agniḥ). Since Sāyaṇa explains it so, there is no room for taking śamitā here as "animal-slayer" and explaining the word Vanaspati as the yūpa-post to which the animal is tied.

अवसृजन् (avasṛjan)—स्वैरं वर्तयन् ऋत्विजः स्वस्वकर्मसु व्यापारयन् । (svairaṃ vartayan ṛtvijaḥ svasvakarmasu vyāpārayan |) The meaning is: setting the priests to their own duties.

Grammar
  • अवसृजन् — सृज विसर्गे इति धातुः । लडर्थे शतृप्रत्ययः । तुदादिभ्यः शः इत्यनेन श विकरणम् । जित्त्वात् गुणो न भवति । तिजि चोदात्तवति (पा. सू. ८-१-७१) इत्यनेन गतेः (अव) निघातस्वरो भवति ।
  • त्मना — आत्मना इत्यत्र मंत्रेष्वाज्यादेरात्मनः (पा. सू. ६-४-१४१) इत्यनेन आकारस्य लोपः ।
  • यक्षि — यज देवपूजासंगतिकरणदासेषु इति धातुः । भ्वादिः । लट् मध्यमपुरुषैकवचने सिप् । बहुलं छंदसि इत्यनेन विकरणस्य (शप्) लुक् । व्रश्चभृस्त्व (पा. सू. ८-२-३६) इत्यनेन जकारस्य षत्वम् । षथोःकःसि (पा सू. ८-२-४१) इत्यनेन तस्य कत्वम् । आदेशप्रत्यययोः (पा. सू. ८-३-५९) इत्यनेन प्रत्ययसकारस्य षत्वम् । अतिजंतस्य परत्वान्निघातस्वरो भवति ।
  • वनस्पते — पारस्कर प्रभृतीनि च संज्ञायाम् (पा. सू. ६-१-१५७) इत्यनेन सुट् सहितं निपातितम् । संबुद्धौ आमंत्रितस्यच (पा. सू. ८-१-१९) इत्यनेन निघातस्वरो भवति ।
  • हव्या — हव्यानि इति रूपे सति शेश्छंदसि बहुलम् (पा.सू. ६-१-७०) इत्यनेन शिलोपः ।
  • सुषूदति — सूद क्षरणे इति धातुः । लेट् प्रथमपुरुषैकवचने तिप् प्रत्ययः । बहुलं छंदसि (पा. सू. २-४-२३) इत्यनेन विकरणस्य (शप्) श्लु आदेशः । श्लु इत्यनेन धातु

p. 278

  • (सुषूदति इत्यस्य शेषः —) धातोर्द्वित्वम् । ह्रस्वः इत्यनेन अभ्यासस्य ह्रस्वः । लेटोऽडाट् (पा. सू. ३-४-९४) इत्यनेन प्रत्ययस्य अडागमः । अतिजंतस्य परत्वान्निघातस्वरो भवति ।
  • मेधिरः — मेधृ मेधाहिंसनयोः इति धातुः । अस्मादौणादिकः इरन् प्रत्ययः । इत्यादिर्नित्यम् (पा. सू. ६-१-१९३) इत्यनेन आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति ।

Ṛk 12

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

पू॒ष॒ण्वते॑ म॒रुत्व॑ते वि॒श्वदे॑वाय वा॒यवे॑ ।
स्वाहा॑ गाय॒त्रवे॑पसे ह॒व्यमिंद्रा॑य कर्तन ॥ १२ ॥

pūṣaṇvate marutvate viśvadevāya vāyave | svāhā gāyatravepase havyamiṃdrāya kartana ‖ 12 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

पूषण्वते । मरुत्वते । विश्वदेवाय । वायवे ।
स्वाहा । गायत्रवेपसे । हव्यं । इंद्राय । कर्तन ॥ १२ ॥

pūṣaṇvate | marutvate | viśvadevāya | vāyave | svāhā | gāyatravepase | havyaṃ | iṃdrāya | kartana ‖ 12 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

पूषण्वते पूष्णा तद्वते ॥ अनो नुडिति नुट् । ह्रस्वनुड्भ्यां मतुबिति मतुप उदात्तत्वं ॥ मरुत्वते मरुद्भिस्तद्वते विश्वदेवाय सर्वदेवसंघाय वायवे गमनशीलाय वायुदेवाय च तथा गायत्रवेपसे । वेप इति रूपनाम । गायत्रशब्द इतरसामोपलक्षणः । गायत्रं वेपो रूपं यस्य तादृशायेंद्राय हव्यं हविः प्रदातुं स्वाहा कर्तन । स्वाहाकारं कुरुत ऋत्विजः ॥ करोतेर्लोटि तप्तनप्तनथनाश्चति तनबादेशः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

पूषण्वते (pūṣaṇvate) means "one possessed of Pūṣan". The augment nuṭ comes (by the rule beginning अनो नुडिति नुट् (ano nuḍiti nuṭ)), and the affix matup takes the udātta (by ह्रस्वनुड्भ्यां मतुबिति (hrasvanuḍbhyāṃ matubiti)). मरुत्वते (marutvate): one possessed of the Maruts. विश्वदेवाय (viśvadevāya): the host of all the gods. वायवे (vāyave): Vāyu, the deity, who is of moving nature. Likewise गायत्रवेपसे (gāyatravepase): vepa is a word for "form"; the word gāyatra stands as an indicator for the other sāmans; Gāyatra is the form of him, so it is to Indra, such as he is. To give him the oblation (havya), perform the cry svāhā—the priests are to make the svāhā-utterance. The root kṛ in the imperative takes the substitute tana (by the rule तप्तनप्तनथनाश्चति (taptanaptanathanāścati)).

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • पूषण्वते (pūṣaṇvate)—united with the god Pūṣan
  • मरुत्वते (marutvate)—united with the Marut deities NOTE
  • विश्वदेवाय (viśvadevāya)—to the host of all the deities
  • वायवे (vāyave)—to the god Vāyu
  • गायत्रवेपसे (gāyatravepase)—who is in the form of Gāyatra
  • इंद्राय (iṃdrāya)—to Indra
  • हव्यं (havyaṃ)—to offer the oblation
  • स्वाहाकर्तन (svāhākartana)—perform the cry svāhā

p. 279

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Perform the cry svāhā in order to offer the oblation to the host of all the deities, united with the god Pūṣan and united with the Marut deities, and to the god Vāyu, and also to Indra who is in the form of Gāyatra.

Printed English

(Priests), present the oblation with Swaha to Indra, in the form of the Gayatra, along with Pushan and the Maruts; also the assembled gods, and to Vayu.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

गायत्रवेपसे (gāyatravepase)—वेप इति रूपनाम । गायत्रशब्दः इतरसामोपलक्षणः । गायत्रं वेप रूपं यस्य तादृशाय इंद्राय । (vepa iti rūpanāma | gāyatraśabdaḥ itarasāmopalakṣaṇaḥ | gāyatraṃ vepa rūpaṃ yasya tādṛśāya iṃdrāya |) Sāyaṇa has explained it as "to Indra who is in the form of Gāyatra". The purport is: one who is gratified by song, one who attains an excellent form through song. This same epithet, in the Ṛk आ त्वविद्य सबर्मघां हुवे गायत्रवेपसं । इंद्रं धेनुं सुदुघामन्या मिषमुरुधारामरंकृतं ॥ (ā tvavidya sabarmaghāṃ huve gāyatravepasaṃ | iṃdraṃ dhenuṃ sudughāmanyā miṣamurudhārāmaraṃkṛtaṃ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-1-10) conveys the nature of Indra. But there Sāyaṇa has made the word गायत्रवेपसं (gāyatravepasaṃ) an epithet of the word धेनुं (dhenuṃ) and explained it as प्रशस्यवेगां (praśasyavegāṃ), "having excessive speed". Some hold that it is correct only as an epithet of Indra. Just as in Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-2 38 the word गाथश्रवसं (gāthaśravasaṃ) is also an epithet of Indra and gives the sense गातव्ययशसं (gātavyayaśasaṃ), so here too the word गायत्रवेपसे (gāyatravepase) gives the same purport and is an epithet of IndraNOTE.

स्वाहा कर्तन (svāhā kartana)—स्वाहाकारं कुरुत । (svāhākāraṃ kuruta |) The particulars of these are explained in the next Ṛk.

Grammar
  • पूषण्वते — पूषा अस्य अस्ति इति पूषण्वान् । तदस्यास्ति इत्यनेन मतुप् प्रत्ययः । अनोनुट् इत्यनेन मतुप् परे नुटागमः । ह्रस्वनुड्भ्यं मतुप् (पा. सू.. ६-१-१७६) इत्यनेन मतुप उदात्तस्वरो भवति । चतुर्थीएकवचनांतरूपम् ।
  • विश्वदेवाय — विश्वे देवाः यस्य सः विश्वदेवः । बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या पूर्वपदम् (पा. सू. ६-२-१) इत्यनेन पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति ।

p. 280

  • गायत्रवेपसे — गायत्रं वेपः यस्य सः गायत्रवेपाः तस्मै गायत्रवेपसे । पूर्ववत् पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति । चतुर्थीएकवचनांतरूपम् ।
  • कर्तन — डुकृञ्करणे इति धातुः । लोट्‌मध्यमपुरुषबहुवचने थ प्रत्ययः । बहुलं छंदसि इत्यनेन विकरणस्य लुक् । तप्तनप्तनथनाश्च (पा. सू. ७-१-४५) इत्यनेन प्रत्ययस्य तनबादेशः । इदं पित्त्वात् सार्वधातुकार्थधातुकयोः इत्यनेन धातोरिको गुणः । अतिजंतस्य परत्वान्निघातस्वरो भवति ।

Ṛk 13

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

स्वाहा॑कृता॒न्या ग॒ह्युप॑ ह॒व्यानि॑ वी॒तये॑ ।
इंद्रा ग॑हि श्रु॒धी हवं॒ त्वां द॑वंते अध्व॒रे ॥ १३ ॥

svāhākṛtānyā gahyupa havyāni vītaye | iṃdrā gahi śrudhī havaṃ tvāṃ davaṃte adhvare ‖ 13 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

स्वाहाकृतानि । आ । गहि । उप । हव्यानि । वीतये ।
इंद्र । आ । गहि । श्रुधि । हवं । त्वां । हवंते । अध्वरे ॥ १३ ॥

svāhākṛtāni | ā | gahi | upa | havyāni | vītaye | iṃdra | ā | gahi | śrudhi | havaṃ | tvāṃ | havaṃte | adhvare ‖ 13 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे इंद्र स्वाहाकृतानि । स्वाहेत्येवंपूर्वा कृतिः करणमुच्चारणं यक्ष्यमाणदेवतानां ताः स्वाहाकृतयः । तद्वंति हव्यानि हवींषि । अत्र प्रयाजेषु वषट्कारप्रदानात्स्वाहाकृतं हविरित्यर्थः । तद्भविरुपेत्य वीतये भक्षणाया गहि । आगच्छ ॥ गमेश्चांदसः शपो लुक् । अनुदात्तोपदेशेत्यादिनानुनासिकलोपः ॥ तथा हे इंद्र आ गहि । स्तोत्राण्यभिलक्ष्यागच्छ । आगत्य हवनस्तदीयमाह्वानं श्रुधि । शृणु । यतस्मामध्वरेऽहिंसात्मके यागे हवंते आह्वयंति ऋत्विजः अतः श्रुधि ॥ हृऋतेर्बहुलं छंदसीति संप्रसारणं ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, स्वाहाकृतानि (svāhākṛtāni)": a svāhākṛti is the making, the utterance, of the word svāhā, preceded thus, for the deities who are about to be sacrificed to; oblations (havya, havis) having that are svāhākṛta. Here, since in the Prayājas the offering is made with the vaṣaṭ-call, the meaning is "an oblation uttered with svāhā". Approach that oblation and come वीतये (vītaye), to eat it: आगच्छ (āgaccha). The root gam in the Vedic idiom has luk of śap, and the nasal is dropped by the rule beginning अनुदात्तोपदेश (anudāttopadeśa). Likewise, "O Indra, come" (आ गहि (ā gahi)): come having the hymns in view; having come, hear their call (श्रुधि (śrudhi), "listen"), since the priests invite you (हवंते (havaṃte)) in the non-violent sacrifice (अध्वरे (adhvare)); therefore listen. For the root hṛ there is saṃprasāraṇa by हृऋतेर्बहुलं छंदसीति (hṛṛterbahulaṃ chaṃdasīti).

p. 281

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • इंद्र (iṃdra)—O Indra
  • स्वाहाकृतानि (svāhākṛtāni)—offered with the utterance of svāhā
  • हव्यानि (havyāni)—the oblations
  • वीतये (vītaye)—for eating
  • उप (upa)—to the vicinity
  • आ गहि (ā gahi)—be pleased to come
  • त्वां (tvāṃ)—you
  • अध्वरे (adhvare)—in the sacrifice that is free from violence
  • हवंते (havaṃte)—(the priests) call
  • (therefore)
  • आ गहि (ā gahi)—be pleased to come (and)
  • हवं (havaṃ)—our invocation
  • श्रुधि (śrudhi)—hear
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, be pleased to come near us to eat the oblations offered with the utterance of svāhā. The priests call you in the sacrifice that is free from violence; therefore be pleased to come and hear our invocation.

Printed English

Approach, Indra, to partake of the oblations consecrated with Swaha ; approach and hear the invocation, as they invoke you to the sacrifice.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

स्वाहाकृतानि (svāhākṛtāni)—स्वाहा इत्येवंपूर्वा कृतिः करणमुच्चारणं यक्ष्यमाणदेवतानां ताः स्वाहाकृतयः । (svāhā ityevaṃpūrvā kṛtiḥ karaṇamuccāraṇaṃ yakṣyamāṇadevatānāṃ tāḥ svāhākṛtayaḥ |) तद्वंति हव्यानि (tadvaṃti havyāni). That is, oblations accompanied by the mantra "svāhā" recited at the offering; the word is an epithet of हव्यानि (havyāni). It is a word chiefly recited in the last Ṛks of the Āprī hymns. In some Ṛks it stands as an adverb: in 1-13-12 as स्वाहा कृषोतन (svāhā kṛṣotana), in 1-146-12 as स्वाहा कर्तन (svāhā kartana); in 3-4-11, 7-2-11 and 10-60-11 in the instrumental sense; in 2-3-11 as an epithet of the oblation (havya); in 10-110-11 as an epithet of हविः (haviḥ); and in the present Ṛk as an epithet of हव्यानि (havyāni). NOTE

In explaining this word, some hold that it denotes the svāhā-utterance as a deity; others that Agni is indicated by it. In the Praiṣa-sūkta it is recited: होता यक्षवग्निग् स्वाहाज्यस्य...........वियंतु होतर्यज । (hotā yakṣavagnig svāhājyasya...........viyaṃtu hotaryaja |) (Trai. Prā. 3-6-2-2) NOTE On this Sāyaṇa explains: योऽयं स्वाहाशब्दोदितः उत्तमप्रयाजदेवः अग्निः तं दैव्यो होता यजतु । (yo 'yaṃ svāhāśabdoditaḥ uttamaprayājadevaḥ agniḥ taṃ daivyo hotā yajatu |)—that is, the word svāhā points to Agni, the deity of the eleventh Prayāja. The author of the Nirukta

p. 282

explains स्वाहाकृतयः (svāhākṛtayaḥ): स्वाहेत्येतत् सु आहेति ना, स्वा नागाहेति वा, स्वं प्राहेति ना, स्वाहुतं हनिर्जुहोतीति ना । (svāhetyetat su āheti nā, svā nāgāheti vā, svaṃ prāheti nā, svāhutaṃ hanirjuhotīti nā |) (Ni. 7-21). NOTE He explains that it is well known as svāhākṛti either because one has recited well, or because Speech itself said "it is well", or because one offers an oblation sanctified by the mantra svāhā. He clarified this idea by citing the Ṛk 10-110-11. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa: स्वाहाकृतीर्यजति प्रतिष्ठा वै स्वाहाकृतयः प्रतिष्ठायामेव तद्यज्ञमंततः प्रतिष्ठापयति । (svāhākṛtīryajati pratiṣṭhā vai svāhākṛtayaḥ pratiṣṭhāyāmeva tadyajñamaṃtataḥ pratiṣṭhāpayati |) (Pa. Prā. 2-4) NOTE It explains that since the oblation is completed by the svāhākṛti, that is the support of the whole sacrifice, and that it establishes the sacrifice on a proper foundation. In the Bṛhaddevatā: स्वाहाकृतयोऽनेकाश्च विदुषां मतयोऽभवन् । तत्सर्वं त्वयमेवाग्निर्भवतीति विनिश्चयः ॥ (svāhākṛtayo 'nekāśca viduṣāṃ matayo 'bhavan | tatsarvaṃ tvayamevāgnirbhavatīti viniścayaḥ ‖) अयं हि कर्ता स्वाहानां कृतिस्तासामिहैकजा । अयं प्रसूतिर्भूतानां सर्वेषामयमव्ययः ॥ (ayaṃ hi kartā svāhānāṃ kṛtistāsāmihaikajā | ayaṃ prasūtirbhūtānāṃ sarveṣāmayamavyayaḥ ‖) (Bṛ. Je. 3-29 to 31) NOTE

Although the opinions of the learned about the svāhākṛti are not of one kind, the whole idea denoted by this word is directed to this terrestrial Agni. Since this Agni is the maker of svāhā and he himself is its making, the terrestrial Agni is so called. Following the view of the Nirukta-author, आग्नेयी इति तु स्थितिः (āgneyī iti tu sthitiḥ) (Ni. 8-22), the author of the Bṛhaddevatā has declared his opinion.

In the last Ṛks of these Āprī hymns, which consist of svāhā, deities such as Pūṣan, the Maruts, Vāyu, Sūrya, Indra and Varuṇa are all addressed; above all of them, पुरोगा अग्निर्देवानां गायत्रेण समज्यते (purogā agnirdevānāṃ gāyatreṇa samajyate) । स्वाहाकृतीषु रोचते (svāhākṛtīṣu rocate) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-188-11) सद्यो जातो व्यमिमीत यज्ञ मग्निर्देवानामभवत्पुरोगाः । अस्य होतुः प्रदिश्यतस्य वाचि स्वाहाकृतं हविरदंतु देवाः ॥ (sadyo jāto vyamimīta yajña magnirdevānāmabhavatpurogāḥ | asya hotuḥ pradiśyatasya vāci svāhākṛtaṃ haviradaṃtu devāḥ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-22) NOTE

p. 283

In these Ṛks Agni is praised as the leader of the gods from the time of his birth. And describing the power of the svāhākṛti: आ याह्यग्ने समिधानो अर्वाजिंद्रेण देवैः सरथं तुरेभिः । बर्हिर्न आस्तामदितिः सुपुत्रा स्वाहा देवा अमृता मादयंतां ॥ (ā yāhyagne samidhāno arvājiṃdreṇa devaiḥ sarathaṃ turebhiḥ | barhirna āstāmaditiḥ suputrā svāhā devā amṛtā mādayaṃtāṃ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-4-11) आग्ने वह वरुणमिष्टये न इंद्र दिवो मरुतो अंतरिक्षात् । सीदंतु बर्हिर्विश्व अ यजत्राः स्वाहा देवा अमृता मादयंतां ॥ (āgne vaha varuṇamiṣṭaye na iṃdra divo maruto aṃtarikṣāt | sīdaṃtu barhirviśva a yajatrāḥ svāhā devā amṛtā mādayaṃtāṃ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-70-11) These Ṛks indicate that, because the gods are gladdened by the mantra svāhā, the word svāhā holds such a divine place in the sacrifice.

(Conclusion on the Āprī hymns) Concerning the necessity and purposes of the Āprī hymns, the scholar Max Müller first says that they were a means of pacifying either gods or kinsmen, and then says that fully understanding their mystic meanings is itself a labour, as follows: "It is possible that Apri hymns may have been the songs of reconciliation and that they were called Apri, i.e., appeasing hymns, not because of their appeasing the anger of Gods but the enmities of the members of the same or different families. However it may be, they indeed prove an active intercourse between the ancient families of India long before the final collection of the ten books....................The original purpose of the Apri hymns and the motive for allowing the priests to choose, are difficult to discover " (Ancient Sanskrit Literature P. 246-7)

Although even among the ancient Vedic scholars there is disagreement about the place of the Āprī hymns in sacrificial rites and about their deities, all the Āprī hymns have many common features; since there is a definite pattern and refinement in their composition and subject matter, one cannot say either that all were composed together or that they have no connection with one another. Except for the seers of the fourth and sixth maṇḍalas, the seers of the remaining

p. 284

maṇḍalas all possess the traditional Āprī hymns of their own families. Though the Kāṇva line of the eighth maṇḍala has no separate Āprī hymn, it is well known that they use the hymn 1-3. But the reason why the seers of the fourth and sixth maṇḍalas have no need of it cannot be stated. Or perhaps the lines of Vāmadeva and Bhāradvāja recited some other mantras in this place (or, since Bhāradvāja was born in the Aṅgiras lineage, the very hymn in question).

Mantras indicated by the names Āprī and Āpra— Kātyāyana in the Sarvānukramaṇī: एतदाप्रिसूक्तं एतेनान्यानुक्तदैवतानि एकादशकानि तु नाराशंसानि आप्रशब्दोक्तानि आतनूनपात्वंति । (etadāprisūktaṃ etenānyānuktadaivatāni ekādaśakāni tu nārāśaṃsāni āpraśabdoktāni ātanūnapātvaṃti |). He says that the mantras recited addressed to the deity Narāśaṃsa are known by the name Āpra, and those recited addressed to the deity Tanūnapāt are known by the name Āprī. But in the Nirukta and the like there are no sentences showing this difference.

The question whether the name Āprī refers to the deity or to the hymn is natural. On close view it may be said that it first referred to the hymn and afterwards to mantras indicating the deity.

Nature of the rite—It may be said that the sacrificial rite prescribed by the Āprī hymn did not hold a subordinate position, as the Brāhmaṇas and others suggest, but held the position of a principal sacrifice. The difference between the Prayāja oblations and the oblations prescribed in this rite is known in many places. In the Ṛks 1-13-8; 1-148-7 NOTE; 1-142-8; 3-4-8; 5-5-2; 9-5-2 the expression इमं यज्ञं (imaṃ yajñaṃ), in the Ṛks 5-5-2; 3-4-5 the expression नः यज्ञं (naḥ yajñaṃ), and in the Ṛks 1-13-2; 7-2-2; 10-110-8 the expression अस्मिन् यज्ञेः (asmin yajñeḥ) show a principal place in the sacrificial rite, whether in the sacrifice or in the offering of oblations, and not a subordinate one like the Prayāja oblations.

From the mantras त्रिर्दिना आमिमिक्षति (trirdinā āmimikṣati) (1-142-3) and त्रिरहन्नायजंते (trirahannāyajaṃte) (3-4-2) it is understood that this rite is to be performed at three times of the day; and from समिद्धो अव्य मनुषो दुरोणे (samiddho avya manuṣo duroṇe) (10-110-1) that there is no separate sacrificial house for it and that Agni may be established in an ordinary house. समित्समित्सुमना बोध्यस्मे शुचाशुचा सुमतिं रासि वस्वः । आ देव देवान्यजथाय वक्षि सखा सखीन्तुमना यक्ष्यग्ने ॥ (samitsamitsumanā bodhyasme śucāśucā sumatiṃ rāsi vasvaḥ | ā deva devānyajathāya vakṣi sakhā sakhīntumanā yakṣyagne ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-4-1)

p. 285

This Ṛk, in which the seer Viśvāmitra poetically describes the blazing of Agni, and जुषस्व नः समिधमग्ने अद्य शोचा बृहद्यजतॆं धूममृण्वन् । उप स्पृश दिव्यं सानु स्तूपैः सं रश्मिभिस्ततनः सूरस्य ॥ (juṣasva naḥ samidhamagne adya śocā bṛhadyajatèṃ dhūmamṛṇvan | upa spṛśa divyaṃ sānu stūpaiḥ saṃ raśmibhistatanaḥ sūrasya ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-2-1) this Ṛk, with its description of the rays of Agni and of the sun spreading together, both show the poetic character of the mantras. These same descriptions show that this sacrifice is to be begun in the morning.

The mantra पूर्व्यं तंतुं तनुष्ट (pūrvyaṃ taṃtuṃ tanuṣṭa) (1-142-1) shows that this sacrifice is ancient. Since the help of Agni, the divine hotṛ, is needed for this sacrifice to be accomplished without obstacle, the oblation of ghee must first be offered to Agni. When Agni is thus satisfied, he spreads toward the atmosphere (7-2-1); then he brings the gods. Because Agni is the friend of men (3-4-1), he does this service.

Artistic skill—Although the Āprī hymns are distinct from one another, were composed at different times and belong to different seer-lines, all these hymns have one and the same manner of speech and aim; hence a harmony and charm in a way greater than in all the other kinds of hymns shows their distinction.

In all the hymns (except two) the number of Ṛks is eleven, and that the hymn begins with the word समिद् (samid) and ends with स्वाहा (svāhā) shows a fixed rule from the poetic and artistic point of view. In the matter of metre there is no such restriction. The hymns 1-13; 1-18; 5-5; 9-5 are composed in the Gāyatrī metre, the hymn 1-142 in the Anuṣṭubh metre, and the hymns 2-3; 3-4; 7-2; 10-70 and 10-110 in the Triṣṭubh metre.

Many mantra-portions such as देवान् आवह (devān āvaha), देवान् वक्षि (devān vakṣi), विप्रा यज्ञेषु मानुषेषु कारुः (viprā yajñeṣu mānuṣeṣu kāruḥ) are repeated.

Grammar
  • गहि — गम्‌ल्य गत् धातुः । लोट् मध्यमपुरुषएकवचने सिपः हि आदेशः । बहुलं छंदसि इति शपः लुक् । अनुदात्तोपदेश (पा. सू. ६-४-३७) इति हेः जातृत्वात् तन्निमित्तीकृत्य धातोः अनुनासिकस्य मकारस्य लोपः । असिद्धवदत्रा—

p. 286

  • गहि (मुंदुवरिकॆ) — असिद्धवदत्राभात् इति असिद्धत्वात् अतो हेः इति हेः लुक् न भवति । अतिजंतस्य परत्वात् निघातस्वरः भवति ।
  • वीतये — वी गतिप्रजनकांत्यसनखादनेषु धातुः । मंत्रेवृषेषपच (पा. सू. ३-३-९६) इति क्तिनः उदात्तस्वरः भवति । चतुर्थीएकवचनांतरूपम् ।
  • इंद्र — पादादित्वात् आमंत्रितनिघातस्वरः न भवति । आमंत्रितस्य (पा. सू. ६-१-१९८) इति आद्युदात्तस्वरः भवति ।
  • श्रुधि — श्रु श्रवणे धातुः । लोट् मध्यमपुरुषएकवचने सिप् । बहुलं छंदसि इति विकरणस्य लुक् । श्रुशृणु (पा. सू. ६-४-१०२) इति हेः धिभावः भवति । NOTE तस्य जित्वात् गुणः न भवति । तिजंतस्य परत्वात् अतिजिः इति निषेधकृतत्वात् निघातस्वरः न भवति । प्रत्ययस्य अपित्वविधानकृतत्वात् तस्य उदात्तः भवति, अंतोदात्तः भवति ।
  • हवम् — ह्वेञ् स्पर्धायां शब्दे च धातुः । भावार्थे अप् प्रत्ययः । धातोः संप्रसारणं, पूर्वरूपम् । प्रत्ययनिमित्तिकत्वात् धातोः इकः गुणः । अवादेशः । प्रत्ययस्य पित्त्वात् धातुस्वरः अवतिष्ठते ।
  • हवंते — पूर्वोक्तस्य धातोः लट् प्रथमपुरुषबहुवचने झ प्रत्ययः । टेः एत्वम् । रोंतः इति अंतादेशः । बहुलं छंदसि इति धातोः संप्रसारणं, पूर्वरूपम् । शप् विकरणम् । तन्निमित्तीकृत्य उकारस्य गुणः । अनादेशः । अतिजंतस्य परत्वात् निघातस्वरः भवति ।
  • अध्वरे — न विद्यते ध्वरः हिंसा यत्र अध्वरः । तस्मिन् । नञ्सुभ्याम् (पा. सू. ६-२-१७२) इति उत्तरपदस्य अंतोदात्तस्वरः भवति । सप्तमीएकवचनांतरूपम् ।

Here ends the hundred and forty-second sūkta.

p. 287

Sūkta 143 (Maṇḍala 1)

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

प्र तव्यसीमित्यष्टर्चं चतुर्थं सूक्तं दैर्घतमसं । तथा चानुक्रांतं । प्र तव्यसीमष्टावाग्नेयं तु तत्तिष्टुबंतमिति । तु तदित्युक्तत्पादिदमादिसूक्ताष्टकस्याग्निर्देवता । अंत्या त्रिष्टुप् शिष्टास्त्रिष्टुबंतपरिभाषया जगत्यः ॥ प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोरुक्तो विनियोगः ॥ अग्निष्टोम अग्निमारुते शस्त्र इदं सूक्तं जातवेदस्यनिविद्वानीयं । अथ यथेतमिति खंडे सूत्रितं । प्र तव्यसीं नव्यसीमापो हि प्रीति तिस्रः । आ. ५-२० । इति ॥ दशरात्रस्य प्रथमेऽप्यहनि जातवेदस्यनिविद्वानं आश्वमेधिके मध्यमेऽहनि च निविद्वानं । तथा चाचार्यातिदेशः । ऐकाहिकान्युपसंशस्य तेषु निविदो दध्यादेवमेवाग्नि मारुते । आ १-१० । इति ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

This sūkta, beginning प्र तव्यसीं (pra tavyasīṃ), has eight verses and is the fourth sūkta (of the anuvāka). Its seer is Dīrghatamas. The Anukramaṇī is quoted: the eight verses beginning प्र तव्यसीं (pra tavyasīṃ) are addressed to Agni, and the word "tu tat" in it marks that the sūkta-octad beginning here has Agni as deity. The last verse is a triṣṭubh; the remaining verses are jagatī by the rule that what is left over, where triṣṭubh is the final metre, is jagatī. The use (viniyoga) in the Prātaranuvāka and the Āśvina śastra has already been stated. In the Agniṣṭoma, at the Agnimāruta śastra, this sūkta serves as the Jātavedasya nivid-vāna (the verses that accompany the nivid for Jātavedas). The Āśvalāyana sūtra prescribes it in the section beginning "atha yathetam": the three verses beginning प्र तव्यसीं (pra tavyasīṃ) and नव्यसीं (navyasīṃ) and आपो हि (āpo hi) (Ā. 5-20). Further, on the first day of the Daśarāta it is the Jātavedasya nivid-vāna, and in the Āśvamedhika on the middle day there is a nivid-vāna also. The teacher's extension of the rule is likewise given: having recited the Aikāhika (one-day) hymns, one is to place the nivids in them, and the same for the Agnimāruta (Ā. 1-10).

Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning "Pra tavyasīm" is the fourth sūkta in the twenty-first anuvāka. It has eight Ṛks. Its seer is Dīrghatamas. The Anukramaṇī says: "Pra tavyasīm: eight Āgneya verses, the last a triṣṭubh." Because the words "tu" and "tat" are used there, it is to be understood that this sūkta and the eight sūktas that follow have Agni as deity. The last Ṛk of this sūkta is in the triṣṭubh metre; the other Ṛks are in the jagatī metre. These sūktas are used for the Prātaranuvāka and for the Āśvina śastra mantras. Also, when the Agnimāruta śastra mantras are recited in the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice, this sūkta is used for the nivid mantras connected with Jātavedas; this is explained in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the section "Yathetam", by the sūtra "the three verses Pra tavyasīm, Navyasīm and Āpo hi ṣṭhā" (Ā. 5-20). Besides, in the sacrificial rite called Daśarātra, performed over ten days, it is to be used on the first day for the nivid mantras connected with Jātavedas, and in the Aśvamedha sacrifice on the middle day for the nivid mantras; this is indicated in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, where the teacher's extension of the rule is explained, by the sentence "Aikāhikān upasaṃśasya teṣu nivido dadhyād evam evāgnimāruta" (Ā. 10-10). NOTE

p. 288

Particulars
  • Sūkta 143
  • Maṇḍala 1; Anuvāka 21; Sūkta 143
  • Aṣṭaka 2; Adhyāya 2; Varga 12
  • Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 8
  • Ṛṣi: Dīrghatamas Aucathya
  • Devatā: Agni
  • Chandas: 1–7 Jagatī; 8 Triṣṭubh

Ṛk 1

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

प्र तव्य॑सीं॒ नव्य॑सीं धी॒तिम॒ग्नये॑ वा॒चो म॒तिं सह॑सः ॒॑ सूनवे भरे ।
अ॒पां नापा॒द्यो वसु॑भिः स॒ह प्रि॒यो होता॑ पृथि॒व्यां
न्यसी॑ददृ॒त्वियः॑ ॥ १ ॥

pra tavyasīṃ navyasīṃ dhītimagnaye vāco matiṃ sahasaḥ sūnave bhare | apāṃ nāpādyo vasubhiḥ saha priyo hotā pṛthivyāṃ nyasīdadṛtviyaḥ ‖ 1 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

प्र । तव्यसीं । नव्यसीं । धीतिं । अग्नये । वाचः । मतिं । सहसः । सूनवे । भरे ।
अपां । नपात् । यः । वसुभिः । सह । प्रियः । होता । पृथिव्यां । नि । असीदत् ।
ऋत्वियः ॥ १ ॥

pra | tavyasīṃ | navyasīṃ | dhītiṃ | agnaye | vācaḥ | matiṃ | sahasaḥ | sūnave | bhare | apāṃ | napāt | yaḥ | vasubhiḥ | saha | priyaḥ | hotā | pṛthivyāṃ | ni | asīdat | ṛtviyaḥ ‖ 1 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

अहमग्नये तव्यसीं तवीयसीमतिशयेन वर्धयित्रीं ॥ तवतिर्वृद्ध्यर्थः सौत्रो धातुः । अस्मात्तृजंतात्तुश्चंदसीतीयसुन् । तुरिष्ठेमेयःस्विति तृलोपः। छांदस ईकारलोपः ॥ नव्यसीं नवतरामपूर्वां धीतिं यागलक्षणामुक्तगुणकं कर्म प्र भरे । प्रकर्षण करोमि । तथोक्तलक्षणां वाचो मतिं स्तुतिरूपं कर्म

Gist of the bhāṣya

"I (offer) to Agni a tavyasī," that is, a more powerful one, one that increases him exceedingly. The root tavati has the sense of growth. नव्यसीं (navyasīṃ) is newer, unprecedented. The dhīti is the action of sacrifice, having the qualities stated; "I offer it forth" (pra bhare), I perform it eminently. Likewise (I offer) the mati of speech, the action in the form of praise,

p. 289

भरे । कीदृशायाग्नये । सहसो बलस्य सूनवे पुत्राय । किंच योऽग्निरपां नपात् तासां नप्ता । अद्व्य ओषधयः ओषधीभ्योऽग्निरित्यग्नेर्नप्तृत्वं । अथवा । अपां न पातयिता वैद्युताग्निरूपेण प्रवर्षकत्वादिति भावः । तथा प्रियो यजमानस्य प्रीणयिता प्रियतमो ना तस्य होता होमनिष्पादकः सोऽग्निर्य्त्वदियः प्राप्तकालः प्राप्तप्रदानसमयः सन्।पृथिव्यां वेदिलक्षणायां वसुभिर्निवासयोग्यैर्गवादिधनैः सहितो न्यसीदत् । नितरां सीदति ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

I offer it to Agni. What sort of Agni? The son of strength (sahas). And further, Agni who is apāṃ napāt, the grandson of the waters: the herbs come from the waters and Agni from the herbs, so he is their grandson. Or else: he is the one who makes the waters fall (?), because as lightning-fire he causes rain. NOTE Likewise he is priya, the one who pleases the sacrificer, the dearest man; hotā, the accomplisher of the homa. That Agni, ṛtviya, having reached his time, the time for giving, sat down on the earth, that is, the altar, together with the vasus, the wealth such as cows fit for dwelling. "Ni-asīdat" means he sat down fully.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • अहं (ahaṃ)—I
  • सहसः (sahasaḥ)—of strength
  • सूनवे (sūnave)—to the son
  • अग्नये (agnaye)—to Agni (with Agni as the object)
  • तव्यसीम् (tavyasīm)—that which gives the greatest vigour
  • नव्यसीम् (navyasīm)—that which is the newest
  • धीतिम् (dhītim)—the action in the form of sacrifice
  • वाचःमतिं (vācaḥmatiṃ)—the action in the form of praise
  • प्रभरे (prabhare)—I perform eminently
  • यः (yaḥ)—which Agni
  • अपां नपात् (apāṃ napāt)—the grandson of the waters
  • प्रियः (priyaḥ)—the giver of delight (to the sacrificer), or the dearest
  • होता (hotā)—the accomplisher of the homa
  • ऋत्वियः (ṛtviyaḥ)—being there at the proper time
  • पृथिव्यां (pṛthivyāṃ)—on the ground in the form of the altar
  • वसुभिः (vasubhiḥ)—with wealth such as dwelling-places
  • न्यसीदत् (nyasīdat)—sits down
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Addressing Agni, the son of strength, I perform eminently the sacrificial action, which gives the greatest vigour and is new, together with speech in the form of praise. Agni, the grandson of the waters, the giver of delight to the sacrificer, the accomplisher of the homa, comes in due season to the sacrifice and sits on the altar with cow-wealth and the like. NOTE

Printed English

I offer devoutly to Agni, the son of strength, an invigorating and most new sacrifice, with words of adoration ; ( that Agni ), the grandson of the waters, who, (present) in due season, the friend and ministering priest (to the sacrificer) sits upon the alter with (many) good things. NOTE

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The sūktā-introduction says: अग्निष्टोमे अग्निमारुते शस्त्रे इदं सूक्तं जातवेदस्यनिविद्वानीयं । (agniṣṭome agnimārute śastre idaṃ sūktaṃ jātavedasyanividvānīyaṃ |) Sāyaṇa has stated in the introduction that this is a sūkta to be recited at the time of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice, forming part of the Agnimāruta śastra. He has also cited as authority the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra (5-20), which says प्र तव्यसीं नव्यसीं आपो हि प्रीति तिस्रः । (pra tavyasīṃ navyasīṃ āpo hi prīti tisraḥ |)

p. 290

This is well known as the Jātavedasya nivid mantra. Since the Vaiśvānara nivid mantra is also a part of the Agnimāruta śastra, he has stated plainly जातवेदस्यनिविधानीयं । (jātavedasyanividhānīyaṃ |) to show the difference from it. Of these, the sūkta that begins with the Ṛk वैश्वानराय पृथुपाजसे विपो रत्ना विधंत धरुणेषु गातवे । अग्निर्हि देवा अमृतो दुवस्यत्यथा धर्माणि सनता न दूदुषत् ॥ (vaiśvānarāya pṛthupājase vipo ratnā vidhaṃta dharuṇeṣu gātave | agnirhi devā amṛto duvasyatyathā dharmāṇi sanatā na dūduṣat ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-3-1) belongs to Vaiśvānara-Agni. The present sūkta, and the sūkta that begins with the Ṛk आपो हि ष्ठा मयोभुवस्ता न ऊर्जे दधातन । महे रणाय चक्षसे । (āpo hi ṣṭhā mayobhuvastā na ūrje dadhātana | mahe raṇāya cakṣase |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-9-1) together with the next two sūktas, belong to the Agni called Jātavedas.

The earlier story that relates to this Agnimāruta and is its cause is told both in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa and in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa. Since the two accounts differ somewhat in the narration, both are set out separately here. Of these, the original story of the Agnimāruta stotra connected with Vaiśvānara-Agni stands thus in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa: वैश्वानरीयेणाग्निमारुतं प्रतिपद्यते वैश्वानरो वा एतद्रॆतः सिक्तं प्राच्यावयत्तस्माद्वैश्वानरीयेणाग्निमारुतं प्रतिपद्यते । (vaiśvānarīyeṇāgnimārutaṃ pratipadyate vaiśvānaro vā etadrètaḥ siktaṃ prācyāvayattasmādvaiśvānarīyeṇāgnimārutaṃ pratipadyate |) (Ai. Brā. 3-35) Vaiśvānara made the semen that had been spilt downwards move. Therefore it is his praise; this indicates the circumstance behind it. That circumstance is as follows: प्रजापतिर्वै स्वां दुहितरमभ्यध्यायद्दिवमित्यन्य आहुरुषसमित्यन्ये तामृश्यो भूत्वा रोहितं भूतामभ्यैत्तं देवा अपश्यन्नकृतं वै प्रजापतिः करोतीति ते तम्मैच्छन्य एनमारिष्यत्येतमन्वोन्यस्मिन्नाविंदंस्तेषां या एव घोरतमास्तन्व आसंस्ता एकधा समभरंस्ताः संभृता एष देवोऽभवत्तदस्यैतद्भूतवन्नाम । (prajāpatirvai svāṃ duhitaramabhyadhyāyaddivamityanya āhuruṣasamityanye tāmṛśyo bhūtvā rohitaṃ bhūtāmabhyaittaṃ devā apaśyannakṛtaṃ vai prajāpatiḥ karotīti te tammaicchanya enamāriṣyatyetamanvonyasminnāviṃdaṃsteṣāṃ yā eva ghoratamāstanva āsaṃstā ekadhā samabharaṃstāḥ saṃbhṛtā eṣa devo 'bhavattadasyaitadbhūtavannāma |) Once Prajāpati looked at his own daughter and was infatuated; she turned into a doe, and he followed her as a buck. Then the gods, knowing this to be an unheard-of wrong deed, tried to have him punished and created this Bhūta, a union of terrible forms.

p. 291

He became Bhūtapati. तं देवा अब्रुवन्नयं वै प्रजापतिरकृतमकरिमं विध्येति स तथेत्यब्रवीत्स वै वो वरं वृणा इति वृणीष्टेति स एतमेव वरमवृणीत पशूनामाधिपत्यं तदस्यैतत्सशुमन्नाम ॥ (taṃ devā abruvannayaṃ vai prajāpatirakṛtamakarimaṃ vidhyeti sa tathetyabravītsa vai vo varaṃ vṛṇā iti vṛṇīṣṭeti sa etameva varamavṛṇīta paśūnāmādhipatyaṃ tadasyaitatsaśumannāma ‖) Then the gods told him of the wrong deed Prajāpati was doing and said he must be punished. He agreed and asked in return, as a boon, for the lordship over animals (to become Paśupati); their consent was given. तमभ्यायत्याविध्यत्स विद्व ऊर्ध्व उदप्रपत्तमेतं मृग इत्याचक्षते य उ एव मृगव्याधः स उ एव स या रोहित्सा रोहिणी यो एवेषुस्तिकांडा सो एवेषुस्ति कांडा । (tamabhyāyatyāvidhyatsa vidva ūrdhva udaprapattametaṃ mṛga ityācakṣate ya u eva mṛgavyādhaḥ sa u eva sa yā rohitsā rohiṇī yo eveṣustikāṃḍā so eveṣusti kāṃḍā |) Then Bhūtapati pierced Prajāpati with his trident, in the form of a three-pointed arrow. At once: तद्वा इदं प्रजापते रेतः सिक्तमधावत्तत्सरोऽभवत्ते देवा अब्रुवन्मेदं प्रजापते रेतो मषदिति यदब्रुवन्मेदं प्रजापते रेतो मषदिति तन्मादुषमभवत्तन्मादुषस्य माडुषत्वं माडुषं ह वै नामैतद्यन्मानुषं सन्मानुषमित्याचक्षते परोक्षेण परोक्षप्रिया इव हि देवाः । (tadvā idaṃ prajāpate retaḥ siktamadhāvattatsaro 'bhavatte devā abruvanmedaṃ prajāpate reto maṣaditi yadabruvanmedaṃ prajāpate reto maṣaditi tanmāduṣamabhavattanmāduṣasya māḍuṣatvaṃ māḍuṣaṃ ha vai nāmaitadyanmānuṣaṃ sanmānuṣamityācakṣate parokṣeṇa parokṣapriyā iva hi devāḥ |) (Ai. Brā. 3-33) At once the semen of Prajāpati began to flow. It became a lake. Then the gods did not let that semen go to waste. Therefore: तद्ग्निना परा दधुस्तन्मरुतोऽधून्वंस्तदग्निर्न प्राच्यावयत्तदग्नि ना वैश्वानरेण परा दधुस्तन्मरुतोऽदून्वंस्तदग्निर्वैश्वानरः प्राच्यावयत्तस्य तद्रेतसः प्रथममददीप्यत तदसावादित्योऽभवत्......... (tadgninā parā dadhustanmaruto 'dhūnvaṃstadagnirna prācyāvayattadagni nā vaiśvānareṇa parā dadhustanmaruto 'dūnvaṃstadagnirvaiśvānaraḥ prācyāvayattasya tadretasaḥ prathamamadadīpyata tadasāvādityo 'bhavat.........) (I. Prā. 3-33) NOTE Then the gods made Agni surround that lake filled with the semen, and made Marut blow upon it. Agni could not make it move. Then, with the help of Vaiśvānara, Agni was able to make Marut move it; this is the circumstance stated. Therefore Vaiśvānara-Agni is praised by the Vaiśvānara nivid mantra, which begins with the mantra "Vaiśvānarāya pṛthupājase" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-3-1). And further,

p. 292

जातवेदस्यं शंसति । प्रजापतिः प्रजा असृजत ताः सृष्टाः पराच्य एवायन्न व्यावर्तंत ता अग्निना पर्यगच्छत्ता अग्निमुपावर्तंत तमेवा द्याप्युपावृत्ताः सोऽब्रवीज्जाता वै प्रजा अनेनाविदमिति तज्ञातवेदस्यमभवत्तज्ञातवेदसो जातवेदस्त्वं ॥ (jātavedasyaṃ śaṃsati | prajāpatiḥ prajā asṛjata tāḥ sṛṣṭāḥ parācya evāyanna vyāvartaṃta tā agninā paryagacchattā agnimupāvartaṃta tamevā dyāpyupāvṛttāḥ so 'bravījjātā vai prajā anenāvidamiti tajñātavedasyamabhavattajñātavedaso jātavedastvaṃ ‖) (Ai. Brā. 3-36) Prajāpati created the creatures. Afterwards all that were created escaped and did not return. Then, when they were surrounded by Agni, they all approached Agni. Because Agni knew the creatures created by Prajāpati, he is called Jātavedas. Therefore it is said that Agni is praised by the sūkta beginning with the Ṛk "Pra tavyasīm"; this is the purpose of this Agnimāruta nivid mantra. The same point is made in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa in this order: प्रजापतिर्ह वै स्वां दुहितरमभिदध्र्यौ । दिवं पोषसं ना मिथुन्येनया स्यामिति ताग्ं संबभूव । तद्वै देवानामाग आस । य इत्थग्ं स्वां दुहितरमस्माकग्ं स्वसारं करोतीति । ते ह देवा ऊचुः । योऽयं देवः पशूनामीष्टेऽतिसंधं वा अयं चरति य इत्थग्ंसां महितरमस्माग्ं स्वसारं करोति विध्यॆममिति तग्ं रुद्रोऽभ्यायत्य विव्याध तस्य सामि रेतः प्रचस्कंद तथेन्नूनं तदास । तस्मादेतदृषिणाभ्यनूक्तं । पिता यस्त्वां दुहितरमधिष्कन् क्ष्मया रेतः संजग्मानो निषिंचदिति तदाग्निमारुतमित्युक्थं तस्मिंस्तद्व्याख्यायते ॥ (prajāpatirha vai svāṃ duhitaramabhidadhryau | divaṃ poṣasaṃ nā mithunyenayā syāmiti tāgṃ saṃbabhūva | tadvai devānāmāga āsa | ya itthagṃ svāṃ duhitaramasmākagṃ svasāraṃ karotīti | te ha devā ūcuḥ | yo 'yaṃ devaḥ paśūnāmīṣṭe 'tisaṃdhaṃ vā ayaṃ carati ya itthagṃsāṃ mahitaramasmāgṃ svasāraṃ karoti vidhyèmamiti tagṃ rudro 'bhyāyatya vivyādha tasya sāmi retaḥ pracaskaṃda tathennūnaṃ tadāsa | tasmādetadṛṣiṇābhyanūktaṃ | pitā yastvāṃ duhitaramadhiṣkan kṣmayā retaḥ saṃjagmāno niṣiṃcaditi tadāgnimārutamityukthaṃ tasmiṃstadvyākhyāyate ‖) (Śa. Prā. 1-7-4-1 to 4) NOTE Prajāpati became enamoured of his own daughter; the gods, regarding it as a sin, said to Rudra that Prajāpati must be punished. Then Rudra pierced Prajāpati, and his seed fell downwards. This same matter, in the Ṛk पिता यत्स्वां दुहितरमधिष्कन् क्ष्मया रेतः संजग्मानो नि षिंचत् । स्वाध्योऽजनयन् ब्रह्मा देवा वास्तोष्पतिं व्रतपां निरतक्षन् । (pitā yatsvāṃ duhitaramadhiṣkan kṣmayā retaḥ saṃjagmāno ni ṣiṃcat | svādhyo 'janayan brahmā devā vāstoṣpatiṃ vratapāṃ niratakṣan |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-61-2) is stated thus: "When the father embraced his own daughter to unite with her, he let his seed fall downwards." This mantra became famous under the name Agnimāruta. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa, describing the efficacy of the Agnimāruta śastra, which is connected with Jātavedas and indicates the present sūkta,

p. 293

जातवेदसे सुनवाम सोममिति जातवेदस्यां पुरस्तात्सूक्तस्य शंसति स्वस्त्ययनं वै जातवेदस्याः स्वस्ति ताय्कॆ । स्वस्त्ययनमेव तत्कुरुते स्वस्ति संवत्सरस्य पारमश्नुते य एवं वेद । (jātavedase sunavāma somamiti jātavedasyāṃ purastātsūktasya śaṃsati svastyayanaṃ vai jātavedasyāḥ svasti tāykè | svastyayanameva tatkurute svasti saṃvatsarasya pāramaśnute ya evaṃ veda |) प्र तव्यसीं नव्यसीं धीतिमग्नय इति जातवेदस्यं प्रेति प्रथमेऽहनि प्रथमस्याहो रूपं । समानमाग्निमारुतं भवति यच्चाग्निष्टोमे यद्वै यज्ञे समानं क्रियते तत्पजा अनु समनंति तस्मात्समानमाग्निमारुतं भवति । (pra tavyasīṃ navyasīṃ dhītimagnaya iti jātavedasyaṃ preti prathame 'hani prathamasyāho rūpaṃ | samānamāgnimārutaṃ bhavati yaccāgniṣṭome yadvai yajñe samānaṃ kriyate tatpajā anu samanaṃti tasmātsamānamāgnimārutaṃ bhavati |)

The Āgnimāruta-śastra addressed to Jātavedas is auspicious and conducive to well-being, and so on. Therefore the greatness of the present sūkta is the greater.

अपां नपात् (apāṃ napāt)—अद्भ्य ओषधयः, ओषधीभ्योऽग्निः (adbhya oṣadhayaḥ, oṣadhībhyo 'gniḥ): thus Agni is the grandson (naptṛ) of the waters. Since plants arise from the waters and Agni from plants, Agni is the grandson of the waters. Or, as Sāyaṇa explains, अपां न पातयिता वैद्युताग्निरूपेण प्रवर्षकत्वादिति भावः (apāṃ na pātayitā vaidyutāgnirūpeṇa pravarṣakatvāditi bhāvaḥ); having shown this derivation, he explains that the name belongs to the lightning-fire. The Nirukta-writers say that the explanation of Apāṃ Napāt is the same as that of Tanūnapāt.

तनूनपादयं त्वेव नाम्ना यच्छत्यस् तनुं । नपादिति प्रजा माहुरमुतोऽस्य च संभवात् ॥ (tanūnapādayaṃ tveva nāmnā yacchatyas tanuṃ | napāditi prajā māhuramuto 'sya ca saṃbhavāt ‖) (Bṛ. De. 3-1)

As is said in many places, the name Tanūnapāt became famous because he is born of himself and so is his own son; the same explanation applies to Apāṃnapāt. This matter is touched upon subtly in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-122-4, in the tenth part of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā. Now there is disagreement as to whether the deity Apāṃnapāt is different from Agni or merely a part of Agni. In the previous sūkta, discussing the Āprī deity Tanūnapāt, the Bṛhaddevatā and other works were cited as saying that this deity is a transformation of Agni, and it was shown that he is not a separate deity. From some further evidence in the Ṛksaṃhitā itself one may say that in the beginning he was regarded as a separate deity and afterwards, united with Agni, was regarded as a part of Agni. According to the Nirukta-writers, Apāṃnapāt and Tanūnapāt are one deity, so one kind of explanation shows the nature of both. If we examine the place of the deity Apāṃnapāt in the Ṛksaṃhitā, we find that in the sūktas addressed to the Viśvedevas Apāṃnapāt is invoked many times.

p. 294

प्र नः पूषा चरथं विश्वदेव्योऽपां नपादवतु वायुरिष्टये । आत्मानं वस्यो अभि वातमर्चत तदश्विना सुहवा यामनि श्रुतं ॥ (pra naḥ pūṣā carathaṃ viśvadevyo 'pāṃ napādavatu vāyuriṣṭaye | ātmānaṃ vasyo abhi vātamarcata tadaśvinā suhavā yāmani śrutaṃ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-92-13)

In this Ṛk, along with the Viśvedevas, Pūṣan and then Apāṃnapāt are prayed to. In the 2nd Ṛk of this sūkta (10-92-2) Agni is praised as the promoter of the sacrifice. In the 13th Ṛk of the 75th sūkta of the 7th Maṇḍala, the deities Ajavikapāt, Ahirbudhnya, Samudra, Apāṃnapāt and Pṛśni are invoked together; Indra and Agni in the first Ṛk, and Agni alone in the fourth. In the 8th and 14th Ṛks of the preceding sūkta (7-34) Agni, and in the 15th Apāṃnapāt, are prayed to as protectors and friends. In the 14th Ṛk of the 52nd sūkta of the 6th Maṇḍala other deities are invoked with Apāṃnapāt; in the 6th and 12th Agni is prayed to. Likewise in the 31st sūkta of the 2nd Maṇḍala and the 50th sūkta of the 6th Maṇḍala, Agni and Apāṃnapāt are mentioned separately. In none of these Ṛks can their identity as one deity be asserted.

The 35th sūkta of the 2nd Maṇḍala is addressed wholly to Apāṃnapāt. Only in the 15th Ṛk is Agni referred to; in the remaining Ṛks, to the end, Agni's name does not occur. Even so, only the 11th and 12th Ṛks could be interpreted as referring to Agni; but the description there too does not apply directly to Agni. Taking these examples, the scholar Bloomfield has given his opinion as follows.

"While Agni became more and more conspicuous, Apam Napat seems to have waned in popularity, until he was so for forgotten that a confusion arose concerning the two uses of the expression (अपा (apā): नपात् (napāt))and Apam Napat, "the son of the waters" was swallowed up in Agni, a 'son of the waters as he was occasionally (twice in the Rik) called, since he too, because of his original lightning nature, was supposed to have been horn of the rain-clouds. To the same source is to be traced the myth of his hiding in the waters, for this myth probably had no connection originally with Apam Napat, beyond the mere fact that both he and Agni were forms of lightning which, appearing when the thunderstorm was at its height, seemed to disappear in the clouds from which they came. The conclusion seems to be warranted, therefore, that Agni and Apam Napat were once distinct Gods—Gods, of the lightning, who were, however, associated with each other and

p. 295

were much alike in certain particulars, and that this association, and resemblance ultimately resulted, possibly at the close of the Vedic Period, in a confusion and Union of the two, as a result of which Apam Napat was absorbed by Agni." ( Journal of American Orintal Society. Vol. XIX. (2) p. 144. )

तव्यसीं (tavyasīṃ)—तवीयसीं अतिशयेन वर्धयित्रीं । तवतिर्वृद्ध्यर्थः । (tavīyasīṃ atiśayena vardhayitrīṃ | tavatirvṛddhyarthaḥ |) It means either "giver of vigour" or "causing growth", and is an adjective of धीतिं (dhītiṃ), "thought" (matim).

स शेवृधमधि धा द्युम्न मस्मे महि क्षत्रं जनाषाळिंद्र तव्यं । रक्षा च नो मघोनः पाहि सूरीन्राये च नः स्वपत्या इषे धाः ॥ (sa śevṛdhamadhi dhā dyumna masme mahi kṣatraṃ janāṣāḷiṃdra tavyaṃ | rakṣā ca no maghonaḥ pāhi sūrīnrāye ca naḥ svapatyā iṣe dhāḥ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-54-11)

In this Ṛk, तव्यं क्षत्रं (tavyaṃ kṣatraṃ) is प्रवृद्दं बलं (pravṛddaṃ balaṃ); it suggests the two meanings "greatly grown" and "endowed with power".

धीतिं (dhītiṃ)—यागक्षलणां उक्तगुणकं कर्म । (yāgakṣalaṇāṃ uktaguṇakaṃ karma |) Here it means the rite of the kind mentioned, of the nature of a sacrifice. The word dhīti has two meanings, "rite" and "wisdom". [In the Nirukta (Ni. 3-8) it is read among the names of the fingers.] The Nirukta-writers have cited two Ṛks in which the two meanings, rite and wisdom, occur:

इयं शुष्मेभिर्बिसखा इवारुजत्सानु गिरीणां तविषेभिरूर्मिभिः । सारावतघ्नीमवसे सुवृक्तिभिः सरस्वतीमा विवसेम धीतिभिः ॥ (iyaṃ śuṣmebhirbisakhā ivārujatsānu girīṇāṃ taviṣebhirūrmibhiḥ | sārāvataghnīmavase suvṛktibhiḥ sarasvatīmā vivasema dhītibhiḥ ‖) ( Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-61-2 )

In this verse they explain धीतिभिः (dhītibhiḥ) as कर्मभिः (karmabhiḥ) (by rites), and in

ऋतस्य हि शुरुधः संति पूर्वीऋतस्य धीतिर्वृजिनानि हंति । ऋतस्य श्लोको बधिरा ततर्द कर्णा बुधानः शुचमान आयोः । (ṛtasya hi śurudhaḥ saṃti pūrvīṛtasya dhītirvṛjināni haṃti | ṛtasya śloko badhirā tatarda karṇā budhānaḥ śucamāna āyoḥ |) ( Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-23-8 NOTE )NOTE

as "wisdom". In some places the word is also used in the sense of "praise". In the present Ṛk it means the rite in the form of sacrifice.

Grammar
  • तव्यसीम्— सूत्रमात्रनिर्दिष्टः तनधातुः वृद्ध्यर्थे प्रयुक्तः । तस्मात् ण्वुल् तृचौ (पा. सू. ३-१-१३३) इति तृच् प्रत्ययः । तुश्चंदसि (पा. सू. ५-३-५९) इति तृजंतात् ईयसुन् प्रत्ययः । तुरिष्ठेमेयस्सु (पा. सू. ६-४-१५४) इति ईयसुनि परे तृचो लोपः । यस्येति च इति अकारस्य लोपः । छांदसत्वात् प्रत्ययस्य ईकारस्य लोपः । ईयसुन् नित्त्वात् इत्यादिर्नित्यम् इति आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति ।

p. 296

  • नव्यसीम्— अतिशयार्थे ईयसुनि आगते पूर्ववत् अकारलोपः । पूर्ववत् स्वरो भवति ।
  • मतिम्— मंत्रे वृषेष— (पा. सू. ३-३-६६) इति क्तिन् उदात्तो भवति । द्वितीया एकवचनांतरूपम् ।
  • भरे— भृञ् भरणे धातुः । लट् उत्तमपुरुष एकवचनांतरूपम् । तिजंतनिघातस्वरो भवति ।
  • अपाम्— ऊडिदं पदादि— (पा. सू. ६-१-१७१) इति विभक्तेरुदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
  • नपात्— पा रक्षणे धातुः । तस्मात् शतृ आगते पात् इति रूपं भवति । तस्य नञ् सह समासे नभ्राण् नपात्— (पा. सू. ६-३-७५) इति नलोपाभावेन निपातितम् ।
  • पृथिव्याम्— पृथिवीशब्दः जीषंतत्वात् अंतोदात्तः । विभक्तौ परायां तस्य यणादेशे जाते तत्परस्य विभक्तेरनुदात्तत्वात् उदात्तयणो— (पा. सू. ६-१-१७४) इति तस्य उदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
  • असीदत्— षद्ल्य विशरणगत्यवसादनेषु धातुः । छंदसि लुज् लज् लिटः— (पा. सू. ३-४-६) इति वर्तमानार्थे लज् भवति । प्रथमपुरुष एकवचने तिप् प्रत्ययः । इतश्च इति इकारलोपः । शप् विकरणः । पाफ्राध्मा— (पा. सू. ७-३-६८) इति धातोः सीदादेशः । यः इति यच्छब्दसंबंधात् निघातस्वरो न भवति । अडागमस्य उदात्तत्वात् आद्युदात्तो भवति ।
  • ऋत्वियः— ऋतुशब्दः । यज्ञर्त्वग्भ्यांघखञ् (पा. सू. ५-१-७१) इति घ प्रत्ययः । आयनेया— (पा. सू. ७-१-२) इति तस्य इयादेशः । यणादेशः । प्रत्ययस्य आद्युदात्तस्वरेण इकार उदात्तो भवति । ॥ १ ॥

p. 297

Ṛk 2

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

स जाय॑मानः पर॒मे व्यो॑मन्या॒विर॒ग्निर॑भवन्मात॒रिश्व॑ने ।
अ॒स्य क्रत्वा॑ समिधा॒नस्य॑ म॒ज्मना॒ प्र द्यावा॑ शो॒चिः पृ॑थि॒वी ॑ अरोचयत् ॥ २ ॥

sa jāyamānaḥ parame vyomanyāviragnirabhavanmātariśvane | asya kratvā samidhānasya majmanā pra dyāvā śociḥ pṛthivī arocayat ‖ 2 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

सः । जायमानः । परमे । विओमनि । आविः । अग्निः । अभवत् । मातरिश्वने ।
अस्य । क्रत्वा । संइधानस्य । मज्मना । प्र । द्यावा । शोचिः । पृथिवी इति ।
अरोचयत् ॥ २ ॥

saḥ | jāyamānaḥ | parame | viomani | āviḥ | agniḥ | abhavat | mātariśvane | asya | kratvā | saṃidhānasya | majmanā | pra | dyāvā | śociḥ | pṛthivī iti | arocayat ‖ 2 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

स पूर्वोक्तोग्निर्जायमानोऽरणीभ्यामुत्पद्यमानः काष्ठेषु ना प्रादुर्भूतः सन् तदानीमेव परम उत्कृष्टे प्रोमनि विविधरक्षणवति वेदिदेशे मातरिश्वनेऽंतरिक्षसंचारिणे नाय्वे प्रथममाविरभवत् । प्रत्यक्षोऽभूत् । त्वमग्ने प्रथमो मातरिश्वन आविर्भव । ऋ. १-३१-३। इत्यादिश्रुत्यंतरप्रसिद्धेः । वायुसंयोगात्पज्वलित इत्यर्थः । अथवा मातरि फलस्य निर्मातरि यज्ञॆ श्वसिति चेष्टत इति मातरिश्वा यजमानः । तदर्थं । किंच समिधानस्येंधनैः सम्यग्दर्धमानस्याग्नेर्मज्जना । बलनामैतत् । बलवता क्रत्वा क्रतुना कर्मणा ज्वालनादिव्यापारेण शोचिद्यावा पृथिवी द्यां च पृथिवीं च प्रारोचयत् । प्रकर्षणादीपयत् ॥ मध्यॆ शोचिःशब्दश्चांदसः ॥ मज्मना क्रत्वा समिधानस्येति वा योज्यं । प्रबलेन समिंधनादिव्यापारेण समिध्यमानस्येत्यर्थः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

That Agni spoken of before, being born—arising from the two fire-sticks—and having appeared in the pieces of wood, at that very moment first manifested himself in the supreme, excellent व्योमनि (vyomani) (the place of varied protection, i.e. the altar), to मातरिश्वने (mātariśvane), the wind moving in the atmosphere. He became visible; this is known from another śruti, त्वमग्ने प्रथमो मातरिश्वन आविर्भव (tvamagne prathamo mātariśvana āvirbhava) (Ṛ. 1-31-3). The meaning: through contact with the wind he blazed up. Or else: Mātariśvan is the sacrificer, who breathes (śvasiti), i.e. exerts himself, in the sacrifice, the maker (nirmātṛ) of its fruit; for his sake. Further, by the मज्मना (majmanā) (a word for strength) of Agni, well kindled with fuel, by powerful क्रत्वा (kratvā), that is, by action, by the work of blazing and the like, the radiance lit up heaven and earth, brightening them intensely. The word शोचिः (śociḥ) in the middle is Vedic usage. Or construe मज्मना क्रत्वा समिधानस्य (majmanā kratvā samidhānasya): of him kindled by powerful action of kindling and the like.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • सः (saḥ)—the one described before
  • अग्निः (agniḥ)—Agni
  • जायमानः (jāyamānaḥ)—as soon as born
  • परमे (parame)—in the excellent
  • व्योमनि (vyomani)—in the atmosphere
  • मातरिश्वने (mātariśvane)—facing the wind
  • आविः अभवत् (āviḥ abhavat)—became visible. [Or व्योमनि (vyomani)—on the altar; मातरिश्वने (mātariśvane)—facing the sacrificer; आविः अभवत् (āviḥ abhavat)—became visible.] (And)
  • मज्मना (majmanā)—powerful
  • क्रत्वा (kratvā)—by the action of blazing and the like
  • समिधानस्य अस्य (samidhānasya asya)—of this Agni kindled by fuel
  • क्रत्वा (kratvā)—by the action of blazing and the like
  • द्यावा (dyāvā)—heaven
  • पृथिवी (pṛthivī)—and earth
  • प्र अरोचयत् (pra arocayat)—lit up

p. 298

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As soon as Agni was born, he became visible in the excellent atmosphere, facing the wind. The radiance of Agni, kindled with fuel, lit up heaven and earth by the powerful actions of blazing and the like.

Printed English

As soon as born, was that (Agni) manifested to Matarishwan in the highest atmosphere, and his radiance, kindled by vigorous effort, spread through heaven and earth.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk it is described that Agni, as soon as born, appeared in the sky to Mātariśvan, and that afterwards the radiance of him, blazing, lit up heaven and earth. Two constructions of the first half are possible here. First: व्योमनि (vyomani)—in the atmosphere, मातरिश्वने (mātariśvane)—before Mātariśvan, आविरभवत् (āvirabhavat). Second: व्योमनि (vyomani)—on the sacrificial altar, मातरिश्वने (mātariśvane)—facing the sacrificer, आविरभवत् (āvirabhavat). (1) That Agni appeared in the sky to Mātariśvan is well known. The word व्योम (vyoma) is read among the names of the atmosphere (Ni. 2-10). It is formed from the root व्येञ् (vyeñ), meaning to pervade, to cover; the sense is the pervading atmosphere.

त्वमग्ने प्रथमो मातरिश्वन आविर्भव सुक्रतू या विवस्वते । अरेजेतां रोदसी होतृपूर्येऽसघ्नोर्भारमयजो महो वसो ॥ (tvamagne prathamo mātariśvana āvirbhava sukratū yā vivasvate | arejetāṃ rodasī hotṛpūrye 'saghnorbhāramayajo maho vaso ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-31-3)

In Ṛks of this kind it is well known that the manifestation of Agni, in the form of lightning, took place first to the wind. Moreover,

वह्निं यशसं विदथस्य केतुं सप्राव्यं दूतं सद्योअर्थं । द्विजन्मानं रयिमिव प्रशस्तं रातिं भरद्भृगवे मातरिश्वा ॥ (vahniṃ yaśasaṃ vidathasya ketuṃ saprāvyaṃ dūtaṃ sadyoarthaṃ | dvijanmānaṃ rayimiva praśastaṃ rātiṃ bharadbhṛgave mātariśvā ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-60-1)

In Ṛks of this kind, Mātariśvan, for the benefit of Bhṛgu and Manu, the performers of sacrifice, brought to the earth Agni who had been hidden in a distant region, and to the earth for the benefit of all creatures

p. 299

(Continuing) It has also been done in many places. Therefore there are sound grounds for stating the first meaning.

  1. If one examines what propriety there is in stating the second meaning, and whether it has sound grounds in support:

व्योमनि (vyomani)—Here the word व्योमनि (vyomani) has been explained as वेदिदेशे (vedideśe). The form is derived from the root अव (ava), meaning protection, joined with the prefix वि (vi). As the etymology of this word, विविधरक्षणवति वेदिदेशे (vividharakṣaṇavati vedideśe) has been shown: the region of the altar furnished with manifold protections. This word is used in this sense in many places in the Ṛk-saṃhitā. For example:

इयं वेदिः परो अंतः पृथिव्या अयं यज्ञो भुवनस्य नाभिः । अयं सोमो वृष्णो अश्वस्य रेतो ब्रह्मायं वाचः परमं व्योम ।

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-35)

In this Ṛk the word for "sky/space" is explained as उत्कृष्टं रक्षकं स्थानं (utkṛṣṭaṃ rakṣakaṃ sthānaṃ), "a superior, protecting place"; and in

ऋतेन ऋतं धरुणं धारयंत यज्ञस्य शोके परमे प्रोमन् । दिपो धर्मन् धरुणो सेदुषो नृञ्चात्यैरजाता अभि ये नसक्षुः ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-15-2)

it is explained as उत्कृष्टे स्थाने उत्तरवेद्यां (utkṛṣṭe sthāne uttaravedyāṃ), "in the superior place, on the northern altar", that is, on the excellent uttaravedi. In the same way, if in the present Ṛk too the word व्योम (vyoma) is taken to mean the altar, then the word मातरिश्व (mātariśva) becomes मातरि फलस्य निर्मातरि यज्ञे श्वसिति चेष्टते इति मातरिश्वा यजमानः (mātari phalasya nirmātari yajñe śvasiti ceṣṭate iti mātariśvā yajamānaḥ): since he is active in the sacrifice, the place of origin of every kind of fruit, मातरिश्वा (mātariśvā) means the sacrificer. It can therefore be explained that Agni, as soon as he was kindled, appeared on the altar facing the sacrificer.

The Brāhmaṇa sentence

व्योमसदित्येष वै व्योमसदृश्योम वा एतत्सद्मनां यस्मिन्नेष आसन्नस्तपति ।

(Ai. Brā. 18-20) also supports this meaning.

If, by the first construction, मातरिश्व (mātariśva) means the wind, one must ask what relation Agni has to this Mātariśvan. If it is said that Agni appeared facing him, it means the two are different persons. But if the history stated here is examined a little more closely, certain grounds show that the two are identical.

उदुष्टुतः समिधा यहो अद्यौद्वर्ष्मन्विवो अधि नाभा पृथिव्याः । मित्रो अग्निरीड्र्यो मातरिश्वादूतो वक्षद्यजथाय देवान् ।

(Khi. Saṃ. 9, 25-9).

p. 300

In this Ṛk Sāyaṇa explains the word मातरिश्वा (mātariśvā) as मातर्यंतरिक्षे श्वसिति प्राणिति सूर्यरूपेण चेष्टत इति मातरिश्वा (mātaryaṃtarikṣe śvasiti prāṇiti sūryarūpeṇa ceṣṭata iti mātariśvā) or मातररण्यां श्वसिति निवसतीति मातरिश्वा (mātararaṇyāṃ śvasiti nivasatīti mātariśvā): Agni has this name either because he moves in the atmosphere in the form of the sun, or because he dwells in the mother-like fire-sticks. He has shown support for his explanation by saying that the Nirukta-writers too show this same etymology and take it to mean Agni. Likewise,

तं शुभ्रमग्निमवसे हवामहे वैश्वानरं मातरिश्वानमुक्थं । बृहस्पतिं मनुषो देवतातये विप्रं श्रोतारमतिथिं रघुष्यदं ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-26-2)

in this Ṛk, and in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-96-4 (स मातरिश्वा पुरुवारपुष्टिः (sa mātariśvā puruvārapuṣṭiḥ)), the identity of Agni and Mātariśvan is stated. And as is said in the present Ṛk (1-143-2),

उदस्तंभीत्समिधा नाकमृष्टोग्नि र्भवन्नुत्तमो रोचमानां । यदी भृगुभ्यः परि मातरिश्वा गुहा संतं हव्यवाहं समाधे ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-5-10)

in this Ṛk it is clearly stated that the two are distinct. [But this is the very sentence of Ṛk 3-5-9 above, which states the identity of Agni and Mātariśvan, or says that the word मातरिश्वा (mātariśvā) is an epithet of Agni.]NOTE

The other qualities and the power of Mātariśvan will be explained later in the contexts suitable to them.

Grammar
  • जायमानः— जनी प्रादुर्भावे धातुः । लडर्थे शानच् प्रत्ययः । श्यन् विकरणम् । ज्ञाजनोर्जा (पा.सू. ७-३-७९) इति जादेशः । आने मुक् (पा.सू. ७-२-८२) इति सूत्रेण अदंतस्य मुकागमः । अदुपदेशस्य परत्र लसार्वधातुकस्य आगतत्वात् तास्यनुदात्तेत् (पा. सू. ६-१-१४६) इति तदनुदात्तं भवति । श्यन् नित्त्वात् आद्युदात्तस्वरः भवति ।
  • मातरिश्वने— मातरि स्वयतीति मारिश्वा । श्वन्नुक्सन् (उ. सू. १-१५७) इति कनि प्रत्ययांतत्वेन निपातितम् । चतुर्थी एकवचनांतरूपम् । प्रत्ययस्वरेण इकार उदात्तो भवति ।

p. 301

  • क्रत्वा— क्रतु+आ इति सति जसादिषु छंदसि वाचनम् इति वचनेन नाभावः न भवति । यणादेशः ।
  • समिधानस्य— इंधी दिप्तौ धातुः । लडर्थे शानच् प्रत्ययः । बहुलंछंदसि इति विकरणस्य लुक् । प्रत्ययस्य जित्त्वात् अनिदितां इति उपधानकारलोपः । शानच् चित्त्वात् चितः (पा. सू. ६-१-१६३) इति अंतोदात्तस्वरः भवति । षष्ठीएकवचनांतरूपम् ।
  • मज्मना— टुमस्टो शुद्ध धातुः । अस्मात् औणादिको मनि प्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्वरेण मध्योदात्तो भवति ।NOTE
  • द्यावापृथिवी— दौश्च पृथिवी च द्यावापृथिव्यौ दिवोद्यावा (पा.सू. ६-३-२९) इति पूर्वपदस्य द्यावादेशः । छांदसत्वेन मध्ये शोचिः इति शब्दः आगतः । सुपां सुलुक् (पा. सू. ७-३-३९) इति द्वितीयाविभक्तेः पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घः भवति ।
  • अरोचयत्— रुच दीप्तौ धातुः । हेतुमति च (पा. सू. ६-१-३९) इति प्रयोजकव्यापारे द्योत्यमाने णिच् । पुगंतलघूपधस्यच इति लघूपधगुणः । लङ् प्रथमपुरुष एकवचनांतरूपम् । तिजंतनिघातस्वरः भवति । ॥ २ ॥

Ṛk 3

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

अ॒स्य त्वे॒षा अ॒जरा॑ अ॒स्य भा॒नवः॑ सुसं॒दृशः॑ सु॒प्रती॑कस्य सु॒द्युतः॑।
भात्व॑क्षसो॒ अत्य॒क्तुर्न सिंध॑वो॒ऽग्ने रे॑जंते॒ अस॑संतो ॒॑ अजराः ॥ ३ ॥

asya tveṣā ajarā asya bhānavaḥ susaṃdṛśaḥ supratīkasya sudyutaḥ| bhātvakṣaso atyakturna siṃdhavo 'gne rejaṃte asasaṃto ajarāḥ ‖ 3 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

अस्य । त्वेषाः । अजराः । अस्य । भानवः । सुसंदृशः । सुप्रतीकस्य । सुद्युतः ।
भात्वक्षसः । अति । अक्तुः । न । सिंधवः । अग्नेः । रेजंते । अससंतः । अजराः ॥ ३ ॥

asya | tveṣāḥ | ajarāḥ | asya | bhānavaḥ | susaṃdṛśaḥ | supratīkasya | sudyutaḥ | bhātvakṣasaḥ | ati | aktuḥ | na | siṃdhavaḥ | agneḥ | rejaṃte | asasaṃtaḥ | ajarāḥ ‖ 3 ‖

p. 302

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

अस्य स्तूयमानस्याग्नेस्तेषा दीप्तयोऽजरा जरारहिता अजीर्णाः । अविरता इत्यर्थः ॥ नञ्चो जरमरेत्यादिनोत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वं ॥ तथा सुप्रतीकस्य शोभनमुखस्यास्याग्नेर्भानवो रश्मयः । दीप्तेरुक्तत्वादत्र विस्फुलिंगा अवगंतव्याः । ते च सुसंदृशः सुष्टु सम्यग्रष्टारः । सर्वतो व्याप्ता इत्यर्थः । सुद्युतः सुष्टु सर्वतो द्योतमानाः । तथास्याग्नेर्भात्वक्षसः । त्वक्ष इति बलनाम त्वक्षः शर्ध इति बलनामसु पाठात् । भासमानबलाः । अक्तुरिति रात्रिनामैतत् अक्तुरूर्म्योति तन्नामसूक्तत्वात् । द्वितीयार्थे प्रथमा । आक्तुं जगदंजकं नैशं तमोऽत्यतिक्रम्य सिंधवः स्यंदमानाः सर्वत्र व्याप्नुवंतोऽससंतः स्वव्यापारेष्वस्वपंतोऽविरताः अत एवाजरा न रेजंते । न कंपंते । दाहपाकादिषु न चलंति न चाल्यंते वानैः । यद्वा । नशब्दो दृष्टांतवचनः । भात्वक्षसो भा एव त्वक्षो बलं यस्य तादृशस्यादित्यस्य सिंधवो न रश्मय इव । ते यथा स्यंदनशीला व्याप्तिमंतोऽक्तुरति अंजकं तमोऽतिक्रम्याससंतो रेजंते तद्वद्दात्वक्षसोs स्याग्नेरुक्तलक्षणा दीप्तयोऽपि सर्वत्र रेजंते । कंपंते । व्याप्नुवंतीत्यर्थः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

Of this Agni who is being praised, the radiances (त्वेषाः (tveṣāḥ)) are अजराः (ajarāḥ): free of old age, undecaying, that is, unceasing. The accent on the first syllable of the second member follows the rule beginning नञ्चो जरमर (nañco jaramara). Likewise the rays (भानवः (bhānavaḥ)) of this Agni of fair face (सुप्रतीकस्य (supratīkasya)); since radiance has been mentioned, sparks are to be understood here. They are सुसंदृशः (susaṃdṛśaḥ), well and fully seen, that is, spread everywhere; and सुद्युतः (sudyutaḥ), shining well in all directions. Likewise of this Agni who is भात्वक्षसः (bhātvakṣasaḥ): त्वक्ष (tvakṣa) is a name for strength, since त्वक्षः शर्ध (tvakṣaḥ śardha) is read among the names of strength; thus "of shining strength". अक्तुः (aktuḥ) is a name of night, as it is recited among its names (अक्तुरूर्म्योति (akturūrmyoti) etc.); the nominative stands in the sense of the accusative. Passing beyond the night-darkness that smears the world, the सिंधवः (siṃdhavaḥ), flowing and pervading everywhere, अससंतः (asasaṃtaḥ), not sleeping in their own activities, unceasing, and therefore undecaying, न रेजंते (na rejaṃte) do not tremble; in burning, cooking and so on they do not waver, nor are they moved by winds.

Or else: the word न (na) expresses comparison. Like the rays of the sun, whose strength is light itself (भात्वक्षसः (bhātvakṣasaḥ)), which, flowing and pervasive, pass beyond the smearing darkness and without sleep रेजंते (rejaṃte) shine tremulously, so the radiances of this Agni, of the stated character, tremble, that is, pervade, everywhere.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • अस्य (asya)—of this Agni
  • त्वेषाः (tveṣāḥ)—the radiances
  • अजराः (ajarāḥ)—free of decay
  • सुप्रतीकस्य (supratīkasya)—of him with excellent face
  • अस्य (asya)—of this Agni
  • भानवः (bhānavaḥ)—rays (sparks)
  • सुसंदृशः (susaṃdṛśaḥ)—pervading so as to be visible to all
  • सुद्युतः (sudyutaḥ)—very bright
  • अग्नेः (agneḥ)—of Agni
  • भात्वक्षसः (bhātvakṣasaḥ)—the powers of the nature of light
  • अक्तुः (aktuḥ)—the darkness that pervades (the world)
  • अति (ati)—pushing through (piercing)
  • सिंधवः (siṃdhavaḥ)—flowing ones
  • अससंतः (asasaṃtaḥ)—without interruption (in their activities)
  • अजराः (ajarāḥ)—not wasting
  • न रेजंते (na rejaṃte)—do not hold back (in their tasks)
  • (Or) भात्वक्षसः (bhātvakṣasaḥ)—of the sun, whose strength is of the nature of light
  • सिंधवो न (siṃdhavo na)—like rays
  • अक्तुः अति (aktuḥ ati)—piercing the darkness
  • अससंतः (asasaṃtaḥ)—without the least interruption (in their duties)
  • रेजंते (rejaṃte)—pervade in the form of tremor
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The radiances of Agni are undecaying. The sparks, the instruments of this Agni of excellent face, pervade so as to be visible to all and are exceedingly bright. The brilliance of this Agni, like the rays of the sun whose strength is of the nature of light, pierces the darkness that envelops the world and, with uninterrupted activity, unwasting, pervades the world.

p. 303

Printed English

His radiance is undecaying ; the rays of him who is of pleasing aspect, are everywhere visible and bright : the intensely shining, all-pervading, unceasing, undecaying (rays) of Agni, desist not (from their functions).

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk the radiance of Agni, and his power of the nature of light, destroying the black darkness and ever intent on its duty, are described.

सुप्रतीकस्य (supratīkasya)—प्रतीकं मुखं प्रकाशाख्यं दर्शनं वा (pratīkaṃ mukhaṃ prakāśākhyaṃ darśanaṃ vā). The word प्रतीक (pratīka) means either face or a radiant appearance. The Nirukta-writer, quoting

यावन्मात्रमुषसो न प्रतीकं सुपर्ण्यो३वसते मातरिश्वः । तावद्दधात्युप यज्ञमायन् ब्राह्मणो होतुरवरो निषिदन् ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-88-19)

has taken it in the sense of radiant appearance. Here the word is used so as to include both meanings: the shining face of the Agni who has appeared.

भानवः (bhānavaḥ)—The word भानु (bhānu) can mean both the sun and rays.

उदपप्तन्नरुणा भानवो वृथा स्वायुजो अरुषीर्गा आयुक्षत । अक्रन्नुषासो वयुनानि पूर्वथा रुशंतं भानुमरुषी रशिश्रयुः ।

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-92-2)

In this Ṛk the golden-hued radiances of the Ushas goddesses darted upward .... .... .... .... then, joined with their splendour, they united with the bright-hued sun; thus both meanings of भानु (bhānu) appear in one Ṛk. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa,

कविशस्तो बृहता भानुनागा हव्या जुषस्व ।

(Ai. Brā. 2-12)

Agni is entreated: "Come with your great splendour and be gracious." Likewise here too the meaning is the radiant rays of Agni.

सुसंदृशः (susaṃdṛśaḥ)—सुष्टु सम्यग्रष्टारः । सर्वतो व्याप्ता इत्यर्थः । (suṣṭu samyagraṣṭāraḥ | sarvato vyāptā ityarthaḥ |) The meaning is: pervading so as to be visible to all.

p. 304

अक्तुः (aktuḥ)—This word is read among the 23 names of night, श्यावी, क्षपा, शर्वरी (śyāvī, kṣapā, śarvarī) and so on (Ni. 1-18). In many places अक्तु (aktu) means just night. The word is also used in the senses of darkness, ray, weapon and so on. Since the root अंज् (aṃj) has the meanings cover, conceal, smear, the meanings arise: darkness that covers with shade; a ray that envelops all around; a weapon that covers the body. For example:

घनेव विष्वग्वि जह्यराष्ट्रपुर्जंभ यो अस्मध्रुक् । यो मर्त्यः शिशीते अत्यक्तुभिर्मा नः स रिपुरीशत ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-36-16)

In this Ṛk the word अक्तुभिः (aktubhiḥ) is explained as अवरकैरायुधैः (avarakairāyudhaiḥ). But in this meaning the word is used rarely. Its use in the meanings darkness, and night enveloped by darkness, is more frequent.

उत्तानायामजनयन्तुषूतं भुवदग्निः पुरुषेशासु गर्भः । शिरिणायां चिदक्तुना महोभिरपरीवृतो वसति प्रचेताः ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-10-3)

In such Ṛks, अक्तुना (aktunā) is explained as अंजनादक्तुस्तमः (aṃjanādaktustamaḥ): darkness is अक्तु (aktu) because it pervades. So in the present Ṛk too the meaning is the darkness that pervades the world. The radiance of Agni drives out such black darkness.

अससंतः (asasaṃtaḥ)—स्वव्यापारेषु अस्वसंतः अविरताः (svavyāpāreṣu asvasaṃtaḥ aviratāḥ). The meaning is: in their own activities, without sloth, with unbroken devotion to work. The Nirukta-writer, quoting

अति वायो ससतो याहि शश्वतो यत्र ग्रावा वदति तत्र गच्छतं गृहमिंद्रश्च गच्छतं । वि सूनृता ददृशे रीयते धृतमा पूर्णया नियुता याथो अध्वरमिंद्रश्च याथो अध्वरं ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-135-7)

explains ससतः (sasataḥ) as अलस्यादिना निद्रां कुर्वतः (alasyādinā nidrāṃ kurvataḥ). The meaning is: without such sloth and sleep, ever engaged in their activities.

भात्वक्षसः (bhātvakṣasaḥ)—त्वक्ष इति बलनाम, 'त्वक्षः, शर्धः' इति बलनामसु (नि३-९) पाठात् । भासमानबलाः । (tvakṣa iti balanāma, 'tvakṣaḥ, śardhaḥ ' iti balanāmasu (ni3-9) pāṭhāt | bhāsamānabalāḥ |) The word त्वक्ष (tvakṣa) is read among the names of strength. The meaning is: powers of the nature of light.

p. 305

Special Topics (continued)

इंद्रियं वीर्यमात्मनत्ते तेजो ना अग्निरिंद्रियं वीर्यमिंद्र उभे वीर्ये । ( (iṃdriyaṃ vīryamātmanatte tejo nā agniriṃdriyaṃ vīryamiṃdra ubhe vīrye | () (Śa. Brā. 5-2-3-9). As described in such passages, Agni's powers in the form of radiance are described here too.

Sāyaṇa has shown that the second half of this Ṛk admits two constructions. First: the words सिंधवः (siṃdhavaḥ), अससंतः (asasaṃtaḥ) and अजराः (ajarāḥ) are adjectives of भात्वक्षसः (bhātvakṣasaḥ). The radiant powers are flowing, unbroken in their operations, and undiminished; and न रेजंते (na rejaṃte) is taken in negative form: they do not shrink back from their works.

Second: न शब्दो दृष्टांतवचनः । भात्वक्षसो भा एव त्वक्षो बलं यस्य तादृशस्यादित्यस्य सिंधवो न रश्मय इव । ते यथा स्यंदनशीला व्याप्तिमंतः अक्तुरति अंजकं तमः अतिक्रम्य अससंतो रेजंते तद्वत् भात्वक्षसोऽस्याग्नेरुक्तलक्षणा दीप्तयोऽपि सर्वत्र रेजंते कंपंते व्याप्नुवंतीत्यर्थः । (na śabdo dṛṣṭāṃtavacanaḥ | bhātvakṣaso bhā eva tvakṣo balaṃ yasya tādṛśasyādityasya siṃdhavo na raśmaya iva | te yathā syaṃdanaśīlā vyāptimaṃtaḥ akturati aṃjakaṃ tamaḥ atikramya asasaṃto rejaṃte tadvat bhātvakṣaso 'syāgneruktalakṣaṇā dīptayo 'pi sarvatra rejaṃte kaṃpaṃte vyāpnuvaṃtītyarthaḥ |). Here the word न (na) expresses a simile. Just as the rays of the sun, which has strength in the form of radiance, pierce the darkness, and without the least break in their duties pervade the world with a quivering motion, so too the rays of Agni pervade; this, Sāyaṇa explains, is the meaning.

Grammar
  • तेषाः — त्रिष दीप्तौ इति धातुः । पचादिषु पाठाद् अच् प्रत्ययः । तं निमित्तीकृत्य धातोर्लघूपधस्य गुणः । चित्त्वात् अंतोदात्तस्वरो भवति । NOTE
  • अजराः — न विद्यते जरा येषां ते अजराः । नञ्स्वरं बाधित्वा नञ्योजरमः (पा. सू. ६-२-११६) इति उत्तरपदस्य अमृदात्तस्वरो भवति । NOTE
  • अस्य — ऊडिदंपदादि (पा. सू ६-१-१७१) इति विभक्तेरुदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
  • भानवः — भा वीप्त धातुः । दाभाभ्यांनुः (उ. सू. २-३०-२) इति नु प्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तो भवति ।
  • सुसंदृशः — दृशिर् प्रेक्षणे धातुः । क्विप् प्रत्ययः । गतिकारकोपपदात् कृत् (पा. सू. ६-२-१३९) इति कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति । प्रथमाबहुवचनांतरूपम् ।
  • सुप्रतीकस्य — शोभनं प्रतीकं यस्य सः सुप्रतीकः तस्य । क्रत्वादयश्च (पा. सू. ६-२-११८) इति उत्तरपदस्य आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति ।

p. 306

Grammar (continued) - भात्वक्षसः — भाः एव त्वक्षः बलं यस्य सः भात्वक्षाः । बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या पूर्वपदम् (पा. सू. ६-२-१) इति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति । - रेजंते — रेज्य कंपने धातुः । लट् प्रथमपुरुषबहुवचनांतरूपम् । अतिजंतस्य परत्वात् निघातस्वरो भवति । - अससंतः — न ससंतः अससंतः । षस स्वष्टे धातुः । लडर्थे शतृ प्रत्ययः । प्रथमाबहुवचनांतरूपम् । तत्पुरुषे तुल्यार्थ (पा. सू. ६-२-२) इति नञ्प्रकृतिस्वरो भवति ।

Ṛk 4

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

यमे॑रि॒रे भृग॑वो वि॒श्ववे॑दसं॒ नाभा॑ पृथि॒व्या भुव॑नस्य ॒॑ मज्मना ।
अ॒ग्निं तं गी॒र्भिर्हि॑नुहि॒ स्व आ दमे॒ य एको॒ वस्वो॒ ॒॑ ॑ वरुणो न राजति ॥ ४ ॥

yamerire bhṛgavo viśvavedasaṃ nābhā pṛthivyā bhuvanasya majmanā | agniṃ taṃ gīrbhirhinuhi sva ā dame ya eko vasvo varuṇo na rājati ‖ 4 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

यं । आईरिरे । भृगवः । विश्ववेदसं । नाभा । पृथिव्याः । भुवनस्य । मज्मना ।
अग्निं । तं । गीःभिः । हिनुहि । स्वे । आ । दमे । यः । एकः । वस्वः । वरुणः । न ।
राजति ॥ ४ ॥

yaṃ | āīrire | bhṛgavaḥ | viśvavedasaṃ | nābhā | pṛthivyāḥ | bhuvanasya | majmanā | agniṃ | taṃ | gīḥbhiḥ | hinuhi | sve | ā | dame | yaḥ | ekaḥ | vasvaḥ | varuṇaḥ | na | rājati ‖ 4 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

विश्ववेदसं सर्वधनं । वेद इति धननाम वेदो वरिव इति तन्नामसु पाठात् । तादृशं यमग्निं भृगवो भृगुगोत्रोत्पन्नाः पापस्य भर्जकाः पृथिव्या वेद्याः । एकदेशे कृत्स शब्दः । यद्वा । एतावती वै पृथिवीत्यादिश्रुतेर्वेद्याः

Gist of the bhāṣya

विश्ववेदसं (viśvavedasaṃ) means "possessing all wealth"; वेदः (vedaḥ) is a word for wealth, since "veda, variva" are read among the names of wealth. Agni, such as he is, was placed by the Bhṛgus—those born in the Bhṛgu lineage, the burners of sin—on the "navel" of the earth, that is, of the altar (the word कृत्स (kṛtsa) being used for a part of it). Or else, on the authority of the śruti beginning एतावती वै पृथिवी (etāvatī vai pṛthivī), the altar has the nature of the earth. (The sentence continues on the next page.)

p. 307

पृथिवीत्वं । तस्या नाभावुत्तरवेद्यां भुवनस्य भूतजातस्य मज्मना बलेन निमित्तेना अभिमुख्यनेरिरे ईरितवंतः स्थापितवंतः तमग्निं स्वे स्वकीये दमे गृह उत्तरवेद्यां गीर्भिः स्तुतिभिरा हिनुहि । प्राप्नुहि ॥ हि गतौ वृद्धौ च । उतश्च प्रत्ययाच्चंदसि नावचनमिति हेर्लुगभावः ॥ योऽग्निरेको मुख्यः सन् एक एव वा वसो वसुनो गवादिधनस्य राजति ईश्वरो भवति । प्रदातुमिति शेषः । राजतीत्यैश्वर्यकर्मा क्षियति राजतीति तन्नामसु पाठात् । तत्र दृष्टांतः । वरुणो न वारक आदित्य इव । स यथा सर्वस्येष्टे तद्वत् ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

On the navel of that earth, the northern altar (uttaravedi), by the strength (मज्मना (majmanā)) of all beings (भुवनस्य (bhuvanasya)) as the cause, the Bhṛgus set Agni before them (ईरिरे (īrire): they set him up, established him). "That Agni, in your own house (दमे (dame)), on the uttaravedi, bring (हिनुहि (hinuhi): reach, obtain) with songs of praise." The root हि (hi) means going and growth; the non-elision of the हि (hi) follows the rule उतश्च प्रत्ययाच्छंदसि ना वचनम् (utaśca pratyayācchaṃdasi nā vacanam). The Agni who, being the chief, or being alone, rules over wealth (वसो (vaso)), cows and the like—he is lord, to bestow it, is the supplied remainder. राजति (rājati) is a word of lordship, since "kṣiyati, rājati" are read among those names. The comparison: वरुणो न (varuṇo na) is "like the restrainer, Āditya"; as he rules over everything, so does Agni.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • यः (yaḥ)—which Agni
  • वरुणो न (varuṇo na)—like Āditya
  • एकः (ekaḥ)—being the sole lord
  • वस्वः (vasvaḥ)—of all wealth such as cows
  • राजति (rājati)—is the master
  • विश्ववेवसं (viśvavevasaṃ)—possessing all wealth
  • यं (yaṃ)—whom Agni
  • भृगवः (bhṛgavaḥ)—the sages born in the lineage of Bhṛgu
  • पृथिव्याः (pṛthivyāḥ)—of the altar
  • नाभा (nābhā)—on the northern part
  • भुवनस्य (bhuvanasya)—of all beings
  • मज्मना (majmanā)—by the strength
  • आ (ā)—facing
  • ईरिरे (īrire)—have established
  • तं अग्निं (taṃ agniṃ)—that Agni
  • स्वे दमे (sve dame)—in your (Agni's) own house (on the northern altar)
  • गीर्भिः (gīrbhiḥ)—with praises
  • आ हिनुहि (ā hinuhi)—bring and establish
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Agni who, like Āditya, is the sole lord and master of all wealth such as cows, and whom all the sages born in the lineage of Bhṛgu have established, with all their strength, on the northern part of the altar, that possessor of all wealth: bring him with praises to the northern altar of your own house and establish him.

Printed English

Bring to his own abode with hymns that Agni, the possessor of all riches, whom the descendants of Bhrigu placed by the strength of all beings upon the navel of the earth : for, like Veruna, he reigns sole (monarch) over (all) treasure.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk, after praising Agni as the sole lord and master of all wealth, the sacrificer is told to bring such an Agni, possessor of all wealth and established on the northern part of the altar.

p. 308

वरुणो न (varuṇo na)—here the word Varuṇa is explained as Āditya the restrainer. Agni's lordship is compared to the sole lordship of Āditya.

राजति (rājati)—"kṣiyati, rājati" and so on are read among the names of verbs of lordship (Ni. 2-21). ईश्वरः भवति (īśvaraḥ bhavati)—he is lord of all wealth. In the Ṛk सप्त क्षरंति शिशवे मरुत्वते पित्रे पुत्रासो अप्यवीवतन्नृतं । उभे इदस्योभयस्य राजत उभे यतेते उभयस्य पुष्यतः । (sapta kṣaraṃti śiśave marutvate pitre putrāso apyavīvatannṛtaṃ | ubhe idasyobhayasya rājata ubhe yatete ubhayasya puṣyataḥ |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 18-13-5) NOTE, the Nirukta authors show as an example that the word राजतः (rājataḥ) gives the sense ईशाते (īśāte); the same sense results here too.

भृगवः ईरिरे (bhṛgavaḥ īrire)—भृगुगोत्रोत्पन्नाः स्थापितवंतः (bhṛgugotrotpannāḥ sthāpitavaṃtaḥ): this points to the old story that the sages born of the Bhṛgu line first established Agni in the house of sacrifice. In such Taittirīya Saṃhitā passages as अयमिह प्रथमो धायि धातृभिर्होता यजिष्ठो अध्वरेष्वीड्यः । यमप्नवानो भृगवो विरुरुचुर्वनेषु चित्रं विभुवं विशेषिविशे ॥ (ayamiha prathamo dhāyi dhātṛbhirhotā yajiṣṭho adhvareṣvīḍyaḥ | yamapnavāno bhṛgavo virurucurvaneṣu citraṃ vibhuvaṃ viśeṣiviśe ‖) (Kṛ. Saṃ. 1-5-1) NOTE, the matter of the Bhṛgus first establishing Agni as hotṛ is told. In the Ṛk Saṃhitā too, in Ṛks such as दधुष्टा भृगवः मानुषेष्वा रयिं न चारुं सुहवं जनेभ्यः । होतारमग्ने अतिथिं वरेण्यं मित्रं न शेवं दिव्याय जन्मने । (dadhuṣṭā bhṛgavaḥ mānuṣeṣvā rayiṃ na cāruṃ suhavaṃ janebhyaḥ | hotāramagne atithiṃ vareṇyaṃ mitraṃ na śevaṃ divyāya janmane |) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-58-6) and द्विता यदीं कीस्तासो अभिद्यवो नमस्यंत उपवोचंत भृगवो मथ्यंतो दाशा भृगवः । अग्निरीशे वसूनां शुचियोर्ण धर्णिरेषां । प्रिया अपिधीर्वनिषीष्ट मेधिर आ वनिषीष्ट मेधिरः ॥ (dvitā yadīṃ kīstāso abhidyavo namasyaṃta upavocaṃta bhṛgavo mathyaṃto dāśā bhṛgavaḥ | agnirīśe vasūnāṃ śuciyorṇa dharṇireṣāṃ | priyā apidhīrvaniṣīṣṭa medhira ā vaniṣīṣṭa medhiraḥ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-127-7), it is praised in many places that the Bhṛgus churned and established Agni in the house of sacrifice, and that Mātariśvan brought Agni from a distant region for these Bhṛgus. That circumstance is hinted at in the present Ṛk also.

p. 309

भृगवः (bhṛgavaḥ)—भ्रष्टारो हविषां पापानां भर्जका वा (bhraṣṭāro haviṣāṃ pāpānāṃ bharjakā vā): either those who offer oblations, or those who destroy sins. Sāyaṇa explains that these sages have this name because the word can be understood in either way and because they had both kinds of power.

The Nirukta authors, with अर्चिषि भृगुः संबभूव भृगुर्भृज्यमानो न देहे (arciṣi bhṛguḥ saṃbabhūva bhṛgurbhṛjyamāno na dehe) (Ni. 3-17), show the derivation of the word Bhṛgu: Bhṛgu, born of the flame, though inside Agni, was not burnt; hence the name. This undying power helps the great sacrificial work, and likewise the destruction of sin. In the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, अथांगारैरभ्यूहति । भृगूणामंगिरसां तपसा तप्यध्वमित्येतद्वै तेजो यद्भग्वंगिरसाग् सुतप्तान्यसन्निति तस्मादेनमभ्यूहति । (athāṃgārairabhyūhati | bhṛgūṇāmaṃgirasāṃ tapasā tapyadhvamityetadvai tejo yadbhagvaṃgirasāg sutaptānyasanniti tasmādenamabhyūhati |) (Ka. Brā. 1-2-1-3) NOTE. In such passages, since those born in the Bhṛgu line are direct relations of Agni, they are said to have extremely brilliant radiance. And, citing the Taittirīya Saṃhitā passages अयमिह प्रथमो धायि धातृभिर्होता यजिष्ठो अध्वरेष्टीड्यः (ayamiha prathamo dhāyi dhātṛbhirhotā yajiṣṭho adhvareṣṭīḍyaḥ) and so on (Śa. Brā. 2-3-4-14) and Tai. Saṃ. (1-5-5-1); and द्वे अग्नेर्जुहोति । द्विपाद्यजमानो यजमानोऽग्निर्यावानाग्निर्यावत्यस्य मात्रा तावतैवैतद्यज्ञग्ं सग्स्थापयतीष्टो यज्ञो भृगुभिरिष्टोऽग्निराहुतः पिपर्तु न इति । (dve agnerjuhoti | dvipādyajamāno yajamāno 'gniryāvānāgniryāvatyasya mātrā tāvataivaitadyajñagṃ sagsthāpayatīṣṭo yajño bhṛgubhiriṣṭo 'gnirāhutaḥ pipartu na iti |) (Pa. Brā. 9-5-1-31) NOTE. By such passages the manner in which the Bhṛgus worshipped Agni and performed sacrifice is also explained.

पृथिव्या नाभा भुवनस्य मज्मना ईरिरे (pṛthivyā nābhā bhuvanasya majmanā īrire)—by this mantra the manner in which the Bhṛgus established Agni is stated. Here पृथिव्या नाभा (pṛthivyā nābhā) is explained as the northern altar. As it is said in Saṃhitā passages such as उत्तरं परिग्राहं परि गृह्णात्येतावती वै पृथिवी यावती वेदिस्तस्या एतावत एव । (uttaraṃ parigrāhaṃ pari gṛhṇātyetāvatī vai pṛthivī yāvatī vedistasyā etāvata eva |) (Kṛ. Saṃ. 2-6-4-3) NOTE, that the earth itself is the altar, so it is explained here also. On such an altar in the form of the earth, gathering together the strength of all beings, the Bhṛgus established Agni.

p. 310

यद्वैतमत्राहरंति । यान्वै तान्सप्त पुरुषानेकं पुरुषमकुर्वन्नयमेव स योऽयमग्निश्चीयतेऽथ यामेषां तामूर्ध्वाग्ग् श्रियग्ं रसग्ं समुदौहन्नेष स यमेतमत्राग्निमाहरंति तद्यदेतमत्राहरंति यैवैतेषाग्‌ं सप्तानां पुरुषाणां श्रीर्यो रसस्तमेतदूर्ध्वग्ं समुद्वहंति तदस्यैतच्छिर आत्म्यायमग्निश्चित आत्मानमेवास्यैतत्संस्कृत्य शिरः प्रति दधाति ॥ (yadvaitamatrāharaṃti | yānvai tānsapta puruṣānekaṃ puruṣamakurvannayameva sa yo 'yamagniścīyate 'tha yāmeṣāṃ tāmūrdhvāgg śriyagṃ rasagṃ samudauhanneṣa sa yametamatrāgnimāharaṃti tadyadetamatrāharaṃti yaivaiteṣāgṃ saptānāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ śrīryo rasastametadūrdhvagṃ samudvahaṃti tadasyaitacchira ātmyāyamagniścita ātmānamevāsyaitatsaṃskṛtya śiraḥ prati dadhāti ‖) (Śa. Brā. 9-2-3-51). By such mantras, the matter explained there is hinted here too: that Agni, installed on the altar, is the essence of the seven persons who reflect all beings.

Grammar
  • ईरिरे — ईर गतौ प्रेरणे च धातुः । लिट्प्रथमपुरुषबहुवचने लिटस्तझयोरेशिरेच् इति इरे आदेशः । अतिजंतस्य परत्वात् निघातस्वरो भवति ।
  • विश्ववेदसम् — विश्वं वेदः यस्य सः विश्ववेदाः तन् विश्ववेदसम् । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति ।
  • नाभा — सुपां सुलुक् (पा. सू. ७-१-३९) इति विभक्तेः आकारादेशः ।
  • मज्मना — टुमस् जो शुद्ध धातुः । औणादिको मनि प्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्य आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति । तृतीयैकवचनांतरूपम् ।
  • गीर्भिः — गृ शब्दे धातुः । क्विप् च इति क्विप् प्रत्ययः । ऋत इद्दातोः (पा. सू. ७-१-१००) इति धातोरित्वं, गिर् शब्दो भवति । भिस् परे हलि च इति धातोरुपधाया दीर्घः ।
  • हिनुहि — हि गतौ वृद्भौ च धातुः । लोट्मध्यमपुरुषैकवचने सिपो हि आदेशः । स्वादिभ्य श्नुः इति श्नुविकरणम् । उतश्च प्रत्ययाच्छंदसि ना वचनम् (पा. सू. ६-४-१०६-१) इति हेर्लुक् न भवति । विकरणस्य सार्वधातुकमपित् इति चित्त्वात् तं निमित्तीकृत्य धातोर्गुणो न भवति । अतिजंतस्य परत्वात् तिजंतनिघातस्वरो भवति ।
  • वस्वः — वसु शब्दः । अस्मात् षष्ठीविभक्तौ परतः जसादिषु छंदसि ना वचनम् इति वचनात् नुम् । गुणादयो न भवंति । यणादेशः ।

p. 311

Grammar
  • राजति — राज धातुः ऐश्वर्य क्रियावाची । क्षयति राजति (निरु. २-२१-४) इति पठितम् । लट् प्रथमपुरुष एकवचनांतरूपम् । यः इति यच्छब्दसंबंधात् यद्वृत्तान्वित्यम् (पा. सू. ८-१-६६) इति निघातप्रतिषेधो भवति । शप् तिप् पित्तात् धातुस्वरो अवशिष्यते ।

Ṛk 5

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

न यो वरा॑य म॒रुता॑मिव स्व॒नः सेने॑व सृ॒ष्टा दि॒व्या ॒॑ यथाशनिः ।
अ॒ग्निर्जंभै॑स्तिगि॒तैर॑त्ति॒ भर्व॑ति यो॒धो न शत्रु॒न्त्स वना॒ ॑ न्यृंजते ॥ ५ ॥

na yo varāya marutāmiva svanaḥ seneva sṛṣṭā divyā yathāśaniḥ | agnirjaṃbhaistigitairatti bharvati yodho na śatruntsa vanā nyṛṃjate ‖ 5 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

न । यः । वराय । मरुतांइव । स्वनः । सेनाइव । सृष्टा । दिव्या । यथा । अशनिः ।
अग्निः । जंभैः । तिगितैः । अत्ति । भर्वति । योधः । न शत्रून् । सः । वना । नि । ऋंजते ।
॥ ५ ॥

na | yaḥ | varāya | marutāṃiva | svanaḥ | senāiva | sṛṣṭā | divyā | yathā | aśaniḥ | agniḥ | jaṃbhaiḥ | tigitaiḥ | atti | bharvati | yodhaḥ | na śatrūn | saḥ | vanā | ni | ṛṃjate | ‖ 5 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

योऽग्निर्वराय वरणाय निग्रहाय न शक्तो न भवति । तत्र दृष्टांतत्रयमुच्यते । मरुतां स्वन इव । स यथाग्राह्यस्तद्वत् । तथा सृष्टा वैरिक्षयार्थं प्रबलेनातिसृष्टा सेनेव । सा यथानैरनिरोध्या तद्यत् । तथा दिव्या दिवि भवाशनिर्यथा पतत्येव न निवार्यते तद्वत् । ईदृक् सामर्थ्यमस्तीति दर्शयति । अयमग्निस्तिगितैर्निशितैस्तीक्ष्णीभूतैः ॥ अंत्यविकारश्चांदसः ॥ जंभैर्दंतैर्दंतस्थानीयाभिर्ज्वालाभिरत्ति । अस्मद्विरोधिनो भक्षयति । तथा भर्वति । हिनस्ति ॥ भर्व हिंसायां ॥ यास्कस्वाह भर्वतिरत्तिकर्मेति । नि ९-२३ । यद्यप्यत्तिभर्वत्योरदनमेवार्थः तथापि तदवांतरभेदोऽवगंतव्यः । तत्र दृष्टांतः । योधो न संप्रहर्ता शूर

Gist of the bhāṣya

The Agni who is not able to be checked (वराय (varāya) = वरणाय (varaṇāya), निग्रहाय (nigrahāya), "for restraining"). Three illustrations are given. He is like the roar of the Maruts, which cannot be seized; like an army let loose with great force for the destruction of enemies, which cannot be obstructed; and like the heavenly thunderbolt, which, as it falls, is not warded off. Thus the verse shows his might.
