  • (आहवम् इत्यस्य शेषः) अवादेशः । समासे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति । अथवा आजियुद्धे (पा. सू. ३-३-७३) इति आगतः अप् प्रत्ययः व्यत्ययेन अत्रापि भवति । NOTE

Here the 155th sūkta ends.

Sūkta 156 (Maṇḍala 1)

[[b-intro not separate]] Introduction The printed Sanskrit introduction: the sūkta भवा मित्र (bhavā mitra) of five Ṛks is the seventeenth sūkta; it is by Dīrghatamas, of the Dairghatamasa line; since it is said "jāgata" it is also jāgata (Jagatī metre); since "vaiṣṇava" is said, it is Viṣṇu's; the Anukramaṇī says भव पंच (bhava paṃca). It is applied in the Ukthya rite, at the third pressing, for the Acchāvāka's recitation; the Sūtra in the section उक्ष्ये तु होत्रकाणामिति (ukṣye tu hotrakāṇāmiti) prescribes it: भवा मित्रः सं नां कर्मणा (bhavā mitraḥ saṃ nāṃ karmaṇā) (Ā. 6-1). In the Saumya-caru, ghee is to be used on both sides; in the upper ghee-offering the ordinary yājyā is उरु विष्णो वि क्रमस्व (uru viṣṇo vi kramasva); on the tenth day this Ṛk भवा मित्र (bhavā mitra) is to be used in its place, as the section दशमेऽहनि (daśame 'hani) states: उरु विष्णो वि क्रमस्वीति धृतयज्यास्थाने भवा मित्रः (uru viṣṇo vi kramasvīti dhṛtayajyāsthāne bhavā mitraḥ) (Ā. 8-12).

Anuvāda. This sūkta भवा मित्र (bhavā mitra) is the seventeenth sūkta in the twenty-first anuvāka. It has five Ṛks. Its seer is Dīrghatamas, son of Ucathya; the deity is Viṣṇu; the metre Jagatī. The Anukramaṇī says "bhava pañca". In the Ukthya sacrifice, at the third pressing, the priest called Acchāvāka is to recite this sūkta, as explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the section "Ukthe tu hotrāṇām", by the sūtra "Bhavā mitraḥ saṃ nāṃ karmaṇā" (Ā. 6-1). In both caru-oblations connected with Soma, ghee is to be used; in this ghee-offering the Ṛk "Uru viṣṇo vi kramasva" is to be used as the ordinary yājyā; but on the tenth day the Ṛk "Bhavā mitra" is to be used in place of it, as the sūtra "Uru viṣṇo vikramasveti dhṛtayājyāsthāne bhavā mitraḥ" in the section "Daśame 'hani" of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra directs (Ā. 8-12).

p. 640

Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 21, Sūkta 156; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 2, Varga 26. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 5. Seer: Dīrghatamas Aucathya. Deity: Viṣṇu. Metre: Jagatī.

Ṛk 1

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

भवा॑ मि॒त्रो न शेव्यो॑ घृ॒तासु॑ति॒र्विभू॑तद्युम्न एव॒या उ॑ ॒॑ सप्रथाः ।
अधा॑ ते विष्णो वि॒दुषा॑ चि॒दर्ध्यः॒ स्तोमो॑ य॒ज्ञश्च॒ राध्यो॑ ॒॑ हविष्मता ॥ १ ॥

bhavā mitro na śevyo ghṛtāsutirvibhūtadyumna evayā u saprathāḥ | adhā te viṣṇo viduṣā cidardhyaḥ stomo yajñaśca rādhyo haviṣmatā ‖ 1 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

भव । मित्रः । न । शेव्यः । धृतआसुतिः । विभूतद्युम्नः । एवयाः । ऊं इति ।
सप्रथाः ।
अध । ते । विष्णो इति । विदुषा । चित् । अध्य ९ः । स्तोमः । यज्ञः । च । राध्यः ।
हविष्मता ॥ १ ॥

bhava | mitraḥ | na | śevyaḥ | dhṛtaāsutiḥ | vibhūtadyumnaḥ | evayāḥ | ūṃ iti | saprathāḥ | adha | te | viṣṇo iti | viduṣā | cit | adhya 9ḥ | stomaḥ | yajñaḥ | ca | rādhyaḥ | haviṣmatā ‖ 1 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे विष्णो मित्रो न । मितेर्दुःखात् त्राता सखा आदित्यो ना मित्रः । प्रमीतेस्त्रायत इति निरुक्तं । १०-२१ । तद्वत् शेव्यः सुखे साधुः सुखकर्ता घृतासुतिः

Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Viṣṇu, like Mitra": Mitra is the friend, the Āditya who saves from distress; he cites Nirukta 10-21, प्रमीतेस्त्रायत इति (pramītestrāyata iti). Like him, Viṣṇu is शेव्यः (śevyaḥ), good at giving happiness, the maker of happiness, and घृतासुतिः (ghṛtāsutiḥ) (continued in the next block).

p. 641

धृतमुदकमासूयते येन स तादृशः । यद्वा । धृतमाज्यमाभिमुख्येन नीयते यस्मै स तादृशः । विभूतद्युम्नः प्रभूतयशाः प्रभूतान्नो वा । एवया रक्षणस्य मिश्रयिता प्रापयिता । सप्रथाः सर्वतः पृथुः । प्रतिविशेषणं नो भवेति संबंधः ॥ द्व्यचोऽतस्तिज इति दीर्घः । उ इति पादपूरणः ॥ हे विष्णो त्वं यस्मादीवृशो भवसि अधास्मात्ते तव स्तोमः स्तोत्रविशेषो विदुषा त्वन्माहात्म्यवेदित्रा यजमानेनार्ध्यः पुनः पुनः प्रवर्धनार्हः । एकवारकरणे न संपूर्यत इत्यर्थः । तथा ते यज्ञश्च हविष्मता तेन यजमानेन राध्यः समाराधनीयः । यद्वा । विदुषा होत्रा स्तोमो राध्यो हविष्मता यज्ञश्च राध्यः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

घृतासुतिः (ghṛtāsutiḥ): he by whom water is pressed out; or else he to whom ghee is brought face to face. विभूतद्युम्नः (vibhūtadyumnaḥ): of abundant fame, or of abundant food. एवयाः (evayāḥ): the one who brings or bestows protection. सप्रथाः (saprathāḥ): broad on all sides. Each of these epithets is connected with "be to us". उ (u) is a verse-filler. O Viṣṇu, since you are such, therefore your स्तोमः (stomaḥ), a special praise, is अर्ध्यः (ardhyaḥ) for the knowing sacrificer who knows your greatness: fit to be furthered again and again; it is not completed by being done once. Likewise your sacrifice is राध्यः (rādhyaḥ), to be accomplished by that sacrificer who has the oblation. Or else: the praise is to be accomplished by the knowing Hotṛ, and the sacrifice by the sacrificer with the oblation.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • मित्रो न (mitro na)—like a friend, or like the Āditya in the form of Mitra
  • शेव्यः (śevyaḥ)—the giver of happiness
  • धृतासुतिः (dhṛtāsutiḥ)—the accepter of the offering of ghee
  • विभूतद्युम्नः (vibhūtadyumnaḥ)—having abundant fame, or abundant food
  • एवयाः (evayāḥ)—the giver of protection
  • सप्रथाः (saprathāḥ)—easily approachable on every side
  • भव (bhava)—be (in our regard)
  • विष्णो (viṣṇo)—O Viṣṇu
  • अध (adha)—because you are filled with these qualities
  • ते (te)—your
  • स्तोमः (stomaḥ)—special praise
  • विदुषा (viduṣā)—by the sacrificer who knows (your greatness)
  • अर्ध्यः (ardhyaḥ)—to be recited again and again
  • यज्ञश्च (yajñaśca)—and the sacrifice (directed to you)
  • हविष्मता (haviṣmatā)—by the sacrificer who has the oblation
  • राध्यः (rādhyaḥ)—to be accomplished
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Viṣṇu, be to us like a friend: the giver of happiness, the accepter of the ghee offering, of abundant fame, the giver of protection, and easily approachable on every side. O Viṣṇu, since you are filled with these qualities, your special praise is to be recited again and again by the sacrificer who knows your greatness; and the sacrifice directed to you is also to be accomplished by the sacrificer who has the oblation.

Printed English

Be (to us), Vishnu, like a friend, the giver of happiness, the accepter of oblations, abounding with food, the granter of protection, and every way accessible; on which account your praise is to be repeatedly recited by the wise, and your worship to be celebrated by the offerer of oblations.

p. 642

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk Vishnu is compared to Mitra. The word Mitra is explained here in two ways: it may mean the worldly friend, or Mitra in the form of Āditya, who has the qualities of that friend. To show that the same benefits of happiness and joy that come from a friend come to the world from Mitra in the form of Āditya, the Nirukta-writer has given a derivation of this word— मित्रः प्रमीतेस्त्रायते । संमिन्वानो द्रवतीति वा । मेदयतेर्वा । (mitraḥ pramītestrāyate | saṃminvāno dravatīti vā | medayatervā |) Yāska explains that the name Mitra arises either from protecting from destruction, or from moving about while measuring (examining) all principles, or from nourishing the world by giving it food and the like and so making the world well-fed. (Ni. 10-21) And further, he quotes the Ṛk मित्रो जनान्यातयति ब्रुवाणो मित्रो दाधार पृथिवीमुत द्यां । मित्रः कृष्णीरनिमिषाभि चष्टे मित्राय हव्यं धृतवज्जु होत ॥ (mitro janānyātayati bruvāṇo mitro dādhāra pṛthivīmuta dyāṃ | mitraḥ kṛṣṇīranimiṣābhi caṣṭe mitrāya havyaṃ dhṛtavajju hota ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-59-1) and, by showing Mitra's beneficial guidance, the manner in which he upholds heaven and earth, and his being ever watchful and protecting the people who belong to him, he explains the qualities of a trusted friend found in Mitra. In the present Ṛk also, Mitra's nature is described by the epithets beginning with शेव्यः (śevyaḥ).

शेव्यः (śevyaḥ)—साधुः सुखकर्ता (sādhuḥ sukhakartā): one who gives happiness. शेव (śeva) means happiness. This word is generally used when the happiness that is the fruit of sacrifice is indicated. यज्ञ साहं दुव इषेग्निं पूर्वस्य शेवस्य । अद्रेः सूनुमायुमाहुः ॥ (yajña sāhaṃ duva iṣegniṃ pūrvasya śevasya | adreḥ sūnumāyumāhuḥ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-20-7) Here the word शेव (śeva) is used as a synonym for happiness that is excellent and is the fruit of sacrifice. In the present Ṛk, in describing Mitra's nature, it is said that Mitra produces happiness of such excellence; and Vishnu too is prayed to be such a Mitra.

फृतासुतिं (phṛtāsutiṃ)—it means an āsuti in the form of ghee. Āsuti means food in the form of juice; milk and the like, the Soma juice that is an oblation, or an oblation in the form of ghee, are all indicated by the word āsuti. त्वे अग्ने विश्वे अमृतासो अद्रुह आसा देवा हविरदंत्याहुतिं । त्वया मर्तासः स्वदंत आसुतिं त्वं गर्भो वीरुधां जज्जिषे शुचिः ॥ (tve agne viśve amṛtāso adruha āsā devā haviradaṃtyāhutiṃ | tvayā martāsaḥ svadaṃta āsutiṃ tvaṃ garbho vīrudhāṃ jajjiṣe śuciḥ ‖) ### Printed p. 643 (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-1-14) Here, saying that by Agni's grace men enjoy foods such as milk, in the form of juice, the word āsuti is used as a synonym of milk and the like. In the present Ṛk it means an āsuti in the form of ghee.

विभूतद्युम्नः (vibhūtadyumnaḥ)—प्रभूतयशाः प्रभूतान्नो वा (prabhūtayaśāḥ prabhūtānno vā): one of abundant fame, or one of abundant food. The Nirukta-writers have included the word द्युम्न (dyumna) among the names of wealth (Ni. 3-9). Moreover, when giving a derivation of this word again, द्युम्नं द्योततेर‍्यशो वा अन्नं वा (dyumnaṃ dyotateryaśo vā annaṃ vā) (Ni. 5-5), they show that, formed from the root द्युत् (dyut) meaning "to shine", it means either fame or food. Quoting the Ṛk शतं ते शिप्रिन्नू तयः सुदासे सहस्रं शंसा उत रातिरस्तु । जहि वधर्वनुषो मर्त्यस्यास्मे द्युम्नमधि रत्नं च धेहि ॥ (śataṃ te śiprinnū tayaḥ sudāse sahasraṃ śaṃsā uta rātirastu | jahi vadharvanuṣo martyasyāsme dyumnamadhi ratnaṃ ca dhehi ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-25-3) they show that, when the prayer is made "give us द्युम्न (dyumna) and treasure", wealth is indicated by the word रत्न (ratna), and so द्युम्न (dyumna) means fame or food. (Ni. 5-5) Likewise in the present Ṛk it means one of abundant fame or of abundant food.

एवयाः (evayāḥ)—this word is generally an epithet of the Maruts. In many places, as in एवैः सखिभिः (evaiḥ sakhibhiḥ)—गमनशीलैर्मित्रभूतैर्मरुद्भिः (gamanaśīlairmitrabhūtairmarudbhiḥ), it indicates the Maruts' nature of moving about and their being always together. Although the root has the sense of moving, in the present Ṛk the sense is "one who unites, who joins", that is, one who provides protection.

सप्रथाः (saprathāḥ)—सर्वतः पृथुः (sarvataḥ pṛthuḥ): spread widely all around. The Nirukta-writers explained the basic meaning of this word thus (Ni. 6-8), त्वमग्ने सप्रथा असि जुष्टो होता वरेण्यः । त्वया यज्ञं वि तन्वते ॥ (tvamagne saprathā asi juṣṭo hotā vareṇyaḥ | tvayā yajñaṃ vi tanvate ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-13-4) and quoting this Ṛk they showed the fitting meaning of the word there as stated above. In the present Ṛk, however, that meaning is somewhat extended: the commentator explains the purport as "be large-bodied all around us".

p. 644

अध्यः (adhyaḥ)—पुनः पुनः प्रवर्धनार्हः । एकवारकरणे न संपूर्णत इत्यर्थः ! (punaḥ punaḥ pravardhanārhaḥ | ekavārakaraṇe na saṃpūrṇata ityarthaḥ !) The stoma-hymn that praises you is to be recited again and again, to sing your qualities; it is not to be finished by reciting once. This is the meaning. राध्यः (rādhyaḥ)—समाराधनीयः (samārādhanīyaḥ): one to be performed with splendour.

Grammar
  • भव—भू सत्तायां धातुः । लोट् मध्यमपुरुषएकवचनांतरूपम् । द्वचोतस्तिज- (पा. सू. ६-३-१३५) इति संहितायां दीर्घो भवति । पादादित्वान्निघातस्वरो न भवति । शप् पित्त्वाद्धातुस्वरो अवशिष्यते ।
  • मित्रः—इमिदा स्नेहने धातुः । अमिजिमि- (उ. सू. ४.६०-३) इति क्र प्रत्ययः । कित्त्वाल्लघूपधगुणो न भवति । प्रत्ययस्वरेणांतोदात्तो भवति । NOTE
  • शेव्यः—शेवे साधुः शेव्यः । साध्वर्थे यत् प्रत्ययः । यतोनावः (पा. सू. ६-१-२१३) इत्याद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति ।
  • धृतासुतिः—धृतं आसुतिः येन सः धृतासुतिः । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति । विभूतद्युम्नः इत्यत्रापि बहुव्रीहिसमासत्वात् पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरो भवति ।
  • सप्रथाः—प्रथ प्रख्याने धातुः । सर्वधातुभ्यः असुन् इत्यसुन् प्रत्ययः । प्रथसा सह वर्तते इति सप्रथाः । तेन सहेति तुल्ययोगे (पा. सू. २-२-२८) इति समासः । वोपसर्जनस्य (पा. सू. ६-२-८२) इति सह इत्यस्य समासे स भावः । NOTE
  • अधा—अथ इत्यत्र छांदसत्वाद्वर्णविकारो जातः । निपातस्यच (पा सू. ६-३-१३६) इति संहितायां दीर्घो भवति ।
  • विदुषा—विद ज्ञाने धातुः । अस्माल्लट् आगते तस्य शत्रादेशः । विदेशिशतुर्वसुः (पा. सू. ७-१-३६) इति शतृवसुरादेशः । तृतीयाविकवचने परे वसोः संप्रसारणम् इति संप्रसारणं पूर्वरूपम् ।
  • अध्यः—ऋधु वृद्धौ धातुः । अस्मादर्हार्थे यत् आगते धातोर्लघूपधस्य गुणः । आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति । एवमेव राध संसिद्धौ धातुः । अस्मादपि यत् आगते आद्युदात्तस्वरो भवति ॥ १ ॥

p. 645

Ṛk 2

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

यः पू॒र्वार्याय॑ वे॒धसे॒ नवी॑यसे सु॒मज्ञा॑नये॒ विष्ण॑वे॒ ॑ ददा॑शति ।
यो जा॒तम॑स्य मह॒तो महि॒ ब्रव॒त्सेदु॒ श्रवो॑भि॒र्युज्यं॑ ॒॑ चिदभ्यसत् ॥ २ ॥

yaḥ pūrvāryāya vedhase navīyase sumajñānaye viṣṇave dadāśati | yo jātamasya mahato mahi bravatsedu śravobhiryujyaṃ cidabhyasat ‖ 2 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

यः । पूर्वार्याय । वेधसे । नवीयसे । सुमत्जानये । विष्णवे । ददाशति ।
यः । जातं । अस्य । महतः । महि । ब्रवत् । सः । इत् । ऊं इति । श्रवःभिः ।
युज्यं । चित् । अभि । आसत् ॥ २ ॥

yaḥ | pūrvāryāya | vedhase | navīyase | sumatjānaye | viṣṇave | dadāśati | yaḥ | jātaṃ | asya | mahataḥ | mahi | bravat | saḥ | it | ūṃ iti | śravaḥbhiḥ | yujyaṃ | cit | abhi | āsat ‖ 2 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

यः यो मर्त्यः पूर्वाय पूर्वकालीनाय । नित्यायेत्यर्थः । वेधसे विविधजगत्कर्त्रे नवीयसे नित्यनूतनाय । अत्यंतरमणीयायेत्यर्थः । स्तुत्याय वा सुमज्ञानये स्वयमेवोत्पन्नाय ॥ जनेर्‌णादिक इण् ॥ सुमत्स्ययमित्यर्थः । नि. ६-२२ । इति यास्कः । यद्वा । सुतरां मादयतीति सुमत् । तादृशी जाया यस्य स तथोक्तः। तस्मै सर्वजगन्मादनशीलश्रीपतय इत्यर्थः ॥ बहुव्रीहौ जायायानिज्॥ पा. ५-४-१३४. ॥ इति निजादेशः समासांतः । वलि लोपः ॥ उक्तगुणकाय विष्णवे व्यापकाय ददाशति हविरादिकं ददाति । किंचास्य विष्णोर्महतो महानुभावस्य महि महत् पूज्यं जातं जन्मोत्पत्तिं हिरण्यगर्भादिरूपं जन्म ब्रवत् ब्रूयात् ॥ ब्रवीतेर्लेट्यडागमः ॥ संकीर्तयेत् । सेदु । उशब्दोऽपिशब्दार्थः । सोऽपि दाता स्तोता च श्रवोभिरन्नॆः कीर्तिभिर्वा युक्तः सन् युज्यं चित् सर्वैर्गंतव्यमेव तत्वदमभ्याभिमुख्येनासत् । गच्छति । प्राप्नोति ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

"He who" (यः (yaḥ)), the mortal, to the one who is पूर्व (pūrva), of former time, that is, eternal; वेधसे (vedhase), the maker of the manifold world; नवीयसे (navīyase), ever new, that is, exceedingly delightful, or else worthy of praise; सुमज्ञानये (sumajñānaye), born of himself (the suffix is Uṇādi इण् (iṇ)), "self-existent" (sumatsyayam), Ni. 6-22, says Yāska. Or else: सुतरां मादयतीति सुमत् (sutarāṃ mādayatīti sumat), one whose wife is of such a kind is so called; thus, to the lord of Śrī, whose nature is to gladden the whole world. In this case the substitute निज् (nij) is a samāsānta by Pā. 5-4-134, and the व (va) is elided. To Vishnu, the all-pervading, who has the stated qualities, "he gives" (ददाशति (dadāśati)) oblations and the like. Moreover, of this great Vishnu, of great majesty, he would proclaim (ब्रवत् (bravat), i.e. would celebrate; the aṭ augment of the Leṭ of ब्रू (brū)) the great, worshipful birth (जातं (jātaṃ)), the birth in the form of Hiraṇyagarbha and the like. सेदु (sedu): the word उ (u) has the sense of "also"; he too, the giver and the praiser, endowed with श्रवः (śravaḥ) (food, or fame), reaches (abhyasat: goes, attains) that place which is to be reached by all (युज्यं चित् (yujyaṃ cit)), facing it directly.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • यः (yaḥ)—which man
  • पूर्व्याय (pūrvyāya)—to the ancient, that is, the eternal
  • वेधसे (vedhase)—to the creator of the world
  • नवीयसे (navīyase)—to the delightful one, because he is new ### Printed p. 646
  • सुमज्ञानये (sumajñānaye)—to him who is self-born, or who is the husband of Lakshmi, who gives joy to the whole world
  • विष्णवे (viṣṇave)—to Vishnu, the all-pervading
  • ददाशति (dadāśati)—offers (oblations and the like)
  • महतः अस्य (mahataḥ asya)—of this great-souled Vishnu
  • महि (mahi)—wonderful and worshipful
  • जातं (jātaṃ)—the birth in the form of Hiraṇyagarbha and the like
  • ब्रवत् (bravat)—praises
  • सेदु (sedu)—he also (who is thus giver and praiser)
  • श्रवोभिः (śravobhiḥ)—endowed with foods or with fames
  • युज्यंचित् (yujyaṃcit)—the presence of that Vishnu, to which (all) must go and unite
  • अभि (abhi)—aiming at
  • असत् (asat)—goes and joins
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The man who offers oblations and the like to Vishnu, the all-pervading, who is eternal, creator of the world, delightful, and self-born, and who praises the wonderful birth of this great-souled Vishnu in the form of Hiraṇyagarbha and the like — he, being both giver and praiser, endowed with fames, goes and joins the presence of that Vishnu, to which all must go.

Printed English

He who presents (offerings) to Vishnu, the ancient, the creator, the recent, the self-born ; he who celebrates the great birth of that mighty one : he verily possessed of abundance, attains (the station) that is to be sought (by all)-

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

सुमज्ञानये (sumajñānaye)—This word is explained in two ways. First, स्वयमेवोत्पन्नाय (svayamevotpannāya): to (Vishnu) who is self-born. Second, सुतरां मादयतीति सुमत् । तादृशी जाया यस्य स तथोक्तः । सर्वजगन्मादनशीलश्रीपतये । (sutarāṃ mādayatīti sumat | tādṛśī jāyā yasya sa tathoktaḥ | sarvajaganmādanaśīlaśrīpataye |) Taking the word सुमत् (sumat) as "bringing delight", the explanation given is: husband of the goddess Lakshmi, who has such a delight-giving quality and gives joy to all the worlds. सुमत्स्ययमित्यर्थः । (sumatsyayamityarthaḥ |) (Ni. 6-22): saying that सुमत् (sumat) means "of oneself, spontaneously", he quotes उप प्रागात्सुमन्मेधायि मन्म देवानामाशा उप वीतपृष्ठः । अन्वेनं विप्रा ऋषयो मदंति देवानां पुष्टे चकृमा सुबंधुं ॥ (upa prāgātsumanmedhāyi manma devānāmāśā upa vītapṛṣṭhaḥ | anvenaṃ viprā ṛṣayo madaṃti devānāṃ puṣṭe cakṛmā subaṃdhuṃ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-16-2) ### Printed p. 647 and, quoting this Ṛk, explains the prayer उपप्रैतु मां स्वयं । (upapraitu māṃ svayaṃ |) "may the object I desire come near me of itself", and so shows the meaning that the word सुमत् (sumat) has. On this basis it can be said that the sense "self-born" is fitting. Moreover, since in this same Ṛk the word जातं (jātaṃ) is explained as जन्म उत्पत्तिं हिरण्यगर्भादिरूपं (janma utpattiṃ hiraṇyagarbhādirūpaṃ), referring to origination in the form of Hiraṇyagarbha and the like, this meaning gains still more support. Or again, since the word सुमत् (sumat) is used in many places as a synonym of कल्याण (kalyāṇa), शोभन (śobhana) or भद्र (bhadra) (auspicious, beautiful), it would not be wrong to give the second meaning. Just as in सुमज्ञानिः (sumajñāniḥ), in places such as सुमद्गणः (sumadgaṇaḥ), सुमदंशु (sumadaṃśu), सुमद्रथः (sumadrathaḥ) the word सुमत् (sumat) has everywhere been given the sense of beautiful or auspicious, as shown with examples in the Special Topics of Ṛk 1-142-7 of this same volume (page 254). (In the Ṛk 1-142-7 the word there means simply "of itself".) However, the epithet श्रीपति (śrīpati) for Vishnu does not seem to occur in the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā. The word श्रीः (śrīḥ) has the meanings wealth and splendour, but not the conventional name Lakshmi. Therefore the first meaning is the more fitting.

जातं (jātaṃ)—हिरण्यगर्भादिरूपं जन्म । (hiraṇyagarbhādirūpaṃ janma |) It is described in the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā itself that, desiring the creation of the world, the divine principle first came into being of itself in forms such as Hiraṇyagarbha and afterwards created the world. हिरण्यगर्भः समवर्तताग्रे भूतस्य जातः पतिरेक आसीत् । स दाधार पृथिवीं द्यामुतेमां कस्मै देवाय हविषा विधेम ॥ (hiraṇyagarbhaḥ samavartatāgre bhūtasya jātaḥ patireka āsīt | sa dādhāra pṛthivīṃ dyāmutemāṃ kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-121-1) In Ṛks of this kind it is said हिरण्यगर्भः जातमात्र एव जगतः ईश्वरः आसीत् (hiraṇyagarbhaḥ jātamātra eva jagataḥ īśvaraḥ āsīt); the same point is stated here too, praising Vishnu's beginningless nature and greatness.

वेधसे (vedhase)—विविधजगत्कर्त्रॆ । (vividhajagatkartrè |) It means: who created the world in its many forms. The word वेधस् (vedhas) is read in the Nirukta among the names of the wise (Ni. 3-19). It is generally an epithet of the wise sacrificer. In some places, even where the sense "producer" occurs, it can only mean producer of the fruit of sacrifice; its use for a creator of the world does not seem to occur. But in the present Ṛk, since words such as सुमज्ञानये (sumajñānaye) and जातं (jātaṃ) describe the nature of the world-creator, this word may fit the meaning Sāyaṇa gives, in keeping with the context.

पूर्व्याय नवीयसे (pūrvyāya navīyase)—these epithets speak at one and the same time of Vishnu's beginninglessness, his perpetual newness, and therefore his endlessness. For the word नवीयसे (navīyase) Sāyaṇa

p. 648

Sāyaṇa explains the word navīyase as नित्यनूतनाय अत्यंतरमणीयाय (nityanūtanāya atyaṃtaramaṇīyāya), that is, "supremely delightful because he is ever new".

The description of Viṣṇu in the same order of words is given in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa as well (3-4-3-9) NOTE. There Sāyaṇa explains the word पूर्वार्यय (pūrvāryaya) NOTE as जगतः पूर्वमेव भवाय (jagataḥ pūrvameva bhavāya), "who existed even before the creation of the world". He explains navīyase as रामकृष्णाद्यवतारैरत्यंतं नूतनाय (rāmakṛṣṇādyavatārairatyaṃtaṃ nūtanāya), "who is ever new through his forms of incarnation, Rāma, Kṛṣṇa and the rest".

śravobhir yujyaṃ cid abhyasat: Sāyaṇa explains this part in one way in the Ṛksaṃhitā and in another in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa (2-4-3-9). In the Saṃhitā: श्रवोभिः— अन्नैः कीर्तिभिर्वा युक्तःसन् (śravobhiḥ— annaiḥ kīrtibhirvā yuktaḥsan), युज्यं चित्— सर्वैर्गंतव्यमेव तत्पदं (yujyaṃ cit— sarvairgaṃtavyameva tatpadaṃ), अभ्यसत्— अभिमुख्येन गच्छति प्राप्नोति (abhyasat— abhimukhyena gacchati prāpnoti). That is, endowed with foods or with fame, he goes towards and reaches the supreme state that must be reached by all. In the Brāhmaṇa: श्रवोभिः—श्रवणीयैर्हविर्दानमंत्र्यैः स्तोत्रविशेषैश्च युज्यंचित् सर्वदा स्वेन युक्तमपि कामक्रोधलोभरूपं शत्रुं अभ्यसत्—अभितः निरस्यति ॥ (śravobhiḥ—śravaṇīyairhavirdānamaṃtryaiḥ stotraviśeṣaiśca yujyaṃcit sarvadā svena yuktamapi kāmakrodhalobharūpaṃ śatruṃ abhyasat—abhitaḥ nirasyati ‖). That is, with the mantras recited audibly while offering oblations and with special hymns, he drives far away the enemy in the form of desire, anger and greed, which clings to oneself.

Further, quoting the verse त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं (trividhaṃ narakasyedaṃ) (भंगी (bhaṃgī)), he explains that the three kinds of enemies described there are nirasyati, driven out; this is the purport he gives for the mantra in the Brāhmaṇa.

Since the word śravas has the meanings food, strength, hymn and so on, either meaning may be given. But it is noted that the particle cit is used in other senses too. In the interpretation of the Saṃhitā, युज्यंचित् (yujyaṃcit) stresses the sense of excellence, सर्वैर्गंतव्यमेव (sarvairgaṃtavyameva), "that which all must attain". In the Brāhmaṇa sentence स्वेन युक्तमति (svena yuktamati) it gives the sense of something to be rejected, "even though clinging to oneself".

Since there is a Nirukta statement चिदित्येषोऽनेककर्मा (cidityeṣo 'nekakarmā) (1-4), this particle can be interpreted according to context. For example, in the sentence आचारश्चिदिदं ब्रूयात् (ācāraścididaṃ brūyāt) ("the teacher himself should say this; others cannot") the particle is used in the sense of honour (पूजायां (pūjāyāṃ)); in दधिचिदित्युपमार्थे (dadhicidityupamārthe) ("like curds") as a word of comparison; and in कुल्माषाश्चिदाहर (kulmāṣāścidāhara) ("bring even sour gruel") a sense of contempt is possible. This is explained in the Nirukta

p. 649

. In the present mantra Sāyaṇa gives this particle the sense of honour in the Saṃhitā and the sense of contempt in the Brāhmaṇa.

अभ्यसत्—आभिमुख्येन गच्छति (abhyasat—ābhimukhyena gacchati): in the Saṃhitā he explains that he goes towards the supreme state; in the Brāhmaṇa he explains that the preposition abhi joins the root as, which gives the sense "throw", and so means "he destroys".

Grammar
  • वेधसे — वि उपसर्गः । डुधाञ् धारणपोषणयोः धातुः । विधाञ्नो वेधच (उ. सू. ४-६६४) इति असि प्रत्ययः । उपसर्गविशिष्टधातोः वेधादेशः । प्रत्ययस्य आद्युदात्तस्वरः भवति । चतुर्थीएकवचनांतरूपम् ।
  • नवीयसे — अतिशयेन नवः नवीयान् । अतिशयार्थे ईयसुन् प्रत्ययः । इत्यादिर्नित्यम् इति आद्युदात्तस्वरः भवति ।
  • सुमज्ञानये — सुमत् स्वयं जानिः उत्पत्तिः यस्य । सुमत्‌स्वयमित्यर्थः (निरु. ६-२२) इति यास्केन उक्तम् । जनी प्रादुर्भावे धातुः । अस्मात् औणादिकः इण् प्रत्ययः । अतउपधायाः (पा. सू. ७-२-११६) इति उपधावृद्धिः । सुमज्ञानि इति रूपं भवति । अथवा सुतरां मादयति इति सुमत् । सु उपपदे सति अंतर्भावितण्यर्थकात् मद धातोः क्विप् प्रत्ययः । सुमत् जाया यस्य सः सुमज्ञानिः । जायाया निज् (पा.सू. ५-४-१३४) इति समासांतत्वेन निजादेशः भवति । लोपोव्योर्वलि इति यकारलोपः । बहुव्रिह प्रकृत्या पूर्वपदम् (पा सू. ६-२-२) इति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः भवति ।
  • ददाशति — दाश्य दाने धातुः । भ्यादिः । लट् प्रथमपुरुषएकवचने परे बहुलं छंदसि इति शपि श्लु आदेशः । श्लु इति धातोः द्वित्वम् । यद्योगात् निघातस्वरः न भवति । अभ्यस्तासामादिः (पा सू. ६-१-१८९) इति आद्युदात्तस्वरः भवति ।
  • महतः — बृहन्महतोरुपसंख्यानम् इति वचनेन षष्ठीविभक्तेः उदात्तस्वरः भवति ।
  • महि — मह पूजायां धातुः । सर्वधातुभ्य इन् इति इन् प्रत्ययः । नित्त्वात् आद्युदात्तस्वरः भवति ।
  • ब्रवत् — ब्रूञ् व्यक्तायां वाचि धातुः । लेट् प्रथमपुरुषएकवचने तिप् प्रत्ययः । इतश्चलोपः परस्मैपदेषु (पा. सू. ३-४-९७) इति इकारलोपः । लेटोऽडाटा (पा सू. ३-४-९४) इति तस्य अडागमः । अदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शपः (पा. सू. २-४-७२) इति शपो लुक् । प्रत्ययनिमित्तेन धातोः इको गुणः अवादेशः । यच्छब्दसंबंधात् निघातस्वरः न भवति । तिप् पित्त्वात् आगमस्यापि अनुदात्तत्वात् धातुस्वरः अवशिष्यते ।

p. 650

  • श्रवोभिः — श्रु श्रवणे धातुः । अस्मात् औणादिकः असुन् प्रत्ययः । नित्त्वात् आद्युदात्तस्वरः भवति । तृतीयाविकवचनांतरूपम् ।
  • युज्यम् — युजिर् योगे धातुः । अस्मात् यत् प्रत्ययः । यतोनावः (पा. सू. ६-१-२१३) इति आद्युदात्तस्वरः भवति ।
  • असत् — अस भुवि धातुः । लज् प्रथमपुरुषएकवचने तिप् । इतश्च इति इकारलोपः । बहुलं छंदसि इति शपो लुक् न भवति । तिजंतनिघातस्वरः भवति ।

Ṛk 3

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

तमु॑ स्तोतारः पू॒र्व्यं यथा॑ वि॒द ऋ॒तस्य॒ गर्भं॑ ज॒नुषा॑
पिपर्तन ।
आस्य॑ जा॒नंतो॒ नाम॑ चिद्विवक्तन म॒हस्ते॑ विष्णो सुम॒तिं ॑ भजामहे ॥ ३ ॥

tamu stotāraḥ pūrvyaṃ yathā vida ṛtasya garbhaṃ januṣā pipartana | āsya jānaṃto nāma cidvivaktana mahaste viṣṇo sumatiṃ bhajāmahe ‖ 3 ‖

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

तं । ऊं इति । स्तोतारः । पूर्व्यं । यथा । विद । ऋतस्य । गर्भं । जनुषा ।
पि प र्तन ।
आ । अस्य । जानंतः । नाम । चित् । विवक्तन । महः । ते । विष्णो इति । सुमतिं ।
भजामहे ॥ ३ ॥

taṃ | ūṃ iti | stotāraḥ | pūrvyaṃ | yathā | vida | ṛtasya | garbhaṃ | januṣā | pi pa rtana | ā | asya | jānaṃtaḥ | nāma | cit | vivaktana | mahaḥ | te | viṣṇo iti | sumatiṃ | bhajāmahe ‖ 3 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

हे स्तोतारः तमु तमेव विष्णुं पूर्व्यं पूर्वाह्नमनादिसंसिद्धमृतस्य गर्भं यज्ञस्य गर्भभूतं । यज्ञात्मनोत्पन्नमित्यर्थः । यज्ञो वै विष्णुः । शत.

Gist of the bhāṣya

"O hymners, that very Viṣṇu, पूर्व्यं (pūrvyaṃ), ancient, beginninglessly established, the germ (गर्भं (garbhaṃ)) of ऋतस्य (ṛtasya), of the sacrifice: he is the embryo of sacrifice, that is, born in the form of sacrifice." The basis is the śruti यज्ञो वै विष्णुः (yajño vai viṣṇuḥ), "sacrifice is indeed Viṣṇu", Śa.

p. 651

१-१-२-१३ । इति श्रुतेः । यद्वा । ऋतस्योदकस्य गर्भं गर्भकारणं । उवकोत्पादकमित्यर्थः ॥ अप एव ससर्जादौ । मनु १-८ । इति स्मृतेः । एवंभूतं विष्णुं यथा विद जानीथ तथा जनुषा जन्मना स्वत एव न केनचिद्वरलाभादिना पिपर्तन । स्तोत्रादिना प्रीणयत । यावदस्य माहात्म्यं जानीथ तावदित्यर्थः॥ विदेर्लटि मध्यमबहुवचनं। विद ऋतस्येत्यत्र संहितायामृत्यक इति प्रकृतिभावः ॥ किंचास्य महानुभावस्य विष्णोर्नाम चित् सर्वैर्नमनीयमभिधानं सार्वात्मप्रतिपाद- कं विष्णुरित्येतन्नाम जानंतः पुरुषार्थप्रदमित्यधिगच्छंत आ समंताद्वक्तन । वदत । संकीर्तयत । यद्वा । नानु यज्ञात्मना नमनं विष्णोरेव सर्वेषां स्वर्गापवर्गसाधनायेष्टाद्यात्मना द्रव्यदेवतात्मना वा परिणाममा जानंतो यूयं विव क्तन । ब्रूत । स्तुत ॥ वचेर्लोटि छांदसः शप श्लुः । बहुलं छंदसीत्यभ्यासस्यॆत्वं । पूर्ववत्तनादेशः ॥ इदानीं साक्षात्कृत्याह । हे विष्णो सर्वात्मक देव महो महतस्ते तव सुमतिं सुष्टुतिं शोभात्मिकां बुद्धिं वा भजामहे । सेवामदे वयं यजमानाः ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

The reference is 1-1-2-13. Or else: ऋतस्य (ṛtasya) means "of water", and गर्भं (garbhaṃ) means "the cause of the germ", that is, the producer of water, on the authority of the smṛti अप एव ससर्जादौ (apa eva sasarjādau) (Manu 1-8). Know such a Viṣṇu and propitiate him (पिपर्तन (pipartana)) with hymns and the like, of your own accord (जनुषा (januṣā), by birth, spontaneously), not through any boon or the like; propitiate him as far as you know his greatness. विद (vida) is the second person plural of the present of the root vid; in विद ऋतस्य (vida ṛtasya) the Saṃhitā has the natural form (prakṛtibhāva).

Further, knowing the name of this greatly glorious Viṣṇu, नाम चित् (nāma cit), the designation to be bowed to by all, which expresses him as the self of all, namely the name "Viṣṇu", as bestowing the goals of man, proclaim (विवक्तन (vivaktana)) it on every side; speak, extol. Or else: knowing the bowing (नाम (nāma)) as the very transformation of Viṣṇu alone, in the form of sacrifice, iṣṭi and the rest, or in the form of substance and deity, for the attainment of heaven and release for all, you declare, praise. The form विवक्तन (vivaktana) is Vedic (the śap replaced by śluḥ, the reduplicative vowel becomes e, the ending tana). Now addressing him directly: O Viṣṇu, god who are the self of all, we sacrificers serve your great सुमतिं (sumatiṃ), good praise, or your beautiful understanding.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • स्तोतारः (stotāraḥ)—O hymners
  • पूर्व्यं (pūrvyaṃ)—the beginninglessly established one
  • ऋतस्य गर्भं (ṛtasya garbhaṃ)—born as the embryo of sacrifice, in the form of sacrifice; or the producer of water
  • तमु (tamu)—that very Viṣṇu
  • यथा विद (yathā vida)—in whatever way you know
  • जनुषा (januṣā)—without any expectation of reward, of your own accord
  • पिपर्तन (pipartana)—propitiate with hymns and the like
  • अस्य (asya)—of this greatly glorious Viṣṇu
  • नाम चित् (nāma cit)—the name "Viṣṇu", to be meditated upon by all
  • जानंतः (jānaṃtaḥ)—knowing it (as bestowing the goals of man), or knowing (that, since he is of the nature of sacrifice, everything is offered to him)
  • आ विवक्तन (ā vivaktana)—proclaim (his name)
  • विष्णो (viṣṇo)—O Viṣṇu
  • महः (mahaḥ)—great-souled
  • ते (te)—your
  • सुमतिं (sumatiṃ)—auspicious understanding
  • भजामहे (bhajāmahe)—we serve; or may we obtain your grace and be happy
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O hymners, that Viṣṇu, beginninglessly established, born as the embryo of sacrifice in the form of sacrifice: in whatever way you know him, propitiate him with hymns, without expecting any reward. Knowing the great name of this greatly glorious Viṣṇu, to be meditated upon by all, as bestowing the goals of man, proclaim his glory. O Viṣṇu, great-souled, may we too enjoy your favour.

p. 652

Printed English

Hymners, propitiate of your own accord that ancient Vishnu, since you know him as the germ of sacrifice ; cognizant of his greatness, celebrate his name : may we, Vishnu, enjoy your favour.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The qualities of Viṣṇu described in this Ṛk are described in the same order in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa (Tai. Brā. 2-4-3-9). But where this Ṛk has जनुषा पिपर्तन (januṣā pipartana) the Brāhmaṇa has हविषा पिपर्तन (haviṣā pipartana), and where this Ṛk has महस्ते विष्णो (mahaste viṣṇo) the Brāhmaṇa has बृहत्ते विष्णो (bṛhatte viṣṇo); a slight change.

ऋतस्य गर्भं (ṛtasya garbhaṃ): he gives two explanations. First, यज्ञस्य गर्भभूतं । यज्ञात्मनोत्पन्नमित्यर्थः । यज्ञो वै विष्णुरिति श्रुतेः (yajñasya garbhabhūtaṃ | yajñātmanotpannamityarthaḥ | yajño vai viṣṇuriti śruteḥ). Since the śruti says that sacrifice is Viṣṇu, one meaning is that he is the embryo of the ṛta that is of the form of sacrifice. Second, ऋतस्य उदकस्य गर्भं गर्भकारणं । उदकोत्पादकमित्यर्थः । अप एव ससर्जादाविति स्मृतेः (ṛtasya udakasya garbhaṃ garbhakāraṇaṃ | udakotpādakamityarthaḥ | apa eva sasarjādāviti smṛteḥ). Since the word ṛta also means water, he gives another meaning, that Viṣṇu is the cause of the germ of water. Because the word ṛta has both meanings, and because both views are supported by śruti statements, either meaning fits.

In the sentences तद्विष्णुः प्रथमः प्राप । स देवानाग्ं श्रेष्ठोभवत्तस्मादाहुर्विष्णुर्देवानाग्‌ं श्रेष्ठ इति । स यः स विष्णुर्यज्ञः स । स यः स यज्ञोसौ स आदित्यः । (tadviṣṇuḥ prathamaḥ prāpa | sa devānāgṃ śreṣṭhobhavattasmādāhurviṣṇurdevānāgṃ śreṣṭha iti | sa yaḥ sa viṣṇuryajñaḥ sa | sa yaḥ sa yajñosau sa ādityaḥ |) (Pa. Prā. 14-1-1-4 to 5) NOTE, यज्ञो विष्णुः प्रजापतिः (yajño viṣṇuḥ prajāpatiḥ) (Mai. Tri. 6-16) NOTE, and त्वं यज्ञस्तं विष्णुस्तं वषट्कारः (tvaṃ yajñastaṃ viṣṇustaṃ vaṣaṭkāraḥ) (Tai. U. 4-25-6) NOTE, and similar sentences, the identity of sacrifice and Viṣṇu is stated: sacrifice is Viṣṇu. By this the first meaning is supported. And in

आपो ह वा इदमग्रे सलिलमेवास ता अकामयंत कथं नु प्रजायेमहीति ता आश्राम्यंस्तास्तपोऽतप्यंत तासु तपस्तप्यमानासु हिरण्मयमांडग्ं संबभूवाजातो ह तर्हि संवत्सर आस तदिदग्ं हिरण्मयमांडं यावत्संवत्सरस्य वेला तावत्पर्यप्लवत । ततः संवत्सरे पुरुषः समभवत् । (āpo ha vā idamagre salilamevāsa tā akāmayaṃta kathaṃ nu prajāyemahīti tā āśrāmyaṃstāstapo 'tapyaṃta tāsu tapastapyamānāsu hiraṇmayamāṃḍagṃ saṃbabhūvājāto ha tarhi saṃvatsara āsa tadidagṃ hiraṇmayamāṃḍaṃ yāvatsaṃvatsarasya velā tāvatparyaplavata | tataḥ saṃvatsare puruṣaḥ samabhavat |) (Ta. Brā. 11-1-6-1) NOTE

p. 653

and similar sentences it is said that water was the beginning of creation and that Viṣṇu in the form of the golden germ was its support. By this the second meaning is supported.

पिपर्तन (pipartana): पिपर्ति पपुरिरिति प्रिणातिनिगमौ वा प्रीणाति निगमौ वा (piparti papuririti priṇātinigamau vā prīṇāti nigamau vā). It has been stated earlier (Ni. 5-24) that this is formed either from the root pṛ, which gives the sense "fill", or from the root prī, which gives the sense "propitiate". In the present Ṛk the meaning is "propitiate Viṣṇu with hymns and the like".

जनुषा (januṣā): this word means जन्ममात्रेण (janmamātreṇa), "from birth itself". Expanded, this meaning comes to "naturally" or "spontaneously". In the present Ṛk, जन्मना स्वत एव न केनचिद्वरलाभादिना (janmanā svata eva na kenacidvaralābhādinā): without expectation of any reward of any kind, with natural and pure praises, "propitiate": a prayer in the form of an injunction.

नाम चित् (nāma cit): सर्वैर्नमनीयमभिधानं सार्वात्मप्रतिपादकं विष्णुरित्येतन्नाम (sarvairnamanīyamabhidhānaṃ sārvātmapratipādakaṃ viṣṇurityetannāma): the name "Viṣṇu", to be bowed to by all, which is all-pervading and has the power of making the whole universe inwardly contained; this is one way of taking it. And the other: यद्वा नाम यज्ञात्मना नमनं विष्णोरेव सर्वेषां स्वर्गापवर्गसाधनायेष्ट्याद्यात्मना द्रव्यदेवतात्मना ना परिणाममा जानंतो वा (yadvā nāma yajñātmanā namanaṃ viṣṇoreva sarveṣāṃ svargāpavargasādhanāyeṣṭyādyātmanā dravyadevatātmanā nā pariṇāmamā jānaṃto vā) NOTE. Since Viṣṇu is himself of the form of sacrifice, the iṣṭis and the like, which are the means to heaven and to release, the substances that are their parts, and the deities addressed in the sacrifice, all are only other forms of Viṣṇu. Knowing that all of them are parts of Viṣṇu, worship and propitiate Viṣṇu through them: this is the other way of explaining it.

Grammar
  • स्तोतारः — ष्टुञ् स्तुतौ धातुः । कर्तरि तृच् प्रत्ययः । संबोधनाबहुवचने गुणे प्राप्ते अप्‌तृन्‌तृच् इति उपधादीर्घः । आमंत्रितस्य च इति निघातस्वरः भवति ।
  • विद — विद ज्ञाने धातुः । अदादिः । लटः मध्यमपुरुषबहुवचने थ प्रत्ययः । विदोलटो वा (पा सू. ३-४-८३) इति तस्य अ आदेशः । सार्वधातुकमपित् इति जीत्वात् लघूपधगुणः न भवति । यथा इति पूर्वं स्थितत्वात्

p. 654

निघातस्वरः न भवति । प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तः भवति । विद+ऋतस्य इति स्थिते संहितायां ऋत्यकः इति प्रकृतिभावः भवति । - जनुषा — जनी प्रादुर्भावे धातुः । जनेरुसिः इति उस् प्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्वरेण उकारः उदात्तः भवति । तृतीया एकवचनांतरूपम् । - पिपर्तन — पृ पालनपूरणयोः पृ इत्येके धातुः । जुहोत्यादिः । लोट् मध्यमपुरुषबहुवचने तप्तनप्तनथनाश्च (पा सू. ७-१-४५) इति तस्य तनपादेशः । श्लौ इति धातोः द्वित्वम् । अर्तिपिपर्त्योश्च (पा. सू. ७-४-२७) इति अभ्यासस्य इत्वम् । प्रत्ययस्य पित्त्वात् जित्वाभावे धातोः इको गुणः । अतिजंतस्य परत्वात् निघातस्वरः भवति । - जानंतः — ज्ञा अवबोधने धातुः । अस्मात् आगतस्य लटः शत्रादेशः । श्नाविकरणे ज्ञाजनोर्जा (पा. सू. ७-३-७९) इति धातोः जादेशः । श्नाभ्यस्तयोरातः (पा. सू. ६-४-११२) इति विकरणस्य आकारस्य लोपः । प्रथमाबहुवचनांतरूपम् । प्रत्ययस्य आद्युदात्तस्वरः भवति । - विवक्तन — वच परिभाषणे धातुः । लोट् मध्यमपुरुषबहुवचने पूर्ववत् तनबादेशः । बहुलं छंदसि इति विकरणस्य श्लु आदेशः । श्लु इति धातोः द्वित्वे प्राप्ते बहुलं छंदसि इति अभ्यासस्य इत्वम् । चोःकुः इति धातुचकारस्य कुत्वम् । तिजंतनिघातस्वरः भवति । - सुमतिम् — मन ज्ञाने धातुः । क्तिन् प्रत्ययः । मंत्रेवृषेषपच (पा. सू. ३-३-९६) इति क्तिन् उदात्तः भवति । प्रादिसमासे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरः भवति । - भजामहे — भज सेवायां धातुः । लट् उत्तमपुरुषबहुवचनांतरूपम् । तिजंतनिघातस्वरः भवति ।

Ṛk 4

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

तम॑स्य॒ राजा॒ वरु॑ण॒स्तम॒श्विना॒ क्रतुं॑ सचंत॒ मारु॑तस्य वे॒धसः॑ ।
दा॒धार॒ दक्ष॑मुत्त॒मम॑ह॒र्विदं॑ व्र॒जं च॒ विष्णुः॒ सखि॑वा ॒ अपूर्णुते ॥ ४ ॥

tamasya rājā varuṇastamaśvinā kratuṃ sacaṃta mārutasya vedhasaḥ | dādhāra dakṣamuttamamaharvidaṃ vrajaṃ ca viṣṇuḥ sakhivā apūrṇute ‖ 4 ‖

p. 655

॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

तं । अस्य । राजा । वरुणः । तं । अश्विना । क्रतुं । सचंत । मारुतस्य । वेधसः ।
दाधार । दक्षं । उत्त् तमं । अहःविदं । व्रजं । च । विष्णुः । सखिवान् । अपऊर्णुते ॥ ४ ॥

taṃ | asya | rājā | varuṇaḥ | taṃ | aśvinā | kratuṃ | sacaṃta | mārutasya | vedhasaḥ | dādhāra | dakṣaṃ | utt tamaṃ | ahaḥvidaṃ | vrajaṃ | ca | viṣṇuḥ | sakhivān | apaūrṇute ‖ 4 ‖

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

अग्नीषोमप्रणयने तमस्य राजेत्येषा प्रयोक्तव्या । अग्नीषोम् प्रणेष्यत्स्विति खंडे सूत्रितं । तमस्य राजा वरुणस्तमश्विनेत्यर्धर्च आरमेत् । आ. ४-१० । इति ॥ मारुतस्य मरुतामृत्विजां संघातो मारुतं। तद्वतः ॥ मत्वर्थो लुप्यते ॥ मरुतां देवानां संबंधिनो वा वेधसो मेधाविनोऽस्य यजमानस्य तं प्रसिद्धं क्रतुं यागं यज्ञात्मकं विष्णुं । यज्योवै विष्णुरिति श्रुतेः । राजा राजमानो वरुणः सचंत । सेवते । तमेव क्रतुं यागमश्विनाश्विनौ सचेते । अन्येऽपि देवाः सचंते। सेवंते । किंच विष्णुः सवनत्रयात्मना व्याप्तो विष्णुः सखिवान् यजमानादिसखिभिर्युक्तः सन्नुत्तममुत्कृष्टतममहर्विदमहर्वेत्तारं। स्वर्गोत्पादकमित्यर्थः। दक्षं बलं फलप्रदानसामर्थ्यरूपं दाधार । धृतवान् । किंच व्रजं च मेघं च । व्रज इति मेघनाम व्रजश्चरुरिति तन्नामसु पातात् । तं वृष्टुवदकार्यापोर्णुते । अपगतावरणं करोति । आहुतिद्वारा यज्ञस्यॆव वृष्टुत्पादकत्वात् । यद्वा । मारुतस्य मरुत्संघातस्य देवगणस्य वेधसो विधातुः स्रष्टुर्विष्णोः क्रतुं कर्म पालनादिरूपं वरुणादयः सचंते । तदधीनत्वात्पालनस्य । स च सखिवानिंद्रमरुदादि सहायोपेतः सन्नुक्तलक्षणं दक्षं वृष्टुत्पादनादिसामर्थ्यरूपं बलं दाधार । तथा व्रजं चापोर्णुते ॥

Gist of the bhāṣya

This Ṛk is to be employed at the Agnīṣoma-praṇayana. The sūtra is: in the section beginning "when they are about to lead forth Agni and Soma", तमस्य राजा वरुणस्तमश्विनेत्यर्धर्च आरमेत् (tamasya rājā varuṇastamaśvinetyardharca āramet) (Ā. 4-10).

मारुतस्य (mārutasya) means belonging to the Maruts, the company of priests (ṛtvij), the suffix of possession being dropped. Or it means belonging to the Maruts, the gods. वेधसः (vedhasaḥ) means "of the wise". The words thus describe this sacrificer. Varuṇa, shining as king, attends that well-known क्रतुं (kratuṃ), the sacrifice, which is Viṣṇu in the form of sacrifice, since the Śruti says yajño vai viṣṇuḥ. The two Aśvins attend that same sacrifice, and other gods attend it too.

Further, Viṣṇu, pervading the three pressings, accompanied by friends such as the sacrificer, bears the दक्षं (dakṣaṃ) that is highest, the best, and "day-finding", that is, the producer of heaven. This power is the strength of bestowing the fruit. He also uncovers the cloud: व्रज (vraja) is a name of the cloud, as it is among the cloud-names listed in the Nighaṇṭu. He removes its covering so that rain falls, because through the oblation the sacrifice itself produces rain.

Or else: Varuṇa and the others attend the work (क्रतुं (kratuṃ)), consisting of protection and the like, of Viṣṇu, the creator of the divine host of Maruts, since protection depends on him. Accompanied by helpers such as Indra and the Maruts, he bears the power described, the strength for producing rain and so on, and uncovers the cloud.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
  • मारुतस्य (mārutasya)—of him who is joined with the company of priests
  • वेधसः (vedhasaḥ)—and who is wise
  • अस्य (asya)—of the sacrificer
  • तं (taṃ)—that well-known
  • क्रतुं (kratuṃ)—sacrifice, or Viṣṇu who is the sacrifice in essence
  • राजा (rājā)—shining
  • वरुणः (varuṇaḥ)—Varuṇa
  • सचंत (sacaṃta)—attends
  • तं (taṃ)—that same, or that same Viṣṇu
  • अश्विना (aśvinā)—the Aśvin deities also (attend)
  • विष्णुः (viṣṇuḥ)—Viṣṇu, who dwells also in the form of the three pressings
  • सखिवान् (sakhivān)—joined with friends such as the sacrificer, or with his friend Indra
  • उत्तमं (uttamaṃ)—the excellent
  • अहर्विदं (aharvidaṃ)—the heaven-producing
  • दक्षं (dakṣaṃ)—power

p. 656

  • दाधार (dādhāra)—has obtained
  • व्रजं च (vrajaṃ ca)—the cloud also
  • अपोर्णुते (aporṇute)—makes (for the sake of rain) to be without covering
भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The shining Varuṇa attends the well-known sacrifice of the sacrificer, who is joined with the company of priests and is wise. The Aśvin deities too attend that same sacrifice. Viṣṇu, who pervades also the form of the three pressings, together with friends such as the sacrificer, has obtained the excellent, heaven-producing power, and he makes the cloud also to be without covering for the sake of rain.

Printed English

The royal Varuna associates (himself) with the sacrifice of the pious worshipper, assisted by the company of the priests: the Aswins (unite with it): Vishnu, with his friend (Indra), possesses supreme heaven-conferring power, and sits upon the clouds.

विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

That this Ṛk beginning तमस्य राजा (tamasya rājā) is to be recited in the Agniṣṭoma-praṇayana rite is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, in the section "when they are about to lead forth Agni and Soma": तमस्य राजा वरुणस्तमश्विनेत्यर्धर्च आरमेत् (tamasya rājā varuṇastamaśvinetyardharca āramet) (Ā. 4-10).

This Ṛk states the relation of Viṣṇu, who is the sacrifice in essence, to Varuṇa, and of Viṣṇu to the Aśvin deities, and praises the power in Viṣṇu of producing heaven and the like.

राजा वरुणः सचंत (rājā varuṇaḥ sacaṃta)—"the shining Varuṇa attends": this states Varuṇa's place in the sacrificial action. Varuṇa has an important place in the optional animal sacrifice. The Saṃhitās and Brāhmaṇas say in many places that on those occasions Varuṇa not only assists Viṣṇu but also completes the sacrifice and himself takes a share in the sacrificial offering. For example:

देवाश्च वै यमश्चास्मिन्‌लोकेऽस्पर्धंत स यमो देवान् - मिंद्रियं वीर्यमयुवत तद्यमस्य यमत्वं ते देवा अमन्यंत यमो वा इदमभूद्यद्वयग्स्मै इति ते प्रजापतिमुपाधावन्त्स एत् प्रजापतिरात्मन उक्षवशौ निरमिमीत ते देवा वैष्णावरुणीं वशामालभंतैंद्र मुक्षाणं तं वरुणेनैव ग्राहयित्वा विष्णुना यज्ञेन प्राणुदंतैंद्रेणैवास्येंद्रियमवृंजत यो भ्रातृव्यवान्तात्स स्पर्धमानो वैष्णावरुणीं ॥ (devāśca vai yamaścāsminloke 'spardhaṃta sa yamo devān - miṃdriyaṃ vīryamayuvata tadyamasya yamatvaṃ te devā amanyaṃta yamo vā idamabhūdyadvayagsmai iti te prajāpatimupādhāvantsa et prajāpatirātmana ukṣavaśau niramimīta te devā vaiṣṇāvaruṇīṃ vaśāmālabhaṃtaiṃdra mukṣāṇaṃ taṃ varuṇenaiva grāhayitvā viṣṇunā yajñena prāṇudaṃtaiṃdreṇaivāsyeṃdriyamavṛṃjata yo bhrātṛvyavāntātsa spardhamāno vaiṣṇāvaruṇīṃ ‖) (Tai. Saṃ. 2-1-4-4)

Once, when a contest arose between the gods and Yama for lordship of this world, Yama brought all the gods' power under his own control; hence his name Yama. Then the gods, thinking much, went to Prajāpati and sought his help. He fashioned from his own body a cow and a bull. The gods offered that animal to Viṣṇu and Varuṇa in the form of a sacrifice (and the bull to Indra). Then Viṣṇu, who is the sacrifice, and Varuṇa bound Yama's course and drove him away. Therefore, when one is contending with rivals, an animal oblation must be offered to Viṣṇu and Varuṇa; the Taittirīya Saṃhitā says that the enemy is then checked.

Similarly, in another context the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa says that Viṣṇu and Varuṇa became entitled to a share of the sacrifice as protectors of different parts of the sacrifice:

ययोरोजसा स्कभिता रजांसीति वैष्णुवारुणीमृचं शंसति विष्णुर्वै यज्ञस्य दुरिष्टं पाति वरुणः स्विष्टं तयोरुभयोरेव शांतै । (yayorojasā skabhitā rajāṃsīti vaiṣṇuvāruṇīmṛcaṃ śaṃsati viṣṇurvai yajñasya duriṣṭaṃ pāti varuṇaḥ sviṣṭaṃ tayorubhayoreva śāṃtai |) (Ai. Brā. 3-38)

The Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra directs that the mantra "ययोरोजसा स्कभिता रजांसि (yayorojasā skabhitā rajāṃsi)", addressed to Viṣṇu and Varuṇa together, be recited at the Vaiśvadeva sacrifice. In the Āśvalāyana sūtra and in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa the mantra runs as follows:

p. 657

ययोरोजसा स्कभिता रजांसि वीर्येभिर्वीरतमा शविष्ठ या पत्येते अप्रतीत्ता सहोभिर्विष्णू अगन्वरुणा पूर्वहूत् ॥ (yayorojasā skabhitā rajāṃsi vīryebhirvīratamā śaviṣṭha yā patyete apratīttā sahobhirviṣṇū aganvaruṇā pūrvahūt ‖) (Tai. Brā. 2-8-4-5)

The meaning of this mantra is: "May the gods Viṣṇu and Varuṇa, by whose power the atmosphere was established, who are the most vigorous and the most brilliant, come together and first." This mantra is not in the Ṛk-saṃhitā; it is in the Tai. Brā. In the Atharva-saṃhitā alone (7-15-1) it is stated with a slight difference.

Because Viṣṇu repairs whatever faults at the time of sacrifice are causes of evil results, and because Varuṇa protects the fruit of the sacrifice gained through excellent performance of the rite, it is prescribed that the oblation be offered to these two deities together (Ā. Śau. 5-20).NOTE

The passage showing in this way the sacrificial relation of Viṣṇu and Varuṇa, Varuṇa's place alongside Viṣṇu, and the equal share of the sacrifice for the two deities is conveyed by the description राजा वरुणः सचंत (rājā varuṇaḥ sacaṃta).

p. 658

तं अश्विना (taṃ aśvinā)—तमेव क्रतुं यागमश्विन् सेवंते (tameva kratuṃ yāgamaśvin sevaṃte). This states the mutual relation of these deities at the time of the sacrifice: the Aśvin deities too attend that same Viṣṇu who is the sacrifice in essence. The Śatapatha and other Brāhmaṇas describe how, at the time of the sacrifice, the head of Viṣṇu, who is the sacrifice in essence, was cut off, how the Aśvin deities repaired it, and how for that reason they too became sharers in the sacrifice.

देवा ह वै सत्त्रं निषेदुः (devā ha vai sattraṃ niṣeduḥ) … प्रचिच्छिदतु (pracicchidatu) NOTE (Śa. Brā. 14-1-1 to 9)

Formerly, all the gods other than the Aśvins, Indra, Viṣṇu, Soma and the rest, together began a sattra at Kurukṣetra, the place of the gods' sacrifice. Then they wished to become renowned and possessed of food. They decided that whoever among them should first complete the sacrifice fully, through toil, faith and oblations, would be reckoned the foremost of all. Viṣṇu first obtained that excellent rank.

p. 659

Viṣṇu, who had attained so excellent a rank, became the sacrifice in essence. Then his pride in his own glory could not be restrained. When he set out taking his bow together with his three arrows, none of the gods dared to oppose him, and they sat stunned. Then ants of the kind called vamrī came and asked Viṣṇu what he would give in return if they gripped, pulled and bent the tip of that bow. He gave the assurance that one with such ability would enjoy full wealth of food and would obtain abundance of water even in a desert. Then they cut through the bowstring. At once the end of the bent bow sprang up straight and cut off the head of Viṣṇu, which was resting on the bent bow. This is the story in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa. In Tai. 4. 1-5-2 it is said that Indra himself, in the form of a vamrī, cut the bowstring.NOTE

The Taittirīya Āraṇyaka tells as follows how, when the head of Viṣṇu, who is the sacrifice in essence, was cut off, the gods knew that the sacrifice itself had become deficient, and while they were brooding the Aśvin deities repaired his severed head.

देवा वै सत्रमासत । युद्धिपरिमितं यशस्कामाः। तेऽब्रुवन्। यन्नः प्रथमं यशः ऋच्छात् । सर्वेषां न स्ततत्सहासदिति। .... .... .... .... । तेषां मखं वैष्णवं यश आर्भत् । ............तस्य सिष्मीयाणस्य तेजोऽपाक्रामत्.... .... .... वारेवृतग्स् हासां । तस्य ज्यामप्यादन् । तस्य धनुर्विप्रवमाणग् शिर उदवर्तयत् । तद्वावापृथिवी अनु प्रावर्तत । यत्पावर्तत । तत् प्रवर्ग्यस्य प्रवर्ग्यत्वं । यद्घ्रां ४ इत्यपतत् । तद्वर्मस्य घर्मत्वं । महतो वीर्यमपप्तदिति । तन्नहावीरस्य महावीरत्वं । यदस्याः समभरन्तत्सम्राजः संम्राट्त्वं । तग्स् स्ततं देवतास्त्रेधा व्यग्रह्णत । अग्निः पात्रः सवनं । इंद्रो माध्यंदिनग्स् सवनं । विश्वेदेवास्तृतीयसवनं । तेनापशीर्ष्णा यज्ञेन यजमानाः । नाशिषोऽनारुंधत । न सुवर्गं लोकभ्यजयन् । ते देवा अश्विनावब्रुवन् । भिषजौ वै स्थः । इदं यज्ञस्य शिरः प्रतिधत्तमिति । तावब्रूतां वरं वृणावहै । ग्रह एव नावत्रापि गृह्यतामिति । ताभ्यामेतमाश्विनमगृह्णन् । तावेतदद्यज्ञस्य शिरः प्रत्यधत्तां । यत्पवर्ग्यः । तेन सशीर्ष्णा यज्ञेन यजमानाः । अवाशिषोऽरुन्तत । .... .... .... अभि सुवर्गं लोकं जयति । तस्मादेष आश्विन प्रवया इव । यत्पवर्ग्यः ॥ (devā vai satramāsata | yuddhiparimitaṃ yaśaskāmāḥ| te 'bruvan| yannaḥ prathamaṃ yaśaḥ ṛcchāt | sarveṣāṃ na statatsahāsaditi| .... .... .... .... | teṣāṃ makhaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ yaśa ārbhat | ............tasya siṣmīyāṇasya tejo 'pākrāmat.... .... .... vārevṛtags hāsāṃ | tasya jyāmapyādan | tasya dhanurvipravamāṇag śira udavartayat | tadvāvāpṛthivī anu prāvartata | yatpāvartata | tat pravargyasya pravargyatvaṃ | yadghrāṃ 4 ityapatat | tadvarmasya gharmatvaṃ | mahato vīryamapaptaditi | tannahāvīrasya mahāvīratvaṃ | yadasyāḥ samabharantatsamrājaḥ saṃmrāṭtvaṃ | tags stataṃ devatāstredhā vyagrahṇata | agniḥ pātraḥ savanaṃ | iṃdro mādhyaṃdinags savanaṃ | viśvedevāstṛtīyasavanaṃ | tenāpaśīrṣṇā yajñena yajamānāḥ | nāśiṣo 'nāruṃdhata | na suvargaṃ lokabhyajayan | te devā aśvināvabruvan | bhiṣajau vai sthaḥ | idaṃ yajñasya śiraḥ pratidhattamiti | tāvabrūtāṃ varaṃ vṛṇāvahai | graha eva nāvatrāpi gṛhyatāmiti | tābhyāmetamāśvinamagṛhṇan | tāvetadadyajñasya śiraḥ pratyadhattāṃ | yatpavargyaḥ | tena saśīrṣṇā yajñena yajamānāḥ | avāśiṣo 'runtata | .... .... .... abhi suvargaṃ lokaṃ jayati | tasmādeṣa āśvina pravayā iva | yatpavargyaḥ ‖) (Tai. Ā. 5-1-1 to 7)

As in the story quoted above from the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, after the head of Viṣṇu, who is the sacrifice in essence, was cut off, they divided the fallen body of the sacrifice into three parts. Then Agni took the morning pressing, Indra the midday pressing, and the Viśvedevas the third pressing. But from a sacrifice that had no head, neither well-being nor heaven came to them.

p. 660

Then they addressed the Aśvin deities: "You are the physicians of the gods. Join again this severed head of the sacrifice." When they asked this, the Aśvins said: "If the Soma oblation may be ours here also, we will join the head to the body." When the gods agreed, they joined the severed head of Viṣṇu, who is the sacrifice in form, and became entitled to a share of the sacrifice. So it is said.

Thus, since in one respect the Aśvin deities are indeed protectors of the sacrifice, the words अश्विना क्रतुं सचंत (aśvinā kratuṃ sacaṃta) in the Ṛk state that the Aśvin deities attend, or attended, this sacrifice.

मारुतस्य वेधसः (mārutasya vedhasaḥ)—मरुतां ऋत्विजां संबंधिनः (marutāṃ ṛtvijāṃ saṃbaṃdhinaḥ) or मरुतां देवानां संबंधिनः यजमानस्य (marutāṃ devānāṃ saṃbaṃdhinaḥ yajamānasya): "of the sacrificer who is a kinsman of the priests, or a kinsman of the gods". Thus two kinds of meaning are given for the word मारुतस्य (mārutasya). The authors of the Nirukta have listed the word मरुत् (marut) among the names of the priest (3-19) and among the names of gold (2-10). But if the name known as that of the Marut deities is to be given the meaning "priest", "gold", and in some places (commonly) "gods", then it takes some effort to find what the root of this word is, in what ways its derivation is possible, and what its derivation is when it denotes the Marut deities. For this word as used of the Marut deities the Nirukta gives the following explanation:

मरुतो मितराविणो ना मितरोचिनो ना महद्भवंतीति वा । (maruto mitarāviṇo nā mitarocino nā mahadbhavaṃtīti vā |) (Ni. 11-14)

Citing Ṛk 1-8, it explains the nature of the Maruts: the name is given because they have measured sound, or measured radiance, or because they run swiftly.

Discussing how hard it is to give a correct explanation of this word, which has so many meanings, the scholar Max Muller says:

"Marut or Maruta in Orninary Sanskrit mean wind, and more particularly a strong wind, differing by its violent character from Vayu or Vata Nor do the hymns themselves leave us in any doubt as to the natural phenomena with which the Maruts are identified. Storms which root up the trees of the forest, lightning, thunder and showers of rain are the background from which the Maruts in their personal and dramatic character rise

p. 661

before our eyes. In most of the later native dictionaries (the Medinī, Viśva, Hemacandra, Amara, Anekārthadhvanimañjarī), Marut is given as a synonym of Deva, or God in general, and so is Maru in Pali. But, while the hymns addressed to the Maruts enable us to watch the successive stages in the development of so called deities more clearly than any other hymns, there is no doubt one drawback, namely, the uncertainty of the etymology of Marut .... .... .... .... .... No better etymology having been proposed, I still maintain that the derivation of Marut from మృ to pound, to smash, is free from any objection and that the original conception of the Maruts was that of crushing, smashing, striking, tearing, destroying storms ". ( The Vedic Hymns. Scererd Books of the East. Vol. XXXII.—P. XXIV ).

Having also stated the views of Western scholars such as Kuhn [these views will be discussed in detail in the sūkta addressed to the Maruts], and having finally pointed out the faults in them, he has given in the sentences above his own view: that the word marut is formed from the root mṛ, meaning "to injure", and denotes a special power that cuts down trees and the like. Since the priests also press out Soma and the like, it appears that the use of the word marut may apply to priests too. Since the Nirukta authors state मितरोचिनो वा (mitarocino vā) — "having measured splendour" — as the reason for the name, and since gods and gold have this quality, the name may have become well known on that account.

In the present Ṛk: मरुतां ऋत्विजां संघातो मारुतं तद्वतः (marutāṃ ṛtvijāṃ saṃghāto mārutaṃ tadvataḥ). The assembly of priests is "Māruta"; the meaning is either the sacrificer connected with them, or, मरुतां देवानां संबंधिनो वा (marutāṃ devānāṃ saṃbaṃdhino vā), the sacrificer connected with the gods. Since the priests obtain their place in the sacrificial act through the sacrificer's undertaking, he is connected with the priests; or, since the gods receive oblations and the like through the sacrificer's sacrificial act, he is the gods' own close kinsman. So either meaning may be given.

वेधसः—मेधाविनः अस्य यजमानस्य (vedhasaḥ—medhāvinaḥ asya yajamānasya): this word is read among the names of the wise (Ni. 3-19), and in this Ṛk it is used as a synonym of the sacrificer. [It was also stated in the previous Ṛk, 1-156-2, that it can mean "creator".]

Vrajaṃ: व्रजंत्यंतरिक्षे (vrajaṃtyaṃtarikṣe) — because it moves in the atmosphere, the cloud has this name (Ni. 6-2).

p. 662

Ahar-vidam: अहर्विदं—अहर्वेत्तारं (aharvidaṃ—aharvettāraṃ), स्वर्गोत्पादकमित्यर्थः (svargotpādakamityarthaḥ): that is, the producer of heaven. "Dakṣa" means that he also bore power; thus Viṣṇu's greatness is praised.

Besides the meaning stated above, Sāyaṇa has explained this Ṛk in another way too. Having stated that vedhasaḥ can mean not only the performer of the sacrifice but also Viṣṇu the ordainer, he says: मारुतस्य मरुत्संघातस्य देवगणस्य वेधसो विधातुः स्रष्टुर्विष्णो क्रतुं कर्म पालनादिरूपं वरुणादयः सचंते । तदधीनत्वात्पालनस्य । सच सखिवान् इंद्रमरुदादिसहायोपेतः सन् दक्षं वृष्टुत्पादनादिसामर्थ्यरूपं बलं दाधार । (mārutasya marutsaṃghātasya devagaṇasya vedhaso vidhātuḥ sraṣṭurviṣṇo kratuṃ karma pālanādirūpaṃ varuṇādayaḥ sacaṃte | tadadhīnatvātpālanasya | saca sakhivān iṃdramarudādisahāyopetaḥ san dakṣaṃ vṛṣṭutpādanādisāmarthyarūpaṃ balaṃ dādhāra |). That is: Varuṇa and the others serve the world-protecting and similar act of Viṣṇu, who is the creator and is connected with the host of gods; and Viṣṇu, joined with the help of Indra, the Maruts and the other gods, obtained power, that is, ability for tasks such as the production of rain. In this way he explained the meaning of the Ṛk a second time.

Grammar
  • राजा — राज्य दीप्तौ धातुः । कनिन्‌युवृषि (उ. सू. १-१५४) इति कसिस् प्रत्ययः । नित्त्वाद् आद्युदात्तस्वरः भवति ।
  • अश्विना — सुपां सुलुक् (पा. सू. ७-१-३९) इति विभक्तेः (औ) आकारादेशः भवति ।
  • सचंत — षच समवाये धातुः । धात्वादेःषःसः इति आदेः सत्वम् । छंदसि वर्तमानार्थे लज् । प्रथमपुरुषबहुवचने झप्रत्ययस्य अंतादेशः । बहुलं छंदस्यमाज्‌योगेऽपि इति अडागमः न भवति । तिजंतनिघातस्वरः भवति ।
  • मारुतस्य — मरुतां समूहः मारुतम् । अत् प्रत्ययः । आदिवृद्धिः । तदस्य आस्ति इति अर्थविवक्षायां मतुप् आगते भांदसत्वेन तस्य लुक् ।
  • दाधार — डुधाञ् धारणपोषणयोः धातुः । लिट् प्रथमपुरुष एकवचनांतरूपम् । पादादौ स्थितत्वात् निघातस्वरः न भवति । णल् लित्त्वात् प्रत्ययस्य पूर्वस्य उदात्तस्वरः भवति ।
  • अहर्विदम् — विद ज्ञाने धातुः । क्विप् च इति क्विप् प्रत्ययः । गतिकारकोपपदात्‌कृत् इति कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरः भवति । द्वितीयाविकवचनांतरूपम् ।

p. 663

  • सखिवान् — सखा अस्य अस्ति इति सखिवान् । छंदसीवनिपौ इति मत्त्वर्थे वनिप् प्रत्ययः । पित्त्वाद् अनुदात्तः भवति । उप इति अच् परत्वात् दीर्घादटि समानपादे (पा. सु. ८-३-९) इति नकारस्य रुत्वम् । आतोटि नित्यम् (पा. सू. ८-३-३) इति पूर्वस्य आकारस्य संहितायां नित्यम् अनुनासिकत्वम् । NOTE
  • अप ऊर्णुते — ऊर्णुञ् आच्छादने धातुः । अदादिः । लट् प्रथमपुरुष एकवचनांतरूपम् । च इति संबंधत्वात् निघातस्वरः न भवति । प्रत्ययस्वरेण अंतोदात्तः भवति । तिजिचोदात्तवति (पा सू. ८-१-७१) इति गतेः (अप) निघातस्वरः भवति ।

Ṛk 5

॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)
